x: Home / Aempaera / The Holy Princes The Holy Princes The Ashraatraal: seven sacred generals, the oldest Vatrajarə in existence. There were nine once. This section follows the Aempaera and Ishphaeno reference documents. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Names are given in Vatrahu unless a Vatraxu form is named. Each Holy Prince commands a regiment of Paev and Laer Vatrajarə. They are AshraaPaev, generals with three pairs of wings, and their back pair, a sign of Jangshe’s and Ashraaha’s favour, is the largest of any Vatrajarə below the rank of Theraapaev. In Vatraxu they are Zashraatraal. Their title Ashraatraal means holy princes, and their council is the Ashraakaenru (Zashraakaenru in Vatraxu). Mikael, who leads them, also holds the title Uthaartraal, the leader-prince. Their motto is Taal vatra lan , “We trust in him.” See Vatrahu and Vatraxu . The seven Prince Domains Human height True form Pattern of markings Aura on Earth Mikael Justice, Humility, Faith, Charity 6'3" to 6'5" 7'5" to 8' Stepped frets, angular and bilateral Not recorded Kaprijael Faith, Kindness, Diligence 6'1" 7'5" to 8' Lines radiating from the wrists Not recorded Ravael Temperance, Healing, Guidance, Humility 5'11" to 6'0" 7'5" to 8' Lines radiating from the breastbone like a heartbeat Nearby tissue heals faster Uthrijael Wisdom, Retribution, Chastity 6'0" 7'5" to 8' Concentric spirals at the temples Shadows withdraw Kamael Fortitude, Love, Charity 5'10" 7'5" to 8' Chevrons, gathered on the chest A sense of being seen and cared for, which unsettles those unused to it Thovijael Patience, Beauty, Hope, Wisdom 5'8" 7'5" to 8' The most ornate and fine-lined Colours look more vivid Thakjael Loyalty, Righteousness 6'1" 7'5" to 8' Clean parallel lines Not recorded The Ashraatraal’s markings are the most complex of any Vatrajarə and the hardest to hide. Their hair moves in true form with particular intention, answering will as well as feeling. A Holy Prince of Aempaera. Concept image. Mikael Mikael leads the Ashraatraal as Uthaartraal and is the only living Theraapaev, with four pairs of wings: feet, wrists, back and eyes. He alone can command the Theraav chorus. He wears only white and black in human form, and his disguise is always slightly insufficient by choice. The two who fell The council was nine until the Krang Uthjook. Thamael , the Ashraatipaev and the highest of the Holy Princes, and Haelael , a Theraapaev, led the opposition and lost. They fell and took new names: Thamael became Sadok , and Haelael became Lioshe . See Krang Uthjook and TeSharani . Before the Fall After the Fall Thamael, now Sadok Ashraatipaev, the only one ever. Five pairs of wings: feet, wrists, back, eyes and temples. See the war page. Haelael, now Lioshe Theraapaev, with four pairs of wings, and the identical twin of Mikael. Same face, same body, same divine pattern. Silvery blond in true form, as the gold of his origin cooled through the Fall. Two tails and blackened wings. In human form the twins are told apart by style and energy alone. Mikael wears white and black. Lioshe wears colour, texture, earth tones and silver chains. Both suppress only as much as they need to pass. The same pattern, one expressing Justice and the other Free Will. Decided How mortals remember them Human scholars who read the Ashraama faith as Abrama meet the Ashraatraal as the seven princes of heaven. Some traditions keep a memory of the two who fell and count eight or nine. x: Home / Aempaera / The Vatrajarə The Vatrajarə A Vatrajarə in true form. Concept image. Created by Jangshe and Ashraaha, fitted to a realm of heavy light and floating stone. This section follows the Aempaera and Ishphaeno reference documents. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Names are given in Vatrahu unless a Vatraxu form is named. At a glance Name Vatrajarə in Vatrahu, Vatrajaro in Vatraxu. Sometimes written Vertroue in older documents. Size A Vatrajarə born in Aempaera stands about 7 feet in true form. Those who were once human, and now carry human proportions, stand 5 feet 8 inches or more. Size shows origin, not power. All are much larger in true form than in human disguise. Skin The full range of dark skin tones inherited from Ashraaha. Albino and pale expressions exist and are rarer. Eyes White sclera with gold irises, from Jangshe. In disguise the gold dulls to warm brown or hazel. Hair Springy coils and loose curls, in natural patterns. In Aempaera or at full power the hair moves by intention, not gravity. Needs No sleep, food or breath. They practise a chosen stillness, which refills aethaari and can be broken at will. Gold markings Gold geometric lines show on the skin like circuitry. They are plain in Aempaera’s light and when power is released in full, and they go dormant in human disguise. Under strong feeling they surface unbidden, first at the temples, breastbone and forearms. The design draws on two traditions, reinterpreted: Maya geometric patterns that are not writing, and the Inuit kakiniit tradition of accumulating lines. As in kakiniit, markings begin sparse and grow outward as rank and power grow. Each domain shapes the pattern. Rank Where markings start Where they grow Laer, new Breastbone only, one or two lines Outward to the ribs Laer, established Breastbone and forearms Up toward the shoulders Paev Breastbone, forearms, upper arms, temples starting Toward the face and back Theraav Breastbone, arms, temples, collarbones, upper back Toward the face and shoulder blades Ashraat Full chest, arms, temples, face starting Toward the jaw and spine AshraaPaev Breastbone, arms, temples, collarbones, upper back, in a pattern of their own domain Across chest and shoulder blades Theraapaev Full chest, arms, temples, face, in stepped angular frets Toward the jaw and spine Ashraatipaev The whole body The fullest expression possible. Ancient lines never fully hide Wings and rank Every Vatrajarə has ivory wings with a lit quality, because the feathers are hollow and filled with aethaari. Wings furl for everyday movement and open fully when power is released. The number and placement of pairs shows rank. Size grows with age and accumulated power, not with rank. Rank Pairs Where Notes Laer 1 Feet and ankles The lowest rank. It includes souls remade from mortals. Paev 2 Feet and wrists The wrist wings give combat-level directional control. Theraav 3 Feet, back, eyes No wrist wings. They report only to Jangshe, Ashraaha and Mikael. Ashraat 4 Feet, back, eyes, temples No wrist wings. The prime guardian force of Aempaera. AshraaPaev 3 Feet, wrists, back The six regular Holy Princes. Wrist wings mark a general. Theraapaev 4 Feet, wrists, back, eyes Theraav rank with wrist wings, held by Mikael and, before the Fall, Lioshe. Ashraatipaev 5 Feet, wrists, back, eyes, temples Ashraat rank with wrist wings. Held before the Fall by Sadok alone. The suffix -paev marks a general above regular Paev rank. It joins a general’s duties to whatever rank the person already holds. It is not a separate tier. Back wings are the largest and carry flight and power. Wrist wings are medium and the most emotional, flaring before any other pair moves. Ankle wings are small and steer precisely. Eye wings are small, delicate and largely involuntary. Temple wings are like the eye wings and angle upward and back. Ancient beings, such as the Holy Princes, have back wings far wider than their arm span. Power Name What it is Ashraavatra, True Voice It projects Aempaera’s own frequency into the mortal world without the slow adjustment of the Praise Fields. For mortals this is a physics mismatch that hurts. The Holy Princes’ voice also carries a pull on the conscience: everyone in range feels their own guilt surface, with no one singled out. The name is the same in Vatrahu and Vatraxu. Aethjarə, aura The environment of Aempaera leaking from the body at all times. It falls with power use and with distance from Aempaera. In disguise it mutes to a warmth that mortals read as charisma. Kraethjarə, aura flare The aura pushed outward at full strength as a weapon. It is especially devastating to the fallen and their children, who are sensitive to aethaari because they fell from it. The Sekh resist it fairly well when prepared. For them it is uncomfortable closeness to something very bright. Aethmaalithi, hard light Condensing aethaari into blades, arrows, barriers and projectiles by will and skill. An ordinary Vatrajarə carries a forged handle or bow frame and makes the rest from light. The higher the rank, the less they carry. The Holy Princes at full power may anchor to nothing. Making ammunition from their own reserves is a heavy drain. Aethmaale Holy forged material made from aethaari and inscribed with working runes. See the weapons that hurt Lamiae and Anu. Human disguise A Vatrajarə in human disguise. Concept image. Any Vatrajarə can hide what they are. Gold irises dull, markings sleep, wings and rank marks are hidden, and the aura softens. A higher rank takes more effort to hold. Under stress, the eyes slip first, as the gold bleeds back, and then the hair, which briefly moves against gravity. Hybrids: the Vo’im and the Kaemeng The Vo’im are children of a Vatrajarə and a human. Their strength scales with the strength of the Vatrajarə parent, so a Vo’im finds a place in the ranks of Aempaera by that parent’s standing as well as in the hierarchy of Ishphaeno . Decided The Kaemeng are children of a Vatrajarə, or of one of the fallen, and a Sekh. They are slightly weaker than the Ashraatraal, the Holy Princes, but have the potential to stand next to Mikael in power. Tales in Aempaera say only one has ever lived. Decided Open questions How rank advancement works beyond meditative practice Open Where exactly a Vo’im of a given parent sits in the chorus ranks Open

x: Home / Aempaera / Krang Uthjook and TeSharani Krang Uthjook and TeSharani The great war, and the Fall that ended it. Everything infernal begins here. This section follows the Aempaera and Ishphaeno reference documents. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Names are given in Vatrahu unless a Vatraxu form is named. The names Event Vatrahu Vatraxu Notes The great war Krang Uthjook Krang Zuthjuk Older documents call it the Krag War. Uthjook is “war” in Vatrahu and Zuthjuk is the Vatraxu word. Decided The Fall Oshnalani TeSharani The O- and Te- are each language’s definite article. The old spelling Oshalani is retired. The Great Mourning TeXathrameni The Vatraxu view of the same event. Decided What happened The Holy Princes’ council once had nine members. Two of them, Thamael, the highest ranking, and Haelael, led the opposition to Jangshe’s order in the Krang Uthjook. They lost. The defeat was the Fall: the losing side was cast out of Aempaera and changed, and everything that Ishphaeno is began there. The two took new names, Sadok and Lioshe. Seven Holy Princes remained. Other peoples were drawn in. Children of Vatrajarə and humans, the Vo’im, already existed, and Aempaera had turned some of them away. That refusal is part of what drove their family toward the war. Many of the fallen’s later children never saw Aempaera at all. The first Lamiae, the first generation, nearly all died in the war, and the Shavari twins fought in it with honour. See The Lamiae and The four broods . How long the war lasted, and when it happened, is not set down in the current references. Open What the Fall did to the body The Fall turned wings into other things, and the fate of each pair depended on which pair it was. Those who had no wrist wings do not grow antlers from that pair, though a few grew antlers anyway. Wings What they became Feet and ankles Tails. Each pair becomes one or more tails. Wrists Antlers of living bone. Only those who had wrist wings. Back Blackened. The stronger keep them even if they cannot fly well, and the weaker lose them entirely. Eyes A second pair of eyes. Temples A third pair of eyes, or a second pair of antlers or horns, or lost. Antlers and horns Antlers are living bone with a blood supply, and they grow in velvet before they harden. They come from wrist wings changed in the Fall: corrupted celestial life, still alive and growing. During the velvet phase, the most powerful beings of the infernal side are briefly vulnerable. Horns are fixed keratin over a bone core and have no blood supply. They come from the ankle wings of those born into Toluqavadoth after the Fall. Colour matches the bearer’s own demon skin, with white bone showing beneath, in natural tones only. Sadok and Lioshe Sadok Lioshe Rank before Ashraatipaev Theraapaev Back wings Blackened and kept Blackened Wrist wings Became Alaskan moose antlers, the widest spread of any being, near black Not recorded Eye wings A second pair of eyes Not recorded Temple wings A third pair of eyes Not recorded Ankle wings Three prehensile forked tails, each with three talon-like fingers that move independently. The fur matches the black of the wings Two tails. One is thinner and whiplike, forked with three gripping fingers. The other is simply forked A new voice The fallen carry Jaħuvatra in Vatrahu, Jaxuvatra in Vatraxu, the mirror of the Holy Princes’ True Voice. It is a voice that compels through broken trust, not holy presence. Where Ashraavatra surfaces guilt, Jaħuvatra amplifies desire, despair or compulsion, depending on the wielder’s purpose and the listener’s weakness. The name means “broken voice,” from jaħu, fragmented, and vatra, voice or trust. What followed The fallen made Ishphaeno from Toluqavadoth’s body, and Sadok built its capital, Xathqaelsel. Sadok himself is imprisoned in Ashraaħəmavel, the punishment facility inside the crystal desert of TeDrona, beyond the heat zone of Pharuhona. The imprisonment was secured by a deal between both primordials. The Holy Princes’ regiments guard it in rotation. One standard rotation is 60 Earth years, a full human lifetime on purpose. An Ishphaeno year is 2.1 to 2.7 Earth years, so that is about 22 to 28 Ishphaeno years, or about 360 Aempaera years. Uthrijael and Kaprijael alternate on the longest turns. See Places and the soil map for TeDrona and the gates, and the sky map for the sky over Xathqaelsel. x: Home / Aempaera Aempaera The heavenly realm: bright, never silent, and built inside the body of its creator. This section follows the Aempaera and Ishphaeno reference documents. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Names are given in Vatrahu unless a Vatraxu form is named. At a glance Names Aempaera in Vatrahu and Zaempaera in Vatraxu. Decided What it is The celestial dominion within Jangshe. It is the home of the Vatrajarə and the seat of the Ashraama faith, which human scholars know as Abrama. Rulers Jangshe and Ashraaha. Jangshe is a primordial. Ashraaha was created by Jangshe and is not one. People The Vatrajarə. They are its soldiers, messengers and citizens, and they speak Vatrahu. Light Torusheva, a luminous orb that never sets. Time Time runs faster here than on Earth. One Earth hour is six Aempaera hours. Seen from Earth The stars of Aempaera are the same stars, seen from another angle. Two primordials Primordial Nature Realm inside it Jangshe Order. Generally formless. Jangshe makes a humanoid avatar when it wants to talk with its creations. Order is not the same as kindness. Aempaera Toluqavadoth Chaos. Generally formless, and it contains every possibility. Each realm of the infernal side sits in its body. Ishphaeno Ashraaha is the mother of the Vatrajarə. She is a nurturer and co-creator with queen-level standing in Aempaera, and she stays in Aethmaeri. Early documents and mortal scholars often call her a primordial, which is wrong. Three zones Zone What it is The Praise Fields (outer) Where the souls of mortal worshippers are ferried at death. To them it is luminous, warm and vibrant. They sing. The Purification Passages (middle) Where souls in transit are remade as Laer, the lowest rank of the Vatrajarə. The Vatrajarə Quarters (inner) Homes, institutions, training grounds and governing chambers. Aethmaeri is here, where Jangshe holds court and where Aethmaale, the holy weapon material, is forged. Floating platforms called Ashraethal carry the buildings, joined by roads of condensed aethaari that only a Vatrajarə can cross. Aempaera is vast, stark and open to the air, in white stone with gold inlay. Jangshe’s court is the most architectural place. At the outer edges the buildings dissolve into boundlessness. A mortal who enters without preparation is overwhelmed by the senses within moments, and getting about without Vatrajarə power is possible but very dangerous. The praise of the outer fields is a constant low harmony that grows more complex toward Aethmaeri. Colours are stronger than mortal eyes can hold: whiter than sunlight, golds that are warm and not harsh, deep greens. A glowing cloud fills the space between buildings. Light and the seasons Torusheva never moves across the sky. It slowly bleaches from full brightness to a dim moonlight, then brightens again. At the dim end the stars blaze. Phase Orb Stars Full brightness Peak Not visible Gradual dimming Bleaching slowly Partly visible Moonlight Dim Blazing Gradual brightening Returning Fading There are two seasons, tied to Jangshe’s own energy and not to weather. Romatoru , the alive season, is Jangshe at full capacity: the orb stays bright, aethaari refills faster, markings show more and wings glow. Hevatoru , the rest season, is Jangshe at slower capacity: the orb dims often, the stars show longer and aethaari refills more slowly. It is the natural time for meditative stillness. Telling time The orb does not move, so shadows always point the same way. Their length changes with the orb’s brightness, and the Shorumael , a post ringed with length-interval marks, reads it. A brighter orb gives a shorter shadow. Wind gives the finer reading: light, frequent gusts mean morning, strong long gusts afternoon, and gentler medium gusts evening. A blind or sensory-impaired Vatrajarə can tell the time by wind alone. Time against the other realms Comparison Rate 1 Ishphaeno hour 6 Earth hours 1 Earth hour 6 Aempaera hours 1 Ishphaeno hour 36 Aempaera hours 1 Ishphaeno day 8 periods, which is 2 Earth days 1 Ishphaeno week 8 Ishphaeno days, which is 16 Earth days Earth is the neutral baseline. Ishphaeno runs slower than Earth and Aempaera runs faster. Aethaari Aethaari is the sacred flame of the Vatrajarə, and it is cultivated, not ambient. Singing with others refills it fastest. Meditative stillness refills it slowly, and it is one of the few reliable paths to higher rank. Using power spends it. A Vatrajarə on Earth spends it faster and recovers slower. For the Holy Princes, whose auras and True Voices cost the most, that is a daily concern. Read next Jangshe The primordial of Order, within whom Aempaera lies. Toluqavadoth The primordial of Chaos, within whom Ishphaeno lies. The Vatrajarə Their bodies, wings, markings, voice and ranks. The Holy Princes The seven Ashraatraal, and the two who fell. Krang Uthjook and TeSharani The great war, the Fall, and what the Fall did to wings. x: Home / Earth / The Anu / Packs, orders and places Packs, orders and places There is no Anu government. There are packs, treaties between them, and a few institutions that reach outward to humans. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Anu Canon Reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. Pack life Sovereignty. A pack’s rule over itself is near absolute. No global Anu authority exists. Matters between packs go to treaty, sometimes with neutral elder mediators, and outside institutions must deal with one pack at a time. Gender. The society is strongly male-dominant. Female warriors are respected, but abstract leadership has long excluded women, and the first female Gammas and Betas are recent. Female Alphas are extremely rare, and a pack with one is fiercely protective of her. An Alpha without a mate and pups is customarily challenged. Inbreeding is warned against. Layout. Younger Anu bunk together and elders have private dens. Rank shows in closeness to the Alpha, or is casual, depending on the pack. Speech and signals Moment Words Before battle Leader: “Bound.” Pack: “To the hunt.” Greeting “We hunt together.” Mating “We run as one.” Funeral “Run the Shadow Path,” then a collective howl. Return “Pack endures.” “Pack always endures.” Gestures. A shoulder clasp for loyalty and readiness, a brow press for private reassurance, a neck nuzzle for pack affection, and a silent circle before a hunt or battle. Howls. Short means greeting or return. Long means alert, distress or mourning. A rising tone is victory and a falling tone is loss. A double howl alerts nearby Anu. Dreamleaf Daigimí is a silvery vine that grows where the Dream touches the world. It is burned at funerals and at rites of alignment to reach the ancestors. A large dose can trap a person in their thread. Institutions Name What it is Order of Shadows ( Shùkízòròmùna , “Followers of the Wolf Spirit”) The human-aligned order of morticians, doctors, caretakers, loremasters and watchdogs. Its devout monastic branch is the ShadowKeepers. In Emsehurst it runs as a legal nonprofit with community and wilderness programmes, real estate, education grants and private security work for Anu-tied families. Its cabins near Grey’s Lake serve as medical outposts, shelters and liaison points. Members wear canid masks at important rites. Human devotees of ’Anpésùmün as a faith group, the Shùkí’Apésùmù or Shùkapémù, are the Anu-side parallel to the Zingans, and the Order is their organised order. An English name for the group has not been chosen. Placeholder Wild Heart Field School ( Zhadín’kání Naibázonáyá ) A Nẹránamün faith school, independent of the Mephis Consortium and comparable to Quranic schools or Hasidic yeshivas. It is respected internationally, mainly within the faith. The main campus is a highland glen in Scotland, founded in 1790. A Cameroon rainforest annex, founded in 1878, is more combat-focused, with Fang-trial courses and Lamiae-watch stations. Yirimbo Academy ( Yírímbo Zonémi ) A private Nẹránamün-aligned school in Emsehurst for gifted human youth and Anu who have not yet awakened. It runs the whole Nok school ladder, from the first primary years to secondary, so pupils range from small children to about 18 or 19. Anu pupils leave at their first shift, which is usually at 19 but can come sooner. Proposed Daimushaifimí Military Institute Public name Dreamguard Military Institute. It stands in the Cimmerian Range north of Emsehurst and was founded in 1912. It is not an Anu institution but has close recruitment ties, and its path opens after the Rite of the Dreamthread. Spirit Council, Elders, Healers Zhạmáná Gùkífẹn’nakhèt , ’Aníkhètímùna , ’Anùmau . The Spirit Council advises. Each pack’s own council governs it. Wolf Valley The Rayan Pack holds the foothills of the Merveilles Mountains northeast of Emsehurst, north of Grey’s Lake. Human campers use the south shore, and rangers say to stay on the trail. Locals call the place Wolf Valley. Concealment. Heavy canopy and mist, moss-and-grass roofs, earth-sheltered dens, low heat signatures, false trails, Dreamward runes and illusion magic. The land is legally a private hunting reserve held by a trust, and local disappearance legends do the rest. Sites. A great den with a council fire and an ancestral altar, overlooking a hidden spring-fed lake called Wolf’s Mirror. A Sacred Spring for initiations, Miyema, prophecy dreams and thread burial. The Forge of ’Ògùsémün in a heated cave. A healer’s hut, an elder council hall and a communal fire pit. A training glade, an Ancestral Trail lit during the düfari rite, and a Dream-Grove for private prayer and grief. A non-interference arrangement with the Sekh covers the area, with shared vigilance on the border. Other peoples People Relationship The Sekh Allies under the same pantheon. The Anu call them “Thread-runners.” The Anu hold the thread tightly as guardians of the dead, and the Sekh walk it boldly as hunters of imbalance. Sekh blood is a hazard to Anu. The Lamiae Hunted when rabid. Their blood is dangerous to ingest. The Witches of Mephis Opposed over souls that are trapped and tricked. Humans The Order of Shadows is the human-aligned face. Exposure management runs through packs and the Order. Pandora’s Pact The Anu are allies of the Pact, not signatories. See Pandora’s Pact . x: Home / Earth / The Anu / Rank, rites and bonds Rank, rites and bonds Five places in a pack, one mark that cannot be faked, and a bond made with a bite at the base of the neck. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Anu Canon Reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. Three blood markers, five positions Three markers are inherited: Alpha, Beta and Omega. Five positions exist in a pack: Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Luna and Omega. Gamma and Luna are positions, not bloodlines, and are open to any blood, though usually of Alpha blood. Position Nok Role Alpha ’Áfá Pack leader. Beta Bimá Second in command. Gamma Gaimá Enforcement and warrior chief. Luna ’Aifá The spiritual heart of the pack. Often Miyema-bonded to the Alpha, but not required. Omega Ómá The base of the hierarchy. The original Anu blessed by the deities were all Alpha. Later human recruits became Beta, and Omegas descend from Beta lines with humans. An Omega-blooded Anu who rises to the Alpha position is so rare that it reshapes a pack’s history. What blood a pup inherits Odds for a child of each pairing. Gamma is a position, not a blood, so the old Gamma lines are folded into Beta. Proposed Parents Alpha Beta Omega Note Alpha and Alpha 95% 5% 0% Beta only if any non-Alpha lineage. Alpha and Beta 60 to 70% 29 to 38% 1 to 2% 70% Alpha if the Alpha parent has a strong lineage, 60% if average. Beta and Beta 0% 98% 2% Alpha or Beta and Omega 5% 35% 60% Alpha only if the Alpha parent is Alpha-blooded or has Alpha ancestry. Omega and Omega 1% 4% 95% All odds shift with the prevalence of each blood in the pair’s ancestry. They are a tool for the stories, not a law of nature. The Rite of the Dreamthread Nok ’ämbózisóróka , “Welcome of the Wolf.” It is a one-week solo wilderness survival and hunt held at a full moon, guided by the land and the youth’s spirit form, as a partner and not a tool. It is traditionally held before or during Tịkhètùbẹsé , the Great Shifting, a week-long holiday of heightened spirit connection. The youth is meant to meet their animal spirit and show it on return. Some packs name an initiate for a deed or for the spirit. Initiation Day is Rï’zháma . On return the pack welcomes the initiate at a fire, chanting the children’s motto. The düfari Three upright paw glyphs joined by a horizontal line, the Dream Thread. It appears by magic, often at night, in black. An elder’s mark may fade to silver or umber. The mark is identical for every Anu, is not a tattoo and cannot be faked. Decided Never on the neck, which is sacred to Miyema. Common places: upper back, over the heart, forearm (warriors), shoulder blade, sternum or ribs (ritualists). It tingles near other Anu, near Dreamgates and during high rituals. It gives no combat bonus, but spirits, dreamwalkers and some Sekh recognise it. Woven or stitched cloth versions may be worn at ceremonies. Newborn alignment A baby is placed on the Daimukómbusubí mat under Dreamleaf ( Daigimí ) smoke to find alignment: Shùnẹ , the Feather, or N’zaikís , the Fang. The Anu prefer the Zídifézí mat, a double-threaded braid. Adults who never received an alignment undergo Kihódání’obuwásóka . Birth month fixes the Dream-Tethered Sign. Alignment can shift with trauma or awakening. Mates: Miyema Thómítámün sees what each being needs and marks them so they may come together, or not. Háshùmün blesses and warms the bond. Pairing is always optional. Decided The marking. Mates bite the base of the neck where it meets the collarbone, open their minds and promise themselves. The magic forms an upward crescent moon with a star and a dot above it, miyema bonyi , “together bond.” The vow is “We run as one.” The effects. Deeper telepathy and shared emotion up to 50 miles. Sensation can be shared. Mates feel each other’s danger at any distance. A cross-species mate can receive the bond if love develops naturally. Thómítámün uses any and all pronouns. Decided When a bond breaks Cause What follows Death The mark turns silver and fades. Betrayal or rejection Shared anguish. The mark bruises over months. The Severance Rite The thread is cut at the fire or the sacred spring, and the bond breaks. One mate’s corruption The mind-link goes silent. The other mate feels it as a death-like absence. The thread tradition Every adult wears a thread in the hair, around the neck, or at the wrist or ankle. A loose thread means unmated. A shared or woven thread means bonded. A frayed or snapped thread means death, betrayal or mourning. The Nok name, Dúmùkwò , may still change. The wider tradition is on the thread tradition page. Moment Phrase Courting, braiding in a piece of the other’s thread “I carry your thread beside mine.” Mate bond exchange “Your hunt is my hunt. Your thread is my thread.” Mourning, a broken thread tied to the wrist “Your thread runs in the Dream. I follow the trail behind you.” Burying the thread at the spring “I release your thread to the Hunt.” Brotherhood or deep loyalty “Two threads. One hunt.” Severance, in public at the fire “Your thread is cut. Your name falls into silence.” A private break “Your thread frays. I walk without you.” A severed thread is shameful for the one cut off, not for the one who cuts. Severance may be kept in clan memory songs as a warning. Moral teaching The Anu hold the thread tightly. Five layers of law run from two foundations to thirty threads, taught in phases from toddlerhood to age fifteen. The full text of each layer, in the Anu edition, is on the moral framework page. Each day, morning and night, the devout recite five threads. Five a day over a six-day Nok week covers all thirty. To pass initiation, the youth recites all thirty in order, explains twenty chosen at random, lives a test week judged by elder watchers, and passes a soul-mirror trial before a ’Anpésùmün priest. Repeated unrepented breaks weaken, decay or turn the spirit. An Anu who dies with too many unrepented breaks has no Shadow Walker path. The spirit wanders and festers. How the initiation challenge relates to the Rite of the Dreamthread Open

x: Home / Earth / The Anu The Anu An Anu in human form. Concept image. Guardians of the border between life and death. They are born to it, they run as packs, and they take the shape of wild canines. “Words fade. The hunt endures.” Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Anu Canon Reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. At a glance Nok name Ánukhèt. Devotional names: Anpésùmù, Anpésùmùna, Anpésùmùkhèt. Patrons ’Anpésùmün, the Opener of Ways, and Bùnumün, the Great Canina Spirit. Calling Guide souls to ’Ätáru, help restless souls find peace, stop grave-robbers, and hunt reckless or rabid Sekh and Lamiae. Language Nok, the tongue of Thàmün’kẹbùkhẹt, the Motherland. Descent is Nok. Lifespan About 150 to 200 years barring death in battle. Motto of the young “We were once human, but we rose to meet the Dream.” Origin In the early Dream, certain humans watched the borders: gravekeepers, hunters, midwives of the dying and mourners. ’Anpésùmün chose them and gave them sight beyond life. Bùnumün lent them the strength and forms of the wild canines. They were bound to the Dream Thread and marked with the düfari. The original rite is lost. Canon The name of the original rite. The working title is “The Binding of Pack and Thread,” with no Nok form yet Open Born, not made. One is Anu by blood. A child of an Anu and a human keeps full Anu capability, and anyone with Anu blood can become active under the right conditions. A legend says a mortal can still be called by the old rite. It stays a legend. The Anu share the Sekh’s pantheon and differ in their ceremonies. See Nẹránamün and the moral framework , where the Anu edition of the 30 Threads is given. Life cycle Stage What happens Gestation Six months, nine at the latest. Newborns look human. Pups Called sórómètù and raised in packs. They have no night vision or notable abilities until initiation. Puberty brings strength spurts, hunger pangs and bone aches. Initiation Nineteen is the standard age. Packs and hard events can move it. Some packs hold a solo rite before twelve, and some Anu receive their animal in their teens. Adulthood From initiation, ageing slows. Physical age falls about three to five years behind actual age through the early decades, and the gap widens with time. See the table below. Death The animal spirit enters the Great Flow and is reborn in a new Anu. Stronger spirits may keep memories. The human soul continues as a Shadow Walker, a spirit wolf that hunts and investigates from beyond the Veil. How an Anu ages Until initiation an Anu grows like any child. After it, ageing slows in three stages: about one physical year for every 1.2 years lived up to physical 45, one for every 2.2 years up to about actual age 100, and one for every 3.75 years after that. Proposed Actual age Looks about 19 19 30 28 40 36 50 45 75 56 100 68 125 74 150 81 175 88 200 94 The curve is built from your own anchors: a lifespan of 150 to 200 years, a gap of three to five years in adulthood, and a gap that widens with age. Profile ages from the 2025 baseline need recomputing against it. Shape and body Shifting. Any canine except the domestic dog. Each Anu has one form per species, larger and stronger than the usual animal. There is no pain after the first shift, and clothes are preserved. Senses. Enhanced speed, strength, durability and vision, especially at night. Smell is strongest: they can smell lies through pheromones, and they know a person by their scent. Healing. Minor to medium injuries close in minutes to an hour. Major injuries need life support or surgery. Eyes. Any natural colour, with round human-like pupils and a blue eyeshine in sharp light. There is no oval-pupil tell, unlike the Sekh. A corrupted Anu has black eyes when shifted. Decided Voice. Howls and whines work even in human form. Spirit howls are heard only by kin, spirits and dogs. Pack mind. A telepathic link that opens and closes at will within about 25 miles. Howls carry about 50 miles. Mates link thoughts and emotions up to 50 miles and feel each other’s danger at any distance. The elder tier Elders can compel a restless spirit to speak, or escort one across the Veil. The cost is left open on purpose. Alphas and Lunas can extend the pack link’s reach and send calm through it, but they cannot lend strength. Placeholder Weaknesses Corruption. An Anu who turns from the light (subterfuge, blood magic, praising other gods, needless killing) sees their spirit corrupt. They gain strength and lose mind, and they are banished. A corrupted Anu caught by another Anu is burned and offered to ’Ògùsémün. Decided Some believe corruption can pass by a bite or a ritual meal. Part of this is superstition, and it drives real choices, including amputation to stop it. Lamia blood. A large amount triggers a berserker state lasting twelve hours to three days. It is hard to control and stains the soul with repeated use. Recovery sleep runs about one day per twelve hours of rage. Sekh blood. It works as an accelerant and an aphrodisiac, like a stimulant, with the consequences to match. Holy steel and infernal aura The Anu share the Sekh’s base resistances. They resist infernal and holy steel somewhat and can still be cut by both. Near a powerful Vatrajarə they feel a mild warmth or pressure that reads as reverence. Prepared Anu stand fairly well against an aura flare, and are not its intended target. The forms The Nok name of each canine form. The domestic dog is excluded. Form Nok Form Nok Red wolf zhire soro Grey wolf zhige soro Algonquin wolf thanikwin soro African wolf ’kebukhet soro Coyote kasiki Ethiopian wolf ’kebushiri soro Golden jackal zhira fari Dhole boronu African wild dog ’kebukhet bunu Side-striped jackal n’kwosi fari Black-backed jackal zhibe n’khot fari Dire wolf sauni soro Arctic wolf wózèsóró Mexican wolf ranashímù sóró Iberian wolf makénísóró Italian wolf yeizáyùsóró Alaskan Interior wolf wózèthímùsóró Great Plains wolf Khètùkùrèwùsóró Mackenzie Valley wolf Kenyèz’kogoikùrèsóró Arabian wolf shíkùrèsóró British Columbian wolf kómbasóró Hokkaido wolf haidosóró Honshu wolf hodosóró Anu wolf names in the stories use the natural range of a species. That range sometimes follows the person’s own ancestry, and sometimes does not. Emblem and marks Emblem of the Anu. Mark of the Anu. Mate mark of the Anu. h: The pyramid How members rise The Ashborn The trial of sorting Uniforms The nítómó weapon The blindfold and the gloves Opening and closing rifts The Weigher’s palm scale Everyday abilities
x: Home / Earth / The House of Ash / Ranks and tools Ranks and tools Five ranks in a pyramid. Movement is only upward, and the marks of every earlier role stay on the body for good. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. The pyramid Tier Nok name English Core work Marks and gear I ’Ójèpamí Ashborn A governing council of up to 13. Final say on sorting and on who becomes Ashborn. Carries out forced erasures. Keeps institutional memory. Sacred blindfold, weapon talisman, armour, Ash Birds tattoo, any earlier path mark. II Yírạpén Weighers Assess petitions and run the trial of sorting. Never sent into the field. Palm scale tattoo, weapon talisman, slate-grey hooded cloak. III Paiwèpén Collectors Elite field operatives. Track anomalies, carry out contracts, hunt irregularities. May open a rift in an emergency, then must call Ghosthands to clean up. Weapon talisman, assignment pocketbook, plain period clothing. IV Wairùmín Witnesses Silent observers, record keepers and field messengers. Lips are spellbound outside House places. Permanent owl bond, recording pocketbook, plain clothing. IV Zhíwatámowo Ghosthands Open and close rifts and clean up residue. Only they and the Ashborn can do both. Daigímí-and-nítómó gloves, slate-grey coveralls. The base has two entry paths and they stay separate. A Ghosthand never becomes a Witness. Everyone rises from where they began. How members rise From Usual step Rarer New recruit Ghosthand or Witness Collector after a strong trial; Ashborn directly only a handful of times in the House’s history Ghosthand Collector Weigher, or Ashborn after exceptional tenure Witness Weigher Collector, or Ashborn after a long tenure as Weigher Collector Weigher, then Ashborn Ashborn directly, for the highest field merit A mark earned on the way up is kept. A Weigher who began as a Witness keeps the owl. A Collector who began as a Ghosthand keeps the gloves. Current rank tells you what someone does, and their marks tell you where they began. Reading someone’s marks is reading their career. The Ashborn The council is capped at thirteen, mirroring the 13 Dream-Tethered Signs. It is not always full. When a seat opens, the Weighers nominate and the remaining Ashborn choose at their own pace. Roughly nine or ten of the current Ashborn are original river-risen members, so the faces at the top have barely changed. Twelve of the thirteen work in six pairs. The thirteenth leads, delegates and watches the whole institution, and keeps the top pair as right and left hands. The trial of sorting A soul arrives at the threshold in the Ways with no memory of who it was. That emptiness is the first thing the trial measures. A recruit who cannot hold together enough to move through the trial is quietly pulled out and erased. The trial has five parts, always in the same order. Stage Tests for Where What happens 1. Dissolution Ghosthand The Ways The recruit meets a residue, a binding or echo caught in the Ways, and must unmake it gently, without force. 2. Witness Witness The living world The recruit walks through a place where something already happened. They need not act. They are judged on what they saw, concluded and chose not to do. 3. Collection Collector The Ways to the living world An active pursuit. A recruit’s first weapon appears here, not summoned, just present. 4. Weighing Weigher The living world A soul in real distress is put in the recruit’s path. The test is whether they can hold compassion and purpose together. 5. Deep Current Ashborn The river’s edge No instructions. The recruit stands at Kàtúngámün’s edge. Whether the river still speaks to them cannot be performed. Weighers run the first stages and watch closely. Ashborn watch the whole, with one always hidden at Stage 5. Afterwards the Weighers hand their notes to the Ashborn, who hold a closed deliberation, much like a papal conclave, and emerge with every recruit assigned. Every new member is paired with a senior of their rank until the senior judges them ready to work alone. Members who are sorted directly into the Ashborn have extraordinary depth and large gaps. They skipped the years of ordinary rank, and their seniors spend the pairing filling in what they missed. Canon Uniforms Rank What they wear Ashborn Armour fitted to the weapon talisman. A House pin. No fixed civilian uniform. Weigher A hooded slate-grey cloak and a House pin. Collector Neutral clothing suited to the place and period, and a House pin. Each dispatch house keeps a wardrobe for the local era. Witness Plain clothes and a House pin. Ghosthand Slate-grey coveralls, with room for personal style, and a House pin. The nítómó weapon Nítómó is a smooth, steely-grey river stone. The name joins nító , “between,” and mó , “stone.” It exists on both planes at once, which is why it anchors a weapon that must work on both. Everything else used in forging must also come from a river, and is best drawn from both the living world and the Ways. The talisman. The weapon is anchored in a piece of jewellery worn in plain sight and touched to call the weapon. A ring is the usual form. Earrings, necklaces, bracelets and anklets are also valid, but hidden piercings are impractical. The weapon. It is personal and unrepeatable. It first appears at Stage 3 of the trial, already attuned, and nobody else can hold it properly. A second, evolved form can be unlocked through experience and long reflection, though not every member reaches it. The smith. One of the original river-risen Ashborn made the forging technique from nothing, using what the river gave her. All talisman jewellery passes through her, and she works blindfolded. A new member describes the design and mould, fetches the river materials, and brings them to her. Attunement follows as part of induction. The smith’s name and full history are still to be written. Placeholder The blindfold and the gloves Every Ashborn wears a sacred blindfold, woven by the founding weaver, who was among the first recruits and is believed to have been blind in her human life. The blindfold is Dreamleaf woven with natural silk, dyed dark grey-black with tuber extract and mud rich in nítómó ore. It layers two or three times around the head. The ore sharpens every other sense while ordinary sight is shut off, and Ashborn still see the veil with the mind’s eye. All are identical, including the smith’s and the weaver’s own. Taking it off is a serious escalation, and when an Ashborn does, something large is happening. The same weaver made the Ghosthands’ gloves after watching the first Ashborn drain themselves opening rifts with bare hands. The old method is not lost, but only the Ashborn still use it. The weaver’s name and history are also still to be written. Placeholder Opening and closing rifts Opening a rift is easier than closing one. Weapons are quicker and less precise. Bare hands are slower, more controlled and more respected. Thin places near an existing weakness are easier to work than stable ground. Only Ghosthands and Ashborn may open and close rifts. A Collector may open one in an emergency. Everyone else uses the sanctioned gates. The Weigher’s palm scale Every Weigher has a scale tattooed into both palms, received on confirmation of rank. It is an enchantment, not plain ink. Only Weighers and Ashborn can see it. When a Weigher assesses a petition, it glows cool blue to the wearer alone, and the answer is felt inside. To onlookers it looks like this: the Weigher holds out both hands palm-up, and the heavier hand sinks like a true scale. The petitioner senses a judgment being made and cannot see how. Everyday abilities Ability What it does Veil-sight Always on and cannot be turned off. Members see the living world and the Ways beneath it at once, including souls in transit, spiritual residue, thin places and creatures pressing through. New members find it overwhelming. Veterans call it reading depth. Ash Birds Message and parcel delivery along veil routes. Every rank has it. Memory powder An ashen powder from the Ways, thrown or blown and set off by a spoken word. Touch is enough. It works on humans, animals and supernatural beings, Sekh included, and wipes one specific memory. The subject never feels that anything is missing.

x: Home / Earth / The House of Ash / Work and standing Work and standing What the House hunts, what it charges, what lives in its territory, and how the rest of the world sees it. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. What the House hunts Matter Meaning Mortals in the Ways Living souls in the Ways without leave. Most are accidents. Deliberate trespass is more serious. Spirits in the living world Souls or beings from the afterlife or the Ways acting in the living world without a sanctioned crossing. Afterlife bleed-through Souls, residue or objects crossing back into the Ways improperly. Immortality anomalies Contracts, curses or stolen divine mechanisms that keep life going past its thread. This is the founding mandate. Chaos Beast incursions Ways-native creatures breaking into the living world or the afterlife. Soul bindings Anything that stops a soul passing naturally through Kàtúngámün. Unsanctioned rifts Rifts held open by anyone outside the House. This is the most critical matter, since too many unravel the dream-thread. Forgotten entities Ancient presences whose containment is failing. Often handled by the Ashborn in person. The contract function The House answers cosmic imbalance, and it lets outsiders bring an imbalance to its attention for a price. Rejected petitions get no reply. Silence is the answer. Payment The cost Years of life A share of the petitioner’s remaining life, given freely and for good. Core memory A significant memory burned out of the petitioner’s thread entirely. Oath-binding A bond to cosmic neutrality for a set time: no supernatural advantage and no contract. Sacred offering A soul object, divine relic or cursed item of real weight. The House assesses and does not haggle. Vow of silence A lifelong oath never to speak of the House. Breaking it counts as a new imbalance. A petition that is accepted is confirmed in set words: “We, the Thámaijí’Ójèpa, acknowledge your plea. The weight has been measured. The echo is of [nature of imbalance]. Correction is required. Payment is set. Silence is sworn.” Secrecy Members never reveal their affiliation, the House’s existence or their missions, to humans, Sekh, Anu, clergy or any other being, unless a mission puts them in direct conflict, in which case negotiation is allowed. The secrecy feeds the legend, and the House likes it that way. The trigger phrase. Collectors and Witnesses in deep cover each have a personal phrase, known to one Weigher, that cuts through a long-held cover identity and brings back who they are. The owl and the spellbound lips. Witnesses cannot speak outside House places. They send written notes by an owl that is sacred to Nèbémün and trained to cross the Ways. A Collector who receives an owl knows what it means. Headquarters and dispatch houses The main headquarters is in the Ways and not fixed to any place. Members find it by feel, nearness to Kàtúngámün and trained recognition, and petitioners never find it. The founding Ashborn’s continuing work holds it steady. It is where members eat, rest, take assignments, deliberate and return when badly hurt. A few dispatch houses on the living-world side serve as entry points, petition desks, staging grounds and wardrobe stores. Each runs under a long-term cover, and the veil is naturally thin there. How much modern technology the House uses, and how its equipment changes across eras Open Creatures of the Ways Zhí- is the Nok prefix for beasts. It marks a creature, not a liminal one, and anything can fall into the Ways, so many kinds turn up there. These are the species the House tracks most. Nok name English What it is Zhísẹtáná Chaos Beasts Born from raw chaos and native to the Ways. Oil-slick fur that swallows light, a horse-like head with a six-segment snout that unzips, retractable tentacles, three independent eyes on each side with star-shaped pupils, and a whip tail. They range from large-dog size to house-sized. Weak to blessed light, harmonic disruption, Sekh or Anu bites, the presence of Zhímá’ạt’tárá, or weapons made from their parts. Zhíwaimísei Aether Wyrms Huge translucent worms that tunnel through reality and leave rifts and anomalies behind. Among the most dangerous things the House tracks. Yẹzhígowá Mirror Phantoms Beings that live in reflections and can step briefly into the living world to nudge events. They leave very little trace. Hódázhí The Forsaken Humanlike creatures born from the deepest regrets of celestial beings, given life by mass loss and loss of faith. They try to make more of their kind by driving people to despair. Zhímá’ạt’tárá Guardians of the Veil Lion-sized cats with aurora-shifting fur, who guard the veil on their own instinct at Nèbémün’s bidding. They help the House when they appear and cannot be summoned. Their presence alone keeps Chaos Beasts away. Zhíkhaidu Shadow entities Ghostly beings that slip through cracks in reality. Open How others see the House Who View Nẹránamün’s gods All are honoured. Loyalty is to Nyámün alone. ’Ègúngumáyámün, Kàtúngámün and Nèbémün are closest, as senior coworkers in Nyámün’s will, not patrons. Kàtúngámün holds a maternal place for some members. Nèbémün is an indirect ally through her Zhímá’ạt’tárá. ’Anpésùmün Mutual respect and shared ground, no formal arrangement. Sekh Many call the House a bogeyman. Some elders know better. One petition sits in the restricted archive. Anu The Düfari pulses in recognition near House members. Elder packs say nothing. Clergy Old priests know. They flinch when the wind dies too suddenly, and some leave quiet offerings at unmarked sites. Infernal hierarchy Natural enemies who deal when they must. The wyrms’ rift-tunnelling helps the Infernals’ aims by accident, and the House tracks it. Lamiae They fear the House absolutely, because it can erase immortals. They never petition. They go quiet. Humans Folklore and legend, as the secrecy intends. Sayings Heard across the supernatural world, source unknown “Ash has no memory, only purpose.” “When you cannot burn it or bury it, Ash will take it.” “Balance remembers what we forget.” “Don’t bring the Ash on us.” “The 13th sign gives death-touched children. Some things you don’t question.” Spoken by very old clergy, never in public “They were here before the schism. They will be here after us.” Some House matters are kept out of this almanac on purpose. Decided Zhíkhaidu The Zhíkhaidu, the shadow entities listed above, drawn as silhouettes. Concept image.

h: At a glance The three-part philosophy The three realms The Ways Between Tether points The Three Tides of Kàtúngámün Origin What members are The covenant Colours and marks
x: Home / Earth / The House of Ash The House of Ash A member of the House in a living-world form. Concept image. Thámaijí’Ójèpa keeps the balance between the living world, the afterlife and the Ways that lie between. Most Sekh think of it as a bogeyman. The House does nothing to correct them. “No flame claimed them. No jackal watched them. The river simply kept them.” Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. At a glance Nok name Thámaijí’Ójèpa, “the House of Ash.” What it does Hunts what is out of place across the three realms, and answers petitions about cosmic imbalance for a price. Who belongs Human souls only. A Sekh, Anu or Lamiae cannot join. Headquarters In the Ways Between, in a place that is found by feel and never by map. Loyalty To Nyámün’s dream itself, not to any single god. The three-part philosophy No single rank holds the whole of the House’s work. The division is deliberate, so that no one person can misuse it. Truth is witnessed. This is the work of the Wairùmín. Truth is understood. This is the work of the Yírạpén. Truth is acted upon. This is the work of the Paiwèpén. The Ashborn, the 'Ójèpamí, hold all three, and the weight of knowing when each applies. Four principles follow from it. Nothing is erased without leaving something behind. Truth must be seen before it is acted on. Power is divided to prevent imbalance. The marks of a member’s past roles never leave them. The three realms Nyámün, the All-Creator, dreams, and the dream holds everything. All three realms below are joined through the Ways. Realm Nok name What it is House colour The mortal world ’Ätozo The living realm, where humans, Sekh, Anu, Lamiae and every embodied being live. Black The Ways Between Thákónítókwéchè, often Thákóníkwé The liminal space of Nyámün’s unresolved dreaming, raw potential that comes before form. Rusted gold The afterlife ’Ätáru The world of the dead, separated from the living world by Nèbémün’s veil. Grey Grey is the House’s main colour: the ash that remains when the living world’s black and the Ways’ gold are both gone. It shows in slate-grey cloaks and coveralls, and gives the House a deliberately funerary look. The Ways Between The Ways are not ordered and not chaotic. They are the moment before either one decides what to be. Terrain shifts, distances disagree, time runs differently in different pockets, and landmarks do not hold from one visit to the next. Experienced members navigate by feel, following the current of Kàtúngámün, the river that is the Ways’ one stable feature. Kàtúngámün runs through the Ways and carries souls across all three of its tides. Chaos Beasts are native to the Ways. Their crossings into the living world are a main House concern. Things fall through rips in Nèbémün’s veil: people, objects, fragments of events. All of it is House business. The Ways have their own ecosystem. Members eat there, and Ways food feeds them in a way living-world food does not. Tether points Divinely anchored. Places where a god’s lasting presence steadies the Ways. Nẹránamün temples stand where communities recognised an anchor and built toward it. Engineered gates. Places held open by constant effort, including the House’s headquarters and dispatch gates. The House watches the number of open rifts closely. Too many held open at once could unravel the thread of Nyámün’s dream. That is not a figure of speech, and it outranks every contract the House takes. Canon ’Anpésùmün, the Opener of Ways, keeps a strong presence in the Ways, and every sanctioned crossing passes through his doorways. The House shares the ground with him in mutual respect and no formal arrangement. The exact working relationship between ’Anpésùmün and the House Open The Three Tides of Kàtúngámün Tide What it does First Carries souls whose threads are complete forward through the veil into ’Ätáru. Second Carries souls back through Daimuzónobu to be reborn, because they are not finished with the living world. Third Pulls sideways, into neither rest nor return. This is the current that calls House members. No temple canon names it. Origin No founding document exists, and the House would never allow one. What survives is one fragment, quoted differently in three sealed archives: “In the time when the river ran thick, when the boundary between ’Ätozo and ’Ätáru thinned to membrane, when wandering souls moved through the living world like winter through cracked walls, something rose. Not from above. Not from below. From within the water itself.” What made the river run thick is not recorded. The institution that erases things erased its own beginning, and the House considers that appropriate. The first members did not join. They rose out of Kàtúngámün fully formed on the day of the founding event, with no past lives and no earlier ranks, already caretakers of balance. The contract work came later. What members are Members are human souls who answered the Third Tide. They are not alive, not dead, not undead and not reborn. They are suspended: present in the living world with full body and mind, but not woven into Daimuzónobu the way the living are. Trait Detail Memory None of their human life. Name, family, age and death are all severed at entry. They take a House name and keep no birthdays. Shapeshifting Develops early. Voice, face, build and apparent age can be changed at will. The change is bodily, not an illusion, so a form with a bad knee brings a bad knee. A full change takes a day or two, and forms far from the default cost more energy. Food and water No need to eat in the living world. They can go about two human years without food on a long mission. They eat in the Ways. Water in any realm sustains them. Rest Can be put off for about twice the human limit before performance suffers. Healing Strong, but slower with a severed limb or a form far from the default. Severe damage makes a member fade and return to headquarters in a coma for one to two weeks. Body They can bleed, fall ill in appearance and have sex, but none of it truly affects them. They cannot sicken, cannot run out of blood, cannot pass on disease and cannot have children. Their blood is deadly to a human if infused. Bonds Outside the supernatural mating network. They feel human emotions, most strongly in deep cover, but train toward detachment. Friendship between partners is encouraged. The House is not cold, only clear about what it is. Ending The only known way to erase a member permanently is a nítómó weapon. The full mechanics are still to be written. How the nítómó weapon erases a member, in full Open The covenant When a soul steps from the current onto the shore of the Third Tide, the covenant seals. Prior name, life and death are severed, and the House keeps no record of what the soul was. It does not expire. There is no retirement and no release. Breaking the laws ends in erasure. The Ashborn carry it out. Demotion does not exist, and every member knows it. “The river chose. The river keeps.” Colours and marks Mark What it is N’túw’ójèpa, the Ojepa Eye The House’s official emblem, used on pins, seals and papers. The outer ring stands for containment, and for the nítómó ring talisman carried by every Collector and above. The vertical line is Nyámün’s dream-thread running through all three realms. The three dots are the three realms. The black interior is ash, void and erasure. ’Ójèpakimai, the Ash Birds The tattoo every member carries in every form. Two birds fly in different directions through the same space, like the House’s double sight of both sides of the veil. A bird can detach, carry a message or small object along veil routes, and return to the sender’s skin. If it is struck in flight it drops its load and flies home. It does not think for itself. Emblem of the House of Ash. The emblem with the Nok name. The Ash Birds, ’Ójèpakimai. Ranks and tools The five ranks, the trial of sorting, uniforms, the nítómó talisman and the Ashborn’s blindfold. Work and standing What the House hunts, how petitions are paid, creatures of the Ways, secrecy and how others see it.

h: The ladder Bediens Standing Servi Abilities, side by side
x: Home / Earth / Emsehurst / Bediens and Servi Bediens and Servi Humans tied to Lamiae . Some tied themselves, some were caught, and some were born into it. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. The ladder Step Who Ordinary human Free, and protected by Pandora’s Pact . Bedien A human in a relationship with a Lamiae: addicted, contracted, or born into it. Servus A human formally blood-bonded to a Lamiae master through a short but permanent ritual. Bediens A Bedien is a human in a relationship with a Lamiae, willing or not. The range is wide. The addicted. Humans who sought out Lamiae blood for its euphoric, aphrodisiac effect and could not stop. The first effects are intensely pleasurable, and the long-term toll on the body is heavy. Many began as willing and underestimated it. The contracted. Humans who signed a blood contract pledging life force, service or both as security for a deal with a Lamiae master. Some owed a debt, some were taken, and some were born into it, bred across generations in Lamiae households. Standing Bediens have almost no legal standing in Emsehurst, and their bondage is invisible to the wider human world. Inside SxSW they are more open, working as performers, domestic workers and, in private, as food and in sexual service. Outside SxSW the bondage is hidden. They appear on no register. Pandora’s Pact protects humans from being forced into this life, but in practice only the Sekh enforce it, and only while they are present and watching. Servi A servus (plural servi) is a human permanently blood-bonded to a Lamiae master through a deliberate ritual. Ordinary feeding never creates the bond. A servus is a step above a Bedien, and the two are different categories. The bond is total. Gains Senses and endurance beyond a normal human: faster, sharper, harder to hurt. Still below a Lamiae or a Sekh. The servus also feels the master’s pain. Loses Autonomy. A servus cannot disobey a direct order from their master. It is a total power exchange written into the body. Death clause If the master dies, from any cause, violent or not, the servus dies too. No way of release is known. Decided It does not work in reverse: a master can outlive a servus, though some choose not to. Turning Only if the master deliberately kills the servus. The bond makes the Turning more likely to succeed than it is for an ordinary human. Death from the master’s own death is a different thing and is not a Turning. Decided Where found Close to their masters, as drivers, bodyguards, household staff and personal assistants. Some Lamiae networks run largely on servi in logistics and public-facing roles. Under the Pact The 1933 text calls them “bonded servants” and treats them as an internal matter for the Lamiae, so long as nobody is taken by force from the general human population in and around Emsehurst. Taking people by force breaches the Pact. The 1964 addendum made the Lamiae a signatory with the same duties. Abilities, side by side Group Supernatural ability Bediens None of their own. Some receive temporary fortifying spells contracted from Witches, and some are subjects of experimental genetic enhancement. Servi Enhanced senses and endurance from the bond. Cannot disobey their master. Die if the master dies. A Bedien does not automatically gain a servus’s gifts or bond. Named masters and their households are left to the character material. Decided

x: Home / Earth / The Nok / Calendar Calendar and festivals The Nok year has twelve named months of thirty days, followed by a five-day sacred month. It follows the Gregorian year closely. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. Epoch Year 1 of the Nok count, Shòní, is 379 BCE. For dates in the common era, the Nok year is the CE year plus 379. For dates before the common era, Kishòní equals the Gregorian BCE year minus 380. So 1982 CE is 2361 Shòní. In those years Khèmọnai runs Jan 30 to Feb 4, and every month after it shifts up one date number but keeps its length. The sacred days of Khèmọnai Day Name Meaning 1 Khèmärạmís Sacred Eternal Day 2 Zhèmídíyèkhèm Sacred Day of Wisdom and Sharing 3 Wạkùnézóníkhèm Sacred Day of Life’s Eternal Cycle 4 Shëraikhèm Strength of the Sacred, celebrating warriors and war games 5 Kwínòfùmakhèm Sacred Memory of Ancestors 6 (leap years) Kòbíkhèm Sacred Release Day: a day of legal purging of dark desires and catharsis, with saunas, rage rooms, firewalking and hedonistic parties No other events are scheduled on these days besides the religious ceremonies. School and work stop completely. The week The Nok week has six days, so each thirty-day month holds five of them. The seventh Gregorian day is named only for translation. Decided The six-day week is the same as the civil week of Kanna, which the Nok are said to have chosen for that reason. Their months run thirty days against Kanna’s twenty-four, because the Nok count Earth days and not Kanna’s.
