Lives loud, dies proud Sunmirror: Gentle rulers who shine light on others; draw communities like a hearth Zhíwanògbàtí Ghostroot Weighted by ancestral voices / speaks through tradition Tuskwalker: Holds sacred grudges for generations; protects burial grounds and historical justice Memorytender: Recites forgotten names and sings old languages into new life; gentle historian Nèbémí Veilborn Hides too deeply in the past / guards what should not be crossed Boneeye: Watches from shadows; may withhold truth to protect; seen as eerie or prophetic Whispersky: Moves silently, speaks with the dead, guides the lost; priestesses and mentors Kwoirádíkhùtạra Eclipseguard Fixates on what might have been / sees strategy in every cycle Howlbrand: Ruthlessly protective; tracks power shifts; war tacticians and oath-forged sentinels Echofang: Silent pathfinders who guard collective memory; twilight diplomacy and death rites Móhónikómbụn Stoneweaver Rooted so deep they forget to grow / moulds change through stillness Rivermaw: Calm with unspoken fury; destroys when threatened Muddreamer: Grounded spiritualists who heal through stillness; gentle giants of the Dream Nímusákhéyí Nightglow Walks gently through inherited grief / guides by moonlight and dream Heartstreak: Quick, alert and guarded; pain shows only in poetry Moonstep: Dances between shadows; soothes the broken by presence; mourning and moon rites Kaníshạng’shạng Heartforged Carries past wounds like coals / leads others through trials with courage Bloodlaugh: Laughs at pain and taunts death; fights dirty, loves loud Shadowgrin: Survivor-souls who protect misfits; turn wounds into wild wisdom Daimùtèzun The Dreamwalker Drifts without anchor / rewrites fate across the stars Threadcutter: Erases old patterns, questions fate, cannot be bound Starweaver: Wakes others inside their dreams; sees futures others cannot endure When the quiz and the birth sign disagree A person can be born under one sign and score the Dreamwalker on an alignment quiz. The source notes offer three readings: Proposed A Sign-Bound Dreamwalker : keeps the birth sign but carries dual-thread potential. Exceptionally rare, perhaps born under an eclipse or a Daimùzónobu storm. A misalignment in childhood: the alignment shifted, the sign did not. A Thread Correction Rite is rarely performed. A false reading : the Dream tests us with illusions. The Kihódání‘obuwásóka rite confirms the truth. Open questions The two reference sheets spell the plural “Wainódudaimukitaismí” and “Wainódudaimukitaisamí”. Confirm one. Open The patron of Sign 13 is written Írubámün and Írábúkhmün here; elsewhere with an initial ‘Í. Standardise. Open The Sign 13 lucky day is Day 2 of the sacred month, which is Zhèmídíyèkhèm. Open

h: Wearing a thread Through a life Spoken phrases The severance
x: Home / Earth / The Nok / Thread tradition The thread tradition Every mature Anu wears a thread: a visible sign that they walk the Dream, and a way to show who they are walking it with. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. The Nok name for it, Dúmùkwò, loosely “thread binding,” is a working name and may change. Proposed Everything on this page is Proposed until confirmed. Wearing a thread A mature Anu wears a thread around the hair, braided in, woven into a loc or tucked behind the ear, or around the neck as a cord or talisman. Each is a little different in colour, weave and material, because each is a spirit. It is private but visible, and it says: “I am a walker of the Dream.” Through a life Stage Thread Meaning Childhood and training None, or a tiny plain one Still learning. Adulthood A personal thread at hair or neck Walking the Dream independently. Courting A small piece of the other’s thread braided into your own A soft promise that is easily undone without shame. Mating Cores exchanged, or a new thread woven from both Two life paths permanently joined. Mourning A broken thread tied to the wrist Honouring loss until the mourning period ends. Letting go The broken thread buried at a sacred spring Returning the dead to the Hunt. After a formal bond the original thread is kept in a secondary place, such as a wrist or near the heart. Some traditional Anu burn the old thread at the ceremony and weave a new one together. Loose threads mean unmated. Woven or shared threads mean bonded. Frayed or snapped threads mean death, betrayal or deep mourning. Spoken phrases When Phrase Weaving a lover’s thread “I carry your thread beside mine.” Exchanging threads at a mate bond “Your hunt is my hunt. Your thread is my thread.” Mourning a mate “Your thread runs in the Dream. I follow the trail behind you.” Burying a broken thread “I release your thread to the Hunt.” Swearing brotherhood, not romantic “Two threads. One hunt.” Public severance “Your thread is cut. Your name falls into silence.” Private break “Your thread frays. I walk without you.” The severance In rare, tragic cases of betrayal, murder or abandonment, the wronged Anu cuts or burns the thread of the other before witnesses at the central fire or sacred spring. The thread is not buried with honour. It is thrown into a wild fire or onto black stone. Being cut off is shameful for the one cut, not for the one who cuts. Severed threads are sometimes kept in clan memory songs as a warning: “Remember ____, whose thread was burned.” The pack may still honour the soul in the Dream but no longer protects the name with warmth.

h: How a contract works The architecture Generations What each generation can do Amplifying a spell Renewal Who leads a line Marriage, half-witches and mixed lines What a half-witch perceives Line dedication Selo and spells
x: Home / Earth / The Witches of Mephis / Contracts and power Contracts and power A witch’s magic is a loan with terms. The terms run in the blood, and they come due every ten generations. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Witches of Mephis reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. How a contract works Power A blood contract with the patron. The bond weakens over time and must be renewed every ten generations. Specialty and sacrifice Each contract has a specialty and a sacrifice, the price. A witch also gains the general ability to see magic and a small natural resistance to its influence. Coming into power A full witch comes into power between 8 and 14 or 15. A mixed full witch may take until 18. A sacrifice that shows from birth is always present. A sacrifice that does not show from birth arrives gradually over the year after renewal. Refusing to renew The family loses all its power. Depending on the patron’s mood, the family may be wiped out. The architecture The patron is Mephithoveles , the first of the eight princes of Ishphaeno. Mephis is the name the witches know him by, and the system of blood contracts is his design. Decided The gift. What he gives a witch is a shard of his own soul, split off and bound into theirs. It is a one-way gift. He stays whole. The witch carries a piece of him for as long as the contract holds, and does not entirely remain themselves, because something of him lives in them from then on. The raw material. His domain is pride, and with it worship: the energy a person gives off when something in them changes because of what they were offered. The contract turns that into power for the witch and a harvest for him. The shape. A family contract is open-ended and runs down the bloodline for as many generations as it renews. There is no set end. An older line at work: the Drummonds. By the early 1810s the contracts were already old enough to be a trade. In the Scottish Highlands the Drummond line, with its power over barriers and wards, had a fifth-generation witch in Griselda Drummond, who married into the name Hawthorne and was known in society as Lady Hawthorne. Her coven cleaned and sold cursed artifacts to private bidders from her own cellar, among them a Lamia’s agent, a human occultist and a rival witch, and her wards kept the cellar and its guests safe. The Drummond price is the body’s own feeling. Each time a Drummond casts, sensation drains from the skin and the nerves, a little at a time and for good. The more she casts, and the stronger the casting, the faster it goes. By middle age Lady Hawthorne could hold a wide barrier almost in conversation and had not felt pain properly in years, and in company this read as perfect composure. Witches did not hide the arrangement from one another. They ran it as a business under their patron’s terms. Decided The Drummonds are shown as one example. The terms of other lines are not published here. Each line’s contract is its own. See the ten family lines . Decided Generations Original signers are Gen 1, their children Gen 2, and so on. Adoption and marriage adjust this: a half-witch adopted by a Gen 2 becomes Gen 1, and a non-witch adopted becomes Gen 2. On renewal the 10th gen becomes the new Gen 1. Full-witch children alive in that generation join it as their sacrifice matures over the year, and children born within that year are new Gen 1 as well. Children born later are Gen 2. What each generation can do The abilities stack, so a Gen 1 witch can do everything below. Decided Generation Abilities Gen 1 to 3 Bond minions. With Lamiae or Sekh blood, cast enhancement spells on humans. Gen 1 to 5 Basic barriers and protections, such as warding a house. A spirit or animal familiar, which acts as a messenger and a spy. Spirits cannot physically affect Earth. Gen 6 to 9 A weaker version of the family specialty, and the ability to create blood contracts. Gen 10 Nothing until renewal. Minions are familiar-like servants and constructs: a raven familiar, a golem, a water witch’s water animus. Decided Amplifying a spell More than one witch casting in unison. New moons and equinoxes. The essence of a magical creature, such as a Fae or a Lamia. Lamiae blood in particular boosts a spell significantly and, for the strongest spells, may be necessary. Decided Witches have the usual human weaknesses, a small natural resistance to magic, and a stronger susceptibility to Temptation unless their specialty or an artifact counters it. Renewal The ceremony. The head of the 10th gen negotiates with the patron in a family-wide ceremony where he is summoned. Only full witches take part. The age. The head negotiates at 19 by default. Some families have special contracts. The Gilbert line is one, and renews when its 10th gen turns 30. Decided The weakest generation. The 10th gen always starts with no abilities, no specialty and no sacrifice paid. The choice. Renew as it is, or offer a new sacrifice for a new power. Renewing with the old sacrifice makes everyone stronger for a year before the older generations fade. A new specialty makes every earlier generation lose its power over six months. Signing. The head signs in their own blood. Today that means a fountain pen loaded with a vial of blood, because many agreements bond with the genetic code. Any witch making a sacrifice that year signs too. Who leads a line Each line decides for itself, and the methods differ by culture: the original signer, if alive. A biological hierarchy with a Main Family in charge. A contest of power and will among the 10th gen. Seniority. An election with campaigns and tests. Or a multigenerational council with a 10th-gen chair. Marriage, half-witches and mixed lines A non-witch spouse may sign the family contract by addendum, make the sacrifice and become a full witch in their spouse’s generation. They may instead stay a non-witch with no access to magic. A half-witch , with one full witch parent, cannot practise magic but always perceives it. A half-witch who marries a full witch may sign on and become a full witch one generation up from their spouse. A half-witch and a full witch have an even chance of a witch child, who can inherit either line’s specialty. A child who does not practise is a mixed half-witch. A half-witch and a non-witch always have a non-witch child. Only mixed full witches can sign or renew contracts. Mixed half-witches must be adopted or married in. Two full witches from different families have a child who manifests one ability with its sacrifice and is counted with that line. What a half-witch perceives It is passive and unchosen. It is sensory and impressionistic, never forensic, and it cannot be suppressed or trained into magic without a contract. Many half-witches never attend a Conservatory and invent their own frameworks. True forms. Supernatural beings cannot hide their nature, though the half-witch has no automatic way to name it. Enchanted objects. A faint luminosity, or a sense of wrongness. Active castings. A flash or ripple, with no knowledge of the spell or the caster. Residual magic. A scent, temperature or sound, the same each time for the same person. They cannot name species without education, read signatures, detect a servus bond, or perceive magic that has fully faded. Line dedication By default a child takes the line of the gestational parent. A dedication overrides that. In Selo it is Insignatio Lineae . A child can be dedicated to a line at three points: before birth, after quickening and before the seventh month; at adoption; or as an adult, in a harsher ritual with a sponsor. Decided Both parents attend, with a representative of the chosen line and an officiant who is a contract scholar. Witnesses and an elder of the releasing line are optional. Beat What happens 1. Naming Full names, magus names, lines, generations and prices are declared. 2. The sigil A Selo sigil is drawn on the womb in blood-and-element ink. The default line’s sigil may first be traced faintly, then overwritten. 3. Vow and registration A record copy goes to the parents and the chosen line, and the patron’s registry is updated. 4. Release The sacrifice flares. The sigil may vanish, fade, or heal into a scar like a C-section. The carrier feels the chosen line’s sacrifice for a while. The baby has no physical mark. If the gestational parent is human, the rite creates the bond and hits harder. Dedicating a child to a 10th-gen line locks the child into the renewal stakes. Selo and spells Selo ( Se³lo³ ) is the universal infernal administrative language and the spine of every official document. Decided It has six tones. A syllable is (C)(w/j)V(N), and the only codas are n and ng. It has four scripts: sin¹ si³ , logoglyphs; yu¹ si³ , a helper syllabary; ro¹ si³ , a romanisation; and do¹ lo³ , the native reading. In¹ marks the plural. Aspect and sentence-final particles carry mood, among them zó, mǎ, hà, lâ, lân, nè, mà and má. Latin supplies many roots. IGN-, for example, becomes ing¹ . Spells are cast in the regional Great Tongue, which is Latin in the Americas and Europe, with short Selo “Min” forms and glyph writing. Each circle’s own Great Tongue is used alongside Selo. Decided The spell lists in the older drafts, including the general Latin incantations and the line-specific lists, are due for a rewrite and are not reproduced here. Placeholder

x: Home / Earth / The Witches of Mephis / The ten family lines The ten family lines Five lines founded the Emsehurst chapter together. Five more joined later, each on its own day. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Witches of Mephis reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. The lines Line Power Price Generation now Emmers Shadow manipulation. Hard objects can be moved as weapons, but the shadow cannot enter them. The strongest can move objects through them. Schizophrenia, with onset that varies with use. 8th and 9th Bonchild Charmspeak. Cannot lie. Stronger generations lose their voice, and weaker ones bleed and choke. 4th and 5th Gilbert Sight of the future. Renews on a special 30-year schedule. Blindness. 9th and 10th Somerhalder Forging magical weapons. Dyslexia and ADHD. Higher generations struggle to sit still. 3rd Payne Telepathy. Deafness. 1st Velasco Plants. Compulsory veganism, with varying reactions. 1st and 2nd Tlaloc Water. Blood sacrifice and lifelong hemophilia or anemia. 1st and 2nd Orendanansi Shapeshifting into beasts. Borderline personality disorder: anger issues, or chronic depression in human form. 6th and 7th Costello Memory-coherence manipulation, used for healing. Reality “rewrites” slightly each time. 3rd Cooper Object teleportation. Spatial Fixation Disorder, with an OCD presentation. 5th Named members of each line are left to the character material. Decided When each line signed Each estimate is counted back from the line’s current generation at about 30 years a generation, calibrated on the Orendanansi. They are estimates only. Decided Line Estimated period Emmers and Gilbert, first cycle (8th to 10th gen) About the 1770s to 1800 The Emsehurst founding, all five lines signing together About the 1780s to 1790s Orendanansi 1851, fixed Cooper (5th gen) About the 1890s to 1920s Costello (3rd gen) About the 1950s to 1970s Velasco and Tlaloc (1st and 2nd gen) About the 1990s to 2010s The generation counts for Bonchild (4th or 5th), Somerhalder (3rd) and Payne (1st) do not fit one shared signing in the 1780s or 1790s. Renewals, new-specialty renegotiations, or marriage and adoption adjustments might explain it. Not urgent Open A line from the Highlands One line outside the ten is known from the early 1810s: the Drummonds of the Scottish Highlands. Their power is over barriers and wards. Their price is the body’s own feeling, which drains from the skin and nerves with every casting and does not return. A fifth-generation Drummond in that period held a wide barrier almost in conversation and could no longer feel pain properly. See the contracts page for her coven. Decided The Orendanansi Akan captives, brought illegally to America in 1810, escaped to the Mohawk Nation in 1824. After two years they fell in love and, in 1827, founded their own tribe in upstate New York. After the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850 they moved to West Virginia, in 1852. They worship Anansi and Orenda . Before any contract they had animal-strength gifts, in short bursts or from birth: monkey-like agility, cheetah speed, rhino-like skin. The First Night of Mefi, 1851 Three elders led a seven-night ritual, two as officiants and one as scribe. Everyone gave blood. On the seventh night a figure of spider and man appeared: Mefi, Keeper of Contracts. In exchange for beast-shifting he set the price, a spirit burden, and the renewal every ten generations. The blood rose like threads, blackened and pooled. The elders signed with a bone stylus. Anyone over 19 at the time became Gen 1, and anyone under 19 became Gen 2. Decided Names The Orendanansi name persists in ritual and in the patron’s records. After the Snyder Act of 1924 the family took English surnames: Greenwood, Highwood, Ironwood, Lightwood, Songwood, Redwood, Windwood, Stormwood and Hearthwood. The marriages of the 1850s carry these names retroactively. Male children take the more prestigious parent’s name. Female children take their father’s. The clan leader is voted in at each renewal, usually from the Greenwoods or the Highwoods. The surname rule does not say what happens in a same-sex couple Open The Costello tiers Tier What it does 1. Contact healing The injury ghosts onto the healer. 2. Memory Descent Trance, time dilation and memory anchors. 3. Somatic Manifestation Damage externalises onto the caster. The first two generations have all three tiers. The third manages tier 3 only with help. A forbidden ritual, Healing Body Coherence , or the “Second Silence,” wakes a dead body for minutes. The soul is gone, and those who patrol the dead notice. The Cooper stability scale An object’s stability when teleported falls as it matters more to someone: functional objects are stable. Then come owned and replaceable objects, gifted objects, identity objects, heirlooms, sacred or contract-tied objects, and finally permanence objects. Frequent teleporting destabilises an object, and the Spatial Fixation Disorder is worst in the earliest generations. Sacred and contract-tied objects, including Sekh, Anu and Lamiae artifacts, draw magical attention.

x: Home / Earth / The Witches of Mephis / The Mephis Consortium The Mephis Consortium Sixty schools in seven circles, joined by one administrative tongue, one entrance test and one rule about how long a student may stay. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Witches of Mephis reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. Core rules Selo is required everywhere. Each circle also teaches one or two regional Great Tongues. Study. The standard course is four years: Foundation in years 1 and 2, then specialisation in years 3 and 4. The maximum enrolment is six years. Years 5 and 6 are extended study: repeating a year, changing tracks, research or teacher preparation. At the end of year 6 a student must graduate, join the staff or apprentice, or be released. Foundation. A unified curriculum of Magic Life Skills (cost literacy, spellcraft, wards, contract literacy, healing, divination and ritual basics) and liberal arts. Nobody skips Foundation. After three years without stabilising, candidacy ends and the student is referred back to line elders or mentors. Leaves and transfers. A leave of absence need not count toward the six years. Transfers within the Network keep a student’s standing, and years add up across schools. Age of entry. 15 to 20 for full enrolment. Junior programmes and legacy students Junior Programmes take early manifesters from 8 to 15. They do not count as full enrolment and cannot be used to get around the six-year cap. Asian-circle schools more often run residential lower divisions. North American schools may keep early manifesters at home and use day classes. Legacy status is for the contractless: Lineborn 10th-gen heirs, half-witches, adopted wards and declared dependents. They get non-fuelled instruction only (Selo literacy, history, contract law, cost theory, forms, circle layouts, sigils and ward diagrams). They are barred from fuelled casting, high-risk rituals and combat tracks, and their time does not count toward the cap. A 10th-gen heir who signs becomes an Active Witch, and the clock starts. Adult late inductees , over about 22, are trained mainly by line, house or spouse, with modular Conservatory courses. A young spouse inside the 15 to 20 window may be admitted as a full student. A spouse who does not contract may attend select lectures only. Getting in S-CAT , the Standard Consortium Aptitude Test: a written and oral exam, a practical manifestation check and a confessional interview. It can be retaken once a year after a total crash. It is a placement tool, not a filter. Local trial, Gate 2. It differs by school. In most circles the token lasts one lunar cycle, each witch gets at most two tokens and two full attempts, and trial windows come twice a year, a season apart. A guide leads the candidate to the site once per attempt, and after that the candidate finishes alone. The outcomes are pass, place-down (admitted with stricter pacing) or fail (no admission this attempt). The Consortium Circuit. The competitions: Clause and Contract; Wards and Structures; Applied Casting; Control and Cost; Craft and Interface; sparring; and obstacle events that are not yet named. Fula, in its Ajami and Adlam scripts, is a noted alternative and has not been adopted. Mandinka is Mande, not Bantu. x: Home / Earth / The Witches of Mephis The Witches of Mephis A witch of Emsehurst. Concept image. Families who trade a price for power. Every contract is signed in blood with one patron, and every contract must be renewed. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Witches of Mephis reference (v3). Tags mark anything less settled. At a glance Patron Mephis, who is Mephithoveles, the first prince of Ishphaeno. The settlers of Emerson met him as Itzal, one of the many names he uses, and the Orendanansi line calls him Mefi. Power Blood contracts. The bond weakens over time and must be renewed every ten generations. Price Each contract gives a specialty and takes a sacrifice. The line’s head, or its symbolic signer, sets both. Blood Always AB positive or AB negative. Tools No wands. Talismans and artifacts help a witch focus, and some families craft enchanted items. Names A witch has a human name and a magus name. The magus name keeps the family line name so witches can recognise one another. Network Sixty schools in seven circles, joined as the Mephis Consortium. See The Mephis Consortium . Origin The patron has made contracts with bloodlines all over the world for about two thousand years. Emsehurst was not the first chapter. It is the showcase chapter, the main setting of the stories, and the most sophisticated structure he has built. Decided The founding of the Emsehurst chapter Eight families settled at the mouth of the Emerson, a tributary of the Squannock. Their leader was taken. The settlers who were taken came back possessed and killed two families, and a teenage girl, the sole survivor, was burned at the stake. Prayer failed. One family fled. At sunset Itzal arrived and offered power in exchange for three things: Secrets, Pride and Servitude. The five founding lines of Emsehurst signed together, in the order Emmers, Bonchild, Gilbert, Somerhalder and Payne. They are the five witch signatories to Pandora’s Pact . Decided Every other line has its own, separate origin date. Five more lines joined later, each on a different day. See the ten family lines . Relations Who How they stand Pandora’s Pact The Witches hold stewardship of their establishments, homes and places of practice, and their contracts are their own business. One witch from each of the five founding families signed in 1933 and again in 1964. The Lamiae See The Lamiae . Their blood is a major amplifier of witch spells, and for the strongest spells it may be necessary. The Sekh Sekh blood also works for enhancement spells on humans. The two peoples are opposed in principle over souls that are trapped and tricked. The Anu Opposed for the same reason. The Human Coalition Hostile in public, and in private some members buy enchanted items and fortifying spells from witches. Emblem Emblem of the Witches of Mephis. h: At a glance The sacred arts they practise In Emsehurst The hope of Rebirth The Anu-side parallel Open questions
x: Home / Earth / Emsehurst / Zingans Zingans Human devotees of ’Èn’zíngámün, the flame and storm daughter of Nyámün. They live close to the Sekh, and some of them hope to become Sekh. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Earth reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Nok spellings follow the current reference documents. At a glance English name Zingans. “Sekh” stays as the one holdover from the old name. Decided Nok name Shùkízíngámùna, in speech Shùkízímù, “followers of ’Èn’zíngámün.” Wider faith They belong to the Shùkíneirana, the True Dreamers, which includes every follower of Nẹránamün. Anyone descended from a Nẹránamün culture, practising or not, is a Daimùyùnä. Those who leave are Lost Dreamers, Hányídaimùyùnä, and some call themselves Kiwásómùna, the woken ones. Ascetic sect The Ikhùkímùna, the Flame Followers, also called the Red Choir or the Choir of Red Dust: ritual dancers, oral keepers, blood-rite singers and temple guardians. They use red ochre and burnt cloth, and keep the tales of Nzinga’s fire. Its devout monastic branch is the House of Ember. Both follow the thirty threads. Symbol The Symbol of the Faithful, Jaibütùw’éh: the divine flame circle with an eye at its centre. Zingans and Sekh both wear it, and the Sekh prefer not to be conspicuous. Place in the Sekh tier system At the base, below formal Sekh acolytes (Sèkhèt’mùna), who are human devotees in training or in the service of the faith. Zingans are recognised as members of the faith and protected in Sekh territory. Abilities None innate, and none gained from worship. They do learn Makésho, the sacred arts, which are open to Zingans and Sekh alike. A lifelong devotee can outdo an untrained Sekh. Decided The sacred arts they practise Fùmamaké , sacred ritual tattooing. Daigímíwaḳùn , Dreamleaf trance and veil-thinning. Nímawaḳùn , ritual healing, herb-lore and thread-reading. Daimùwaḳùn , counsel through the 13 Dream-Tethered Signs. Ikhùwaḳùn , performance as ritual: chant and blood rite, done by the Red Choir. Each is described on Sacred arts and symbols . In Emsehurst Most Zingans live in the Zingan Quarter, east of the Squannock River in the Merveilles Valley. The district has had this name in every source, including the 1933 Pact. Decided Yírímbo Zonémi is their spiritual and teaching centre, founded in 1738 in Hurste. It is the oldest Nẹránamün institution still working in the Americas. Moreau College ( Móró Khọzìyí ) is the college where the faith’s two groups meet: devotees who have studied for decades, and the newly Reborn. It is one of five institutions of its kind in the world. Many people compete to teach there, to work at The Meridian Group, to become acolytes, and in the end to become Sekh. The hope of Rebirth The Zingan aspiration is Rebirth: becoming a Sekh. The community speaks of it openly, and the Sekh regard it with mixed feelings. Not every practitioner fully believes in it. It is nearer to sainthood or nirvana than to a promotion. A human who goes through Rebirth does not come back, because something else returns. Contact with family is usually cut, because the bloodlust that follows makes proximity dangerous. Those chosen receive a funeral on the scale of a saint’s canonisation, with celebration and mourning together, and families may later make offerings to them. The Sekh do not encourage the hope and do not forbid it. Only a Sekh at least a hundred years past their own Rebirth may Initiate, and there are only about 100 to 150 Sekh in the world. Most Zingans never act on it. A very few do. See Rebirth and the Four Trials . The Anu-side parallel The human devotees of ’Anpésùmün as a faith group, the Shùkí’Apésùmù or Shùkapémù, stand to the Anu as the Zingans do to the Sekh. The Order of Shadows is their organised order. See Packs, orders and places . Placeholder Open questions Older notes describe matrilineal Houses of Flame, with Flamemothers as high priestesses, queer-affirming roles such as the Ash Rite, and titles such as Voice of the Ember, Shield of ’Èn’zíngámün and Hand of the Ash. Whether any of it survives as Zingan or Red Choir structure has not been decided. The House of Ember is already called strongly matrilineal Open Whether the Anu-side faith group needs an English name, as the Zingans have Open

In the early years of Ishphaeno, during the war, four women carried trial pregnancies in an attempt to make better creations than humans. Each gave birth to a different people. Decided Brood Original number Mother Today Lamiae 8 Hashaeqa See the Lamiae pages. Veskari 4, quadruplets Zaelith or Pholaeth Open Their numbers have fallen and the decline is certain. Shavari 2, a sister and a brother Naevoshi , her first children They were unable to have children. The Shavari are the only brood unable to reproduce. Decided Veskari Veskari in four colourings, standing and climbing. Concept image. Serpentine and omnivorous. They have long bodies, flexible spines, powerful joints and limbs, and skulls a little wider and longer than a human’s. Their hands and feet are broad and strong, with gripping pads that let them climb sideways and upside down. A crocodile-like tail grows from the tailbone. The sister was said to lean masculine and the brother feminine. Vatraxu personal names are usually gender-neutral, though some pick up gendered associations in time. Skin Said to have been ashen purple with pale blue and white star-like flecks. Eyes Silver sclera, gold irises and black segmented pupils like a gecko’s, with several pinholes. Features Nubian features, a large black 4A afro and slightly sharpened ears. Horns Short, straight and upright, like antennae, above the forehead and brows. Wings and tail Golden gossamer wings and a thin, wispy black tail that was very expressive. Body Fine cat-like fuzz across the midriff and hips, calloused hands and feet with strong nails, full chests and sculpted hips within a graceful frame. Flight. Legends say the Shavari could fly faster than sound, and could make themselves silent whenever they wished. Those who claimed to have seen one in the sky said they heard nothing until it was gone. Decided Masquerade. A Shavari body was said to flow between forms. They could imitate another body’s look and proportions without gaining its powers, and they would often default to copying each other. They were said to talk without words, through shifts of features, posture, expression and colour. This was not telepathy. Decided Borrowed power. Eating another species was said to give a weaker, temporary copy of that being’s inborn supernatural abilities. How strong it was and how long it lasted depended on the one eaten. The store faded with both time and use, with no fixed timer. They remembered an appearance after the borrowed power ran out. They needed human flesh and were choosy eaters. Decided The twin bond. Distance was said to dull their power only a little, but apart, deliberate shifting was harder, and one twin could stay stuck in a form far longer than was natural. Hurting one troubled the other and might upset the shape or stability of either, even side by side. They were trained in restraint, discretion, a steady public identity and guarding each other. They fought with honour in the Krang Uthjook. Decided Kharuvi Kharuvi in four colourings, with wings spread. Concept image. A Kharuvi, wings folded. Concept image. Smaller, slighter, light-boned fliers that eat carrion. Wing surfaces are joined to the arms and unfold like an accordion, as pleated membranes mixed with feather-like structures. The arms help in flapping, and the legs fold to cut drag. Face Stubbier, with sharper mouths and small pointed teeth. Hands and feet Strong grasping, tearing toes and claws, which they sharpen like a cat. Skin Mahogany to ash-white, for camouflage. Eyes Yellowish sclera, brown to nearly black irises and round pupils. Build Females are generally larger and more aggressive. Attack They strike in flight or step forward, cock the head to one side and let out an incapacitating screech. Weakness Sensitive to heat. The East gate sign over Haelvatael, the Two Brothers , first stood for the Shavari. As the memory of who the pair were faded, the name shifted to the Two Brothers. x: Home / Ishphaeno / Materials and Craft / Clothing and Regalia Clothing and Regalia Ishphaeno dresses by draping, not tailoring. Rank is worn, and anyone at court can read it at a glance. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Ishphaeno garments and material culture reference. Materials are explained on Materials and Craft . Draping philosophy The court aesthetic is not medieval Europe with demons. It blends West African, Indian, Japanese and Greco-Roman drapery, filtered through an immortal civilisation. Tailoring exists, but draping is the highest art. The silhouette. The basic wardrobe is long wrapped tunics, layered robes, split skirts, wrapped trousers, sashes, shoulder drapes, sleeveless outer coats and shawls. Everything moves, and even soldiers wear garments that billow when they walk. No gendered clothing. Dress divides by profession, climate, rank and personality. A broad-shouldered blacksmith and a dancer may wear nearly the same base garment, differing in fabric, chest wrapping, sleeve length, jewellery, colour and hairstyle. Chest manes. Heavy collars are avoided. The three eldest princes have ascot-like chest manes, so necklines are built to frame them with open V-necks, deep wrap fronts, asymmetric robes and crossed lapels. Jewellery. Status sits at the face and limbs, not the throat: circlets, forehead chains, ear cuffs, multiple earrings, arm cuffs, stacked bracelets, anklets and elaborate belts. Footwear. Not boots by default. Wrapped sandals, leather slippers, soft boots, split-toe shoes and high platform ceremonial shoes. Ports run barefoot surprisingly often. Hooved and draconic-legged princes wear different footwear from their humanoid-footed brothers. Capes become shoulder drapes. The diagonal drape crosses the body from one shoulder to the opposite hip, and it is the form that clears a working wing pair. The vertical drop is a shorter length falling straight down one side. It is open to any prince without functional flight wings. The rank wraps Rank is worn through a single-cloth wrapping technique that scales in pleat count and difficulty. The garment never changes: one continuous length of cloth, wrapped and pleated, never cut into separate pieces. What changes is how many pleats the wearer can execute and how fine a cloth they can do it in. Rank Pleats Style Cloth TeMize 1 (single pass, single tuck) Solthrael Kelnithsol, plain-grade Kelnith weave Kharu 3 Nathrael Vranethiq, a finer Kelnith and Qalthiq blend Veshael 6 Qethravael Zenthiq, a fine weave and the ceiling of pure wrap skill Lamqa 8 Lamqavael Full Luthaevel Jamija 12 to 14, styled tight to read as endless Xashvael Individual, always sealed with sovoq rather than tucked TeMize through Veshael is pure technique. A single pass takes 3 to 4 yards, and a Veshael’s six pleats take up to 6 or 7 yards, each pleat about four fingers wide, gathered and tucked left of centre in the same method as a Nivi-style drape, then carried over one shoulder as a trailing panel. Heavier, finer fabric is harder to pleat evenly, not easier, so a Veshael’s Zenthiq is years of craft. Lamqavael, the Prince’s Wrap The same technique as Qethravael, one full skill tier higher. Eight pleats, each held taut and precise, and the count itself carries meaning: eight pleats for eight princes. It is cut from full Luthaevel, so the cloth shifts with the Toluqavel overhead before anything else goes on. A sash at the waist and a shoulder drape are standard daily dress with it. Neither is counted. The outer coat, the circlet and footwear are separate ceremonial and regalia categories. A prince in the wrap, sash and drape alone is not underdressed, and the outer coat works more like a smoking jacket than a base garment. Xashvael, the Jamija Wrap The mechanic changes at this tier. Twelve to fourteen passes of cloth are pulled taut so the fabric compresses around the body instead of falling open in pleats, closer to gift-wrap tension than to a sari. It is closed by small sovoq pins, one at each pass, and one load-bearing key pin sits at the collarbone or breastbone. Pull that pin and every pass sealed after it comes free at once. Each of the four Jamija handles the key pin differently: worn openly among a cascade of chainwork, hidden among a matched pair of decorative points, kept modular with extra release points at shoulder, hip and forearm, or replaced by a small engineered interlocking mechanism. The wider Jamira nobility wear a deliberately looser version of the same silhouette, with slack pleats and gaps where skin shows by design, and an ordinary clasp instead of a key pin. The Jamija’s tightness says I am sealed and you have not earned the seam . A lesser succubus’s looseness says I choose what you see . Both are control, in opposite directions. Regalia Raqelath, the royal ring The ring is named for Raqal, heart-stone, which is also a real gemstone of the same family as Xathqal and Sobraeqal. Raw, uncut Raqal is dull until it touches blood. It then absorbs a portion of what touches it and glows ruby, deeper the stronger the blood. A human barely tints it, a Vatrajaxo shifts it further, and a Vatrajaxu saturates it to a near-blinding depth. Anyone who knows the stone can read a wearer’s vitality from how the ring glows. Raw deposits lie in and beneath boulders along the boundary between Pharuhona and TeDrona, an uncomfortable stretch to mine, which keeps the raw stone rare however common finished rings appear at court. When a ring is given, in the ceremony of recognition that means you are one of us , the recipient’s blood is pressed into the raw stone before final setting. That keys the glow to them. A bonded ring cannot be worn meaningfully by anyone else, so a forged or stolen inheritance claim is detectable. Sadok, Lioshe, all eight Lamqa, the Jamija and any future prince or princess wear one. A folk rumour says a Raqelath is forged from a piece of someone’s heart-stone. It is not quite right, but it is not nothing either. Shaelith, the circlet Named for Shaelruq and Shaelrukan. The ring marks family, and the circlet marks office. It is worn only by those who hold one of Ishphaeno’s great governing seats. Both are polished sovoq, the same steel that arms the kingdom. No one wears a heavy European crown, because the circlet is designed around the wearer’s anatomy. Circlets and footwear are never counted in a wearer’s pleat rank. Sadok. The nine-headed fan is the Navaxushe, his heraldic beast. Concept image. Lioshe. Beadwork in metal, drawing on Benin coral crowns and the regalia of Queen Nzinga. Concept image. Mephithoveles. Concept image. Belzevuv. The loops stand for hunger. Concept image. Zamodes. One strip of chainlink, with the short tassels cast as solid metal. Concept image. Belishael. The linked rings stand for connecting with others through dreams. Concept image. Mamon. The teardrop is a single stone of sky-blue hope sobi. Concept image. Lamjamon. Concept image. Dagan. Concept image. Zarazael. Concept image. The circlet slides on from the front like a headband and does not cradle the antlers or horns. Antlers and horns are left clear. The older generation’s circlets close with a clasp. The younger five hold by tension. The Jamija wear forehead veils, layered brow chains and temple ornaments in worked sovoq instead. The eight princes, standard attire Prince Wrap and cloth Drape Notes Mephithoveles Eight-fold wrap in deep Luthaevel, with a tight, high front that suits his compact mane. Diagonal, out of necessity, in sheer Sobraevit wing-fabric. Sash and trim in worked sovoq thread. Outer coat in silver-grey to near-black Kelnith-Luthaevel blend. Minimal leather slippers. Belzevuv Generous, voluminous eight-fold wrap with a deep wrap front in warm Mresovel, framing the fullest mane. Diagonal by choice, in iridescent Mresorak scale-work, out of pride in his wing scars. Outer coat in buttery Ruqorith leather. Often barefoot at the ports. His scarification stays visible through every layer. Zamodes Eight-fold wrap cut to expose his V-shaped mane, front and back, in Sobraevael-trimmed Mresovel or fine Luthaevel. Diagonal, out of necessity, clearing his single leathered wing pair. Jewellery-forward, with stacked arm cuffs and ear cuffs. His arm-sleeve tattoo stays uncovered. Wrapped sandals, with high platform versions for court. Mamon Eight-fold wrap in Qalthiq and Kelnith, buried under Vorunith feather trim and Sobraevael living jewellery. Vertical drop. Crystal inlay on the outer coat. Lower garments are wrapped with give below the knee. Clawed sandals with feathers in the straps. Lamjamon Eight-fold wrap in thick battle-treated Ruqorith leather, the most martial rendering of the wrap. Vertical drop, for a lower profile in combat. Xathelun fur trim on ceremonial pieces. Qorazil quills in his sash, tuned to chime. Dagan Eight-fold wrap in dark Mresovel, cut close, built for concealment. Vertical drop, dark and barely visible. No Qorazil quill anywhere. Footwear and leg wraps built for land and water. Belishael Eight-fold wrap that looks accidental, in soft Kelnith and Mresovel in warm neutrals. Vertical drop, worn loose. A Miravun shell-plate shawl, worn loose. Hooved feet go bare or wrapped. The hardest look in the dynasty to build correctly. Zarazael A deliberately simple eight-fold wrap under an extravagant layer of Sobraevael living jewellery and Mresorak scale-work. Diagonal, purely for theatre, in the sheerest Sobraevit wing-fabric. The highest platform shoes in the dynasty. These are the descriptions as written for the garments reference. The princes’ other details are not published here. This section follows the Ishphaeno Governance Compendium and the Aempaera references. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Gate Naethvatael (Naethva), North quarter. Decided Species Vatrajaxo. See The Vatrajaxo . Character Ambitious, sensual, possessive, proud and willful. The first Jami and the symbolic matriarch of the four. She oversees Ishphaeno as a de facto queen by the weight of her place in society. It is social and political capital, not a formal title. Sons Mephithoveles, Belzevuv and Zamodes, the three eldest of the eight princes. She is also the mother of the first Lamiae. See The Lamiae . She needs the confidence to let it be seen and to trust that most will not dare touch it. See Clothing and Regalia . Elsewhere She is also called the nominal ruler of the Lamiae and the Sire of every Sireline. See The Lamiae . Their title is Jami. Decided Who Four women: Hashaeqa, Naevoshi, Pholaeth and Zaelith. They are the original mates of Sadok , who never wed any of them. After his imprisonment all four were married to Lioshe . Decided Species Vatrajaxo, counted as the first of them. They were human women, each transformed after giving birth, so they neither fell nor were born to the fallen. See The Vatrajaxo . Decided Role Gate wardens and regional administrators. They are not commanders over the princes. Their authority runs parallel. Sons Hashaeqa bore Mephithoveles, Belzevuv and Zamodes. Naevoshi bore Mamon and Zarazael, Pholaeth bore Lamjamon and Dagan, and Zaelith bore Belishael. See The Lamqaxath Monja . Descendants The Jamira, the succubi of Ishphaeno, descend from them. The Vashaanil, the incubi, arose later. Dress The Xashvael, a wrap of twelve to fourteen passes sealed with sovoq. See Clothing and Regalia . The four Jami Gate Quarter Hashaeqa Naethvatael (Naethva) North Naevoshi Haelvatael (Haelva) East Pholaeth Taepvatael (Taepva) South Zaelith Jaeshvatael (Jaeshva) West Each gate is held by one of the four and their estates sit near their gates. See Places and Powers . Decided How they live The princes were raised collectively and each Jami held authority over every child. The four are not rivals. Their relationship is dry camaraderie: practicality, ancient familiarity, institutional trust, blunt honesty, mutual competence and shared trauma. Love between them is measured by endurance, not tenderness. Decided Every child born to the Jamija after the first eight sons has been a daughter. Those daughters are the first of the Jamira. x: Home / Ishphaeno / Peoples of Ishphaeno / Lioshe Lioshe The Morning Crown. He governs a kingdom he did not found and has come to love. This section follows the Ishphaeno Governance Compendium and the Aempaera references. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Names are given in Vatraxu unless a Vatrahu form is named. It is written to be read before the books, so some family detail is left out on purpose. At a glance Names Lioshe after the Fall, Haelael before it. Lioshe Maethluq in full. Scholars of the Abrama tradition know the same figure as Helel. Decided Family The younger brother of Sadok and the identical twin of Mikael. The eight princes are his nephews. Decided Title Maethlukan, “Morning Crown.” There is only ever one Lioshe. Decided Before the Fall Theraapaev, a general of the Holy Princes with wrist wings. He and Sadok led the opposition to Jangshe’s order. Species Vatrajaxu. See The Vatrajaxu . Seat Xathqaelsel, which is both the capital and its palace, on the Xathhona obsidian plains. Role Steward, not sovereign. He keeps Sadok’s institutions until the Twilight Crown returns. Marriage Married to the four Jamija after Sadok’s imprisonment. Decided The steward Lioshe holds nominal legal authority over the whole of Ishphaeno and sets the kingdom’s laws. His authority is real but loosely exercised outside the capital. How closely each prince follows the law inside their own territory is left to that prince’s discretion, much as a provincial governor decides how a central statute is enforced. All eight princes keep rooms and staff in Xathqaelsel and most of them grew up there. It is the place where they are legible under court observation. Their own territories are where they go to escape it. Decided In public Lioshe is devoted to restoring his brother. In practice he neither obstructs that goal nor advances it, having grown deeply attached over the millennia to the kingdom he keeps. Decided How he is known To most of Ishphaeno’s citizens Lioshe is the only ruler they have known. His name is on every decree, he is rarely seen, and loyalty to him is more habit than love. Decided The Jamija treat him as king in public. After Sadok’s imprisonment all four were married to him, since Sadok had never wed any of them. Decided See The Jamija . Haelael on Earth Before the war Haelael was a general of Aempaera, and gate-travel carried him to Earth. He was drawn by the flare of a gate opening over new life in an alien ley field, where three Hvaena had fled to after the Ambush: Staenhild, Nosmaera and Hjordin. He stayed among them and fathered the children who became the proto-Rejfê. Decided See Rejfê and the timeline . He was tender with them, and the survivors’ lives were tangled with his. After the Fall that ended. He became Lioshe, stopped visiting, and his children never knew him as a father. They inherited a resonance they could not name. Decided The bargain with Skandaer After the Fall the Gate-Maker Skandaer bargained with Lioshe. Lioshe swore two things for the safety of the survivors on Earth: to keep the Vorfae hidden, and to stay a presence on Earth who answers when they call for help. In return Skandaer helped shape the gate system of Ishphaeno and taught gate-craft to both brothers. Decided Sadok built the gates of Ishphaeno with that craft and founded Xathqaelsel on the ground where he fought Qavasha, the last known Navaxushe . Lioshe worked beside him, and the two are said to have made it together. Decided The gates are containment, not a gift. They are strong enough to work and restricted enough not to spill past a bounded depth, so that Ishphaeno stays a caged network and not a cosmic infection. The skill passed to the princes as a birthright. Decided See The Vorfae for Skandaer. The oath and the oathtree Scholars say the oath was sealed in living wood. Skandaer gave a tooth, and Lioshe wound a lock of his hair around it. The tooth was set in the ground. Then the two stood over it with their forearms crossed and their fists raised, and squeezed their cut palms until the blood of each fell upon the same spot. Sadok and two leaders of the Vorfae of that time are said to have stood witness. Decided A tree is said to have risen there, in the forests near Hjamblynd. It is called Ndajihvane in the old tongue, the oathtree. It is said to thrive while the oath is kept and to wilt as it fails. It does not hold the gates. The bargain does, and if the bargain fails the gates loosen, the people of Ishphaeno may slip through unchecked, and the bounded depth of the containment gives way. The Lyndfe who remained on Earth are said to tend the tree and to tell the tale of those who guard the world against a great calamity. Decided For a time Lioshe answered the Vorfae when they called. When he could not answer directly a few times, they stopped calling. Decided Lioshe stopped visiting his children after the Fall. Some read that silence as part of the oath’s cost, since showing himself too often would have exposed the people he swore to hide. Others say he simply let them go, and that in time they forgot him. Open After the Fall Lioshe’s Fall followed the chart for his rank, Theraapaev. His wrist wings became antlers, his ankle wings became his two tails, and his back wings blackened, like Sadok’s. Decided One tail is thinner and whiplike, forked with three gripping fingers, and the other is simply forked. The antlers in his regalia are covered on Clothing and Regalia , where the circlet is built around them. By the same chart his eye wings would have become a second pair of eyes. Proposed Open questions Whether the oath can be called lapsed now that the calls have stopped, and what the oathtree shows of it Open Whether he has a second pair of eyes, as the chart for his rank would give him Open

Decided Prince Sin Mother Dabit Mephithoveles Pride Hashaeqa Rides inside the terms of an agreement and passes to those who sign, spreading an inability to back down or admit fault. Belzevuv Gluttony Hashaeqa Marks a target to be hunted and devoured, permanently trackable. He can also make a person feel a portion of his own hunger. Zamodes Lust Hashaeqa Matched marks on two people draw them together. An unmatched mark draws the longing to him. Mamon Greed Naevoshi Spreads an acquisitive compulsion. He can set the thing wanted. Lamjamon Wrath Pholaeth Spreads ungovernable rage, which he then steers mostly through psychological pressure. Dagan Envy Pholaeth Spreads fixation and obsession, with the object steered mostly by ordinary manipulation. Belishael Sloth Zaelith Spreads sleep and dreams. He can steer the dream or nightmare directly and use it to move the sleeper. Zarazael Vanity Naevoshi Spreads devotion. Once a person is devoted he can simply ask and be obeyed. Veshael (many: Veshaelja) Heads of the great houses Each house holds a function of government, such as salt, records, ceremony or fashion, and serves a prince. Kharu (many: Kharuja) Governors of an estate, district, valley, island or township Hereditary. Succession needs the Veshael’s confirmation and, ultimately, the Lamqa’s. x: Home / Ishphaeno / Materials and Craft / Instruments and Music Instruments and Music Ishphaeno makes music from what it already has: skulls, wing-bone, living crystal and a wetland flower that happens to be shaped like a horn. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Ishphaeno musical instruments and ensembles reference. Materials are explained on Materials and Craft . Skull drums and percussion Instrument Kind Description Mresotharu Skull-banjo A polished Mresorak head carapace as the body, sometimes back-stretched with thin Mresovel. One eye socket holds a single drone string and the other is a grip. Three melody strings run between the mandibles, which double as the bridge. Folk versions use twisted Kelnith cord, court versions use Luthorun silk-thread, and a strange high-end version uses living Sobraevael tendrils that keep growing, so it needs retuning from growth, not wear. Humble and borderland-coded, the music of the Mresibooshle folk. Ruqorathum Bass drum A hollowed Ruqorith skull with a Ruqorith-hide membrane. Deep and communal, the standard harvest-festival drum and the working drum of Ruqoravael. Vulqorathum War drum The same build on a Vulqorith mount skull, taken only from an animal that died of old age, since these are bred and bonded, not hunted. Enormous and deep, played before battle in Lamjamon’s territory. Dronathum Hunter’s drum A rarer, sharper-toned drum from a wild Droneth skull. Higher and more piercing than herd-stock drums. Owning one is a hunter’s trophy. Qorashil Quill tambourine A Ruqorith horn or hide-wrapped wood hoop strung with paired Qorazil quills in place of metal zils. Makers select and position quills by pitch, so the tone is craft-tunable. A thin Mresovel or hide head turns it into a frame-drum hybrid. Strings Instrument Kind Description Sobrathel Living-string instrument Sobraevael tendrils across a Qalthorut-wood frame. Because the tendrils keep faintly growing, pitch drifts during one session, and mastery means chasing a string that will not hold still. Vorunathel Harp Strung across a Vorunith wing-bone frame with the feathers left on. They vibrate in sympathy with the plucked strings and add a soft shimmering overtone. Zelnithuk Panpipes Bound from hollow shed limb casings of molted Zelnith and lashed with Kelnith cord. The cheapest, most universal folk instrument, because the material is a byproduct of an industry already running at bread-production scale. Vibrants Instrument Kind Description Sobraevrin Crystal chimes Tuned Sobraeqal shards struck like chimes. Each strike gives a faint glow, and during a Toluqavel display the chimes pulse roughly in sync with the aurora. Rare, sourced from TeDrona, almost always ceremonial. Sovoxel Gong or bars Forged, tuned sovoq. A deep, martial, carrying tone and Lamjamon’s court instrument of choice. The same pattern used to open a ceremonial piece is legible across a garrison as an alarm. Vitharin Glass-tone bowed membrane Sobraevit wing membrane stretched over a small frame and played by bow, breath or fingertip friction. An eerie, glassy, near-continuous tone like a bowed water-glass, associated with Belishael’s dream and astral ceremonies. Zelivrithum Light drum A drumhead embedded with cultured strips of bioluminescent Zelivrrutes eel tissue, flashing faintly with each strike. Visible underwater or in cave darkness, so it doubles as a signal drum. Winds Instrument Kind Description Ruqorivel Bone flute Carved from Ruqorith long-bone. Cheap and common, and the first instrument most Ishphaenan children learn. Xathelothivel Deep bone flute Carved from Xathelun bone. Lower and breathier than the common flute, and owning one carries a hunter’s prestige. Sobraevoi Crystal horn Hollow, naturally tubular Sobraeqal played like a horn. The warmth of breath makes it faintly glow while sounding. Rare and ceremonial. Voruniveth Transverse flute Vorunith wing-bone, naturally hollow and light, with several finger holes for real melodic range. Feather fringe at the mouth end adds a breathy shimmer. Zelnithera Reed pipes Short hollow segments of molted Zelnith casing, lashed in graduated lengths. A double-reed buzzing tone, and the cheapest wind instrument in Ishphaeno. Xathvoreth Conch horn A conch-style horn from a large Xatheloru shell. Deep and carrying, and the traditional signal sounded from the docks of Qaeldreth and Qaelvaelvo for ship arrivals and departures. The brass family Vondrathovun grows in shallow water and riverbank mud along both the Malovrrutes and the Zelivrrutes. Its long flower bulb is already shaped like a horn bore and bell, narrow at the stem and flaring at peak bloom. Cut at peak bloom and dried, the fibrous walls stiffen to something like bark, hollow and resonant. Blown as harvested, it gives a deep, sustained, trombone-like tone with no shaping at all. Trimming the flared head and tightening the taper by hand before it hardens brightens the tone toward a trumpet. The two voices are finishing choices on the same bulb, and a skilled maker knows exactly how far to trim a given bulb to reach the tone a musician wants. The trombone is the plant’s default voice, and the trumpet is the one that takes craft, which inverts Earth’s usual brass hierarchy. The finished instrument is the Vondrathoreth . Krathovun is a tall, palm-like tree along the streams and pools at the foot of the West’s floating-island waterfalls, exactly where prey gathers. Fine fibres sensitive to motion run its height. When warm-blooded prey passes close, the crown whips violently and flings its hardened fruit with force. The fruit, Krathoq , is coconut-shaped but far denser, dense enough to crack bone, and it still stores water inside. Once prey is down, the roots sense blood in the soil, grow toward it and digest the remains from below. In dry periods the feeding roots recede to the taproot, so the danger zone reads like a flood line, wide in the wet season and narrow in the dry. The strike itself is dangerous in any season. A split and hollowed Krathoq shell becomes the Krathvreth , a mute cupped over a Vondrathoreth’s bell. It tightens the tone toward something nasal and urgent, with a slight buzz from the fibrous interior. One Vondrathoreth therefore has three registers: natural bulb, trimmed bulb, and either one muted. Ensembles Ensemble Occasion Make-up Vaetheluqavrin, the sky-bound ceremonial array The most formal court occasions at Xathqaelsel, and the most solemn seasonal moments. A tuned array of Sobraevrin chimes whose glow-and-ring responds to the aurora in patterned sequence, so the sky plays part of the piece. Trained musicians add Sovoxel strikes, the Vitharin drone and the drifting Sobrathel strings around that core. It works only under open sky, so the most solemn halls are open courtyards or have an oculus, closer to a Pantheon than an enclosed throne room. Indoors the crystals hold only a dim afterglow. No two performances are alike. Zelnithuvrek, the harvest ensemble Struck up the moment a Zelnith field finishes molting and the grain-flour harvest begins. Zelnithuk panpipes and Zelnithera reed pipes carry the melody, Qorashil drives rhythm and a Mresotharu holds a low drone, with the tempo climbing. Loud and deliberately imperfect, played by whoever grabs an instrument. Shaelovrin, the formal court ensemble The standing formal arrangement for any court occasion, joyous or ceremonial. Vorunathel and Voruniveth form the melodic core. Xathelothivel enters underneath as a countermelody. Sobraevoi punctuates entrances, toasts and declarations. Vitharin sustains a continuous drone beneath everything. Sovoxel anchors the rhythm and marks transitions. Vondrathoreth supplies the only brass voice. Three registers, three occasions. The Vaetheluqavrin is unpredictable and sky-dependent. The Zelnithuvrek is loud and harvest-triggered. The Shaelovrin sits between them as the dependable formal default. Open questions Scales, tunings and notation, which are not yet established. Open Songs, singing and voice culture on Ishphaeno. Only instruments and ensembles are recorded so far. The moons stop keeping their calendar, tides run wrong, and the wandering festival drifts out of recognition. This is the phase people witness. 4. Impact One day Kiruvyn and Kiravin collide. Most debris stays in orbit and gathers again. A fragment about 18 km across strikes Kanna at about 13 km/s, with about twice the energy of the Chicxulub impact on Earth. 5. Aftermath Decades to centuries and beyond Impact winter, a global firestorm worsened by 30% oxygen, extreme tides, centuries of meteors, and a visible debris ring that takes millions of years to clear. The impact is civilization-ending but survivable for sheltered and marine populations, which is exactly the survival pattern the peoples show. Canon The myth and the mechanism The Vorfae tell it as dying forests and a sickening sky. Kresyva felt it first, and sacrificed themself to hold Kanna steady long enough for the convoys to escape. The mechanical account says the same thing in numbers: the trees sickened because the ley field was draining, and Kresyva's sacrifice reads as the last surge of that field, spent to buy the Exodus time. The two accounts sit side by side rather than in tension. Canon More on the Vorfae page . Sidlosa, the moon that remains Sidlosa (also Khùm) formed from the merger. It has 0.38 Luna's mass, orbits at 313 Mm in 21.39 days, and looks about 0.38° across, visibly smaller than Kiruvyn once was. Its tides are steady and weaker, at 0.70 times Luna. Canon The calendar after The new sky holds 8.886 moon-months per year, not a whole number. The old year held exactly 12.00, and no adjustment can make the old calendar fit the new sky. The twelve-month moon calendar did not vanish. Every descendant culture still keeps it as the religious calendar, out of reverence for a sky none of them has ever seen, so they count twelve months while the moon above them keeps a different rhythm. Decided Civil life moved to a solar calendar: 8 months of 24 local days, a six-day week, four weeks to a month and 32 weeks to the year, with two months to each season. It follows the star, so the broken moons do not touch it. Decided The two meet every 48 days: three moon-months, two civil months and eight six-day weeks all end together at the turn of a season. Decided The tides broke too. Before, two moons gave an irregular combined range of 0.71 to 0.98 times Luna. Now one moon gives a steady 0.70. Every creature that timed its breeding to the two-moon beat lost its cue for good, a mass extinction in the intertidal zone separate from the impact. A hotter, burnier world The greenhouse rebound pushed the equatorial heat higher. The uninhabitable band now reaches about ±18°. With mature forest destroyed and replaced by fast post-fire growth in 30% oxygen, the fire season is more frequent and more severe than before, and has not fully recovered. Biome Latitude Character Burnt Belt 0 to 18° Steaming equatorial rainforest under permanent cloud. Lethal wet-bulb heat. Crossed by sea, never settled. Tropical coast and archipelago 5 to 25° The ocean makes coasts livable where interiors are not. Volcanic subtropics 18 to 28° Ash-fertile, hot, geothermally active, with the heaviest fire season. Subtropical desert 30 to 38° The true arid zone. Fire-edge savanna and woodland 26 to 40° Annual burns. Lignotuber plants dominate. Riverside corridor forest Any Fire refuges with the deepest surviving biodiversity. Warm temperate interior 38 to 55° Highland valleys and lower mountains. The prime habitable band. Temperate grove forest 32 to 46° Deep-soil forest that supports cultivated groves. Coastal margin and delta 30 to 50° Shifting tidal flats and reedlands, rich in fish. Subpolar highland 58 to 72° A growing season of only 60 to 70 local days and a long dark winter. Karst and lava-tube systems 25 to 45°, underground Thermally stable. The reason anything survived. Who survived Anything keyed to the two-moon tides is extinct, for reasons unrelated to the impact. Plants with underground storage organs and fire-cued seeds were already suited to what the Calamity produced, and now dominate. Riverside corridor species survived disproportionately. Expect relict species found nowhere else. Fast post-fire plants inherited a planet with no competition, and the modern landscape is still shaped by that head start. Color did not change. Hvan is still orange, so the biosphere is still dark red, bronze and purple-black. Still to decide Where the impact struck: which hemisphere, latitude, ocean or continent. Open

x: Home / Kanna / Peoples / Dorrwfø Dorrwfø A Dorrwfø of the Leopard clan. Concept image. Five sovereign clans on the southern continent, a seafaring, four-armed people with no crown to sign a treaty for them. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Land The southern continent, from 18 to 50°S Government Five fully separate clans. There is no paramount chief. Language Dorrwfø, with Icelandic-leaning conservative consonants. Script undocumented. Skin #351e10, a warm charcoal red-brown called Hickory. Clan markings run about two shades darker than the wearer's own base. Body Four arms, tusks, horizontal-slit pupils and clan markings on the skin Anatomy mix About 40% dual-set, 60% dimorphic and 3% intersex. The dual-set share fell to about 20% during the wars with the Rejfê and Kannafê. Decided Clothing Thai Lifespan 80 to 250 years, the shortest of the peoples, from constant conflict The five clans Clan Native territory Place Character Wave βongeheleð (Vhongeheledh) North coast, the Crossing Gate Sailors, navigators, raiders and long-distance traders. They control the maritime passage as a toll of risk, not a lock. Claw Salaɫiβo (Salalhivho) West, arid coast Cold-upwelling fisheries. Maritime despite a dry hinterland. Thunder Zaziɫiβo (Zazilhivho) East, monsoon coast Wetter, greener and heavily forested, with a storm regime. Fire ðavþɯr̥mˠote (Dhavthwrhmhote) The Dry Heart, central desert The outcast clan. Caravan and covert trade routes. See below. Leopard Kojisað (Kojisadh) The temperate south The coolest and most fertile land, the agricultural heartland, and home to the oldest major sacred tree. Enviable, not authoritative. No paramount chief Clans cooperate only through occasional treaties. There is no apex authority and no seat to inherit or contest, which is deliberately unlike the Rejfê rotating High King. Outsiders complain that the Dorrwfø sign treaties and then raid anyway, claiming it was a clan, not the crown. There is genuinely no crown. The charge of duplicity comes from misreading a political structure they do not understand. It also fits the chief-in-the-tree belief. A chief tied to one tree and buried at its roots is local by nature. You cannot rule five regions from inside a tree in one of them. The four old clans Wave, Claw, Thunder and Leopard are sacred hereditary dynasties. Each traces its authority to a founder who planted the clan's sacred tree. The ruling bloodline has drunk from that tree ever since, a real and compounding biological and magical advantage. Ruling children train from youth in combat, endurance, clan law, ritual duty, local survival skills and diplomacy. They are not decadent aristocrats. Ruling families hold regular friendly bouts. Each is training, a prestige contest, political theatre, matchmaking and a way to size up rivals. A defeat, injury or insult read as weakness can tip a bout into war, so sanctioned bouts need strict ritual rules, witnesses, stopping conditions and limits on killing or maiming heirs. Fire: exile, not settlement Every other clan has a story of migration. Fire has only a sentence. The Dry Heart was chosen as exile land because it was harsh and expected to kill or contain whoever was sent there. The founders were Dorrwfø rejected, suppressed or expelled by the other clans, and they survived long enough to plant a sacred tree. The first Fire chief took power by dominance, not lineage or election. Fire succession is hereditary continuity without hereditary security: the chief's child holds a privileged but insecure claim, and anyone may challenge. If the challenger wins, they live at the tree, gain its power, and found the next line. The tree belongs to the office, never permanently to one bloodline. Fire is more mobile than the other clans, but only for those who are strong, useful, clever, magical, ruthless or charismatic. Birth does not cap how high you can rise, but weakness gets little protection. For anyone who cannot prove their use, Fire can be harsher than the hereditary clans. Dorrwfø intersex people are mostly forced into Fire, and treated as a lower-class laborer caste everywhere else. Fire likely has the highest share of them. Decided The other clans publicly treat Fire as degraded or disposable, while privately relying on them for dangerous work they do not want attached to their own prestige. Many Fire members work in liminal trades: caravans, long-distance trade, black-market shops, smuggling, mercenary work, brokering and discreet go-between roles. The Dry Heart is not an empty wasteland but a covert network hub whose public reputation understates its real reach. The contrast to preserve: the four old clans prove legitimacy by lineage. Fire proves it by continued dominance. When a Fire challenger beats someone from an old founder dynasty, the insult is especially severe. Canon What binds them without governing them The universal rite. The temperate south is sacred to all five clans, because every clan began there. Young members of any clan may always travel there to hunt the Boskamyra in season, as a rite of passage that holds no matter who is at war with whom. Cooperation is real but always pairwise and conditional. Marriages and festivals are shared bilaterally with whichever clans are currently at peace. The crossing is a toll, not a lock. Other clans can sail further east or west to bypass Wave ships. It is simply more dangerous, and someone desperate enough will take the eastern route and may not come back. Crossing the Burnt Belt The Dorrwfø sail around or through the Belt and never live in it. They time voyages to the cooler hours and seasons, carry large freshwater reserves, build shaded ships for airflow, and hop between sea refuges. Their bodies help: the best eyesight in the family, ears adapted to the sea, and coarse body hair that reads wind, current and pressure. They are not immune to lethal wet-bulb heat. They are simply the people best equipped to attempt the one place where crossing is survivable at all. Canon Ancestor practice The chief lives in the sacred tree. Sap plus a few drops of blood make a ritual wine that is generally shared, while only the chief's own family eats the fruit. The chief is buried at the roots at death, which links the office to that ground and is another reason no Dorrwfø chief could rule paramount from elsewhere. Canon Clan markings Every Dorrwfø has melanistic skeletal patterning from birth, about two shades darker than their base skin. It follows the bones (jaw, collarbone, shoulder blades, spine, ribs and hips), flows like natural organic lines, and identifies the clan. Canon Clan Marking Leopard Dense freckling across the shoulders and up the neck and jaw. Spots rather than lines, the most animal reading, with visual weight on the upper body and face. Claw Jagged slash marks across the torso, arms and face. Angular and aggressive, most striking in combat. Wave Curling marks that follow horizontal body contours: ribs, hips and shoulders. Probably the strongest maritime identity. Fire A large chest mark narrowing upward in a curving flame to the neck, with wisps along the collarbone and shoulders like dissipating smoke. All the energy draws up to the throat. Thunder Jagged bands on the lower body and abdomen, with lightning mapped to the pelvis, thighs and lower ribs. All the weight sits low, powerful and grounded. Body Gestation 8 to 10 months Pupil Horizontal slit Iris Cool yellow or pale gold Ears Slightly adapted for sailing and swimming; they love being scratched by loved ones Tongue Longer, slightly flat, purple-black, rough Blood Burnt orange (vanadium-adjacent, maritime chemistry) Nose The flattest in the family Teeth Tusks Arms 4 (the second pair sits below the pectorals and has four fingers) Spine Flexible thoracic spine for swimming and rowing, reinforced lumbar for combat, wide thoracic vertebrae for the four-arm shoulder girdle Joints Human typical Strongest sense Sight (best in the family) Body hair Visible coarse hair that senses wind, current and pressure Build (masc) Linebacker Build (femme) Tailback or halfback Height 5'9" to 6'10" Height by sex Masc 1 to 4 inches taller than femme Skin tone #351e10 (Hickory) base, warm charcoal red-brown Markings Melanistic skeletal patterning from birth that identifies the clan Lifespan 80 to 250 Active period Maritime rhythms set by tide and weather How the land was held The Dorrwfø once held a far broader share of Kanna before Rejfê and Kannafê systems pushed them south. A possible older map: Leopard held most of the southern continent, Wave once held what is now Ostirynd and Hestirynd, Thunder lived along the Havdèl coast, and Claw lived along the western Rejfê coast. Fire formed later as an exile population and was never an original clan. Proposed Still to decide Whether Fire's real power is respected, feared or flatly denied by the other four clans. x: Home / Kanna / Peoples / Kannafê Kannafê A Kannafê in ceremonial dress. Concept image. Four sovereign grove polities on the eastern continent. They are the Lyndfe who went back, and the clearest living form of Grombaer's teaching. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Land The eastern grove continent, a living forest of groves Government Four separate sovereign states, not one country Language Kannafên, the Kanna dialect of the Lyndfe language Skin #4c3228 to #7f6050 Clothing A modified Toghu, the Bamileke royal velvet tradition from Cameroon Age-bands Fewer than the Vorfae, with longer gaps between them Grove culture The grove is the community center, and caring for it is worship. Fruit is shared by everyone. The mèla (soul) is understood to circulate through the grove cycle, the clearest surviving form of Grombaer's original teaching of any people. Canon The four polities They form one broad ecological and cultural zone, set apart mainly by water. Their political habits follow from their ecology, not the other way round. Canon Polity Place Character Nyrstirynd North. The coolest and wettest, with deep riverside corridors and the oldest, slowest-growing groves. Preservationist. A grove that takes centuries to replace makes a people conservative: they truly cannot afford a mistake. Vastirynd West and interior. Harbors and major river mouths. Pragmatic and open to trade, because ships have somewhere to arrive. Will deal with the Rejfê where it pays. Ostirynd East and south. The largest southeastern territory, fire-edge forest next to hotter, drier land. Diplomatic out of necessity. Their groves burn, so they must negotiate for refuge, seed stock and grafting rights. Hestirynd South. A federation of volcanic islands with some mainland coast and fertile ash soils. Agrarian and humanitarian. The first landfall from the southern crossing, so they meet everyone who arrives half-dead from the sea. The most exposed of the four. Naming A full name follows this pattern: [Epithet name] by [Birther's name] uta [Home tree] vanje uta [Grove nation] . A name therefore says who you are, who bore you, which sacred tree you belong to, and which nation you come from. Canon Hajmblynd is the Kannafê Homegrove and means “home-grove” (hjam, home, plus lynd, grove). It is not the same grove as the Earth-side Hjamblynd, the Rejfên and Stamfaen form, founded near the Cameroon fault line. The Kannafê named their new Homegrove after the old one: the same word in two languages, with hj- becoming haj-, and a deliberate echo of the lost home.
