x: Home / Kanna / Peoples / Mylzhfã Mylzhfã A Mylzhfã in festival dress. Concept image. A sovereign people beneath a dry limestone plateau, safe because their land looks worthless. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Land A karst plateau at 25 to 45°N on the Rejfê continent, with caves, lava tubes and aquifers far larger than the surface footprint Government One sovereign polity, not part of any Rejfê tribe Language Mylzhfã, shaped by cave acoustics and Yoruba contact. Script undocumented. Skin #3d251e to #4c3228, the deepest in the family Clothing Georgian. The chokha coat (with cartridge rows adapted to grove and ancestor motifs) in the style of the Khevsureti and Mtiuleti mountain dancers: compact, explosive and knee-drop heavy. The karst sovereignty Above ground: arid limestone, a former seabed pushed up, near-treeless and full of sinkholes and cave mouths. It looks worthless to outsiders. Below ground: huge cave networks, lava tubes, aquifers, settlements, glowing ley-supported grove farms and sacred burial-farming chambers. The sovereign cave network is far larger than the surface footprint. The land defends itself. The desert above has scarce water, and a handful of cave mouths act as chokepoints. That is why they were never conquered. Rain falling on the plateau soaks down into the aquifers. They have water because the surface is dry, while anyone standing on top is dying of thirst. Why they are the most orthodox Underground there is no sunlight, no photosynthesis and no farming. For the Mylzhfã, Grombaer's rite was never symbolic. It was the food supply, the only closed loop available, and for centuries the burial cycle was literally dinner. Other peoples had fields and sun, so their rite could drift toward symbol. The Mylzhfã orthodoxy is not piety. It is what survives when a practice carries the load. It also explains why they hold the most complete Stamfaen records of any living people. Canon Body and build Short and compact, 4'8" to 5'8", with a rugby build, from generations of underground compression. Their large ears need real changes to headwear. They are the people most likely to develop the strongest toe flexibility, since climbing and working in the dark rewards it. Dual-set people are unusually common, about 60%. Gestation runs 20 to 22 months. x: Home / Kanna / Peoples Peoples Four peoples live on Kanna today. All of them descend from, or evolved alongside, the Vorfae. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. People Land Government Language Rejfê Northern supercontinent, four tribal territories Four allied tribes; the High King (Ran) seat rotates Rejfên, in the Skoentega script Kannafê Eastern grove continent Four sovereign grove polities Kannafên Mylzhfã Karst plateau and the caves beneath it, on the Rejfê continent One sovereign polity Mylzhfã, script undocumented Dorrwfø Southern continent Five sovereign clans, no paramount chief Dorrwfø, script undocumented How they relate The Vorfae are the ancestors. They were born on Kanna, left in the Exodus, and are no longer there. Both the Rejfê and the Lyndfe lines arose on Earth during the Exodus. At the Return, the Lyndfe who went back to Kanna became the Kannafê. The Mylzhfã and the Dorrwfø are not part of that split. They evolved independently on Kanna during the long absence, and are closer relatives of the Rejfê than of the Lyndfe. Think of it the way you would think of two human peoples: both descend from the Vorfae, and neither is a subset of the other. The Fjarafê, who stayed on Earth A Fjarafê on Earth today. Concept image. The Lyndfe and Rejfê who remained on Earth after the Return interbred with each other and with humans, and became the Fjarafê. They have dissolved into the general Earth population and hold no land on Kanna. They survive as the root of the fae myth, and as the ancestors of the Earth cultures that appear in the Earth section. Canon Their skin range is shared with the Lyndfe: #5b3e31 to #8b6c5c, the widest of any people. A single age-band is typical, because human interbreeding diluted the tradition. Compare their bodies See Biology compared for eyes, ears, blood, build and lifespan across all the peoples side by side. Naming The peoples' names carry an ê. In the daughter languages the Stamfaen “ae” reduces to ê, so Rejfê, Kannafê and Fjarafê each end in it. The Vorfae keep the full spelling. The Dorrwfø are Dorufê to outsiders, and the Mylzhfã are Muldfê.

Land The northern supercontinent, 18 to 72°N Government Four allied tribes. The High King (Ran) seat rotates among them. See Lioshe . After the Return, the four tribes carved out Kanna land together as allies who had fled and fought side by side, not as one ruling the others. Canon The four tribes Tribe Element and place Land Clothing inspiration Tavgrirejfê Earth. Centre, 38 to 55°N Warm temperate highland valleys, forested, with a major river system. The prime habitable band and the ruling seat. Ethiopian Havdèlrejfê Water. West coast, 30 to 50°N Coastal margins, tidal zones, deltas, reedlands and rich fisheries. Fulani, Ivorian, Beninese, Guinean Dhavgrirejfê Fire. South, 18 to 28°N Volcanic subtropics, ash-fertile. Borders the Burnt Belt with no buffer, so they face the worst fire season of the four. Basotho blanket tradition, with Mongolian and Sámi influence Savkalrejfê have a growing season of only 60 to 70 local days. That is the physical reason for their blood-accelerated grove practice: they cannot wait for slow natural fruiting, and the fruit's ley boost gives surplus warmth, a real survival edge at that latitude. Tavgrirejfê feel Kanna's baseline seasonal swing with no extra regional extreme, which is why their footwear is a single versatile design. Terrain there is forested ridges, lower mountains and river-cut valleys, clearly mountainous but nowhere near Savkalrejfê scale. Havdèlrejfê economy sits on exactly the biome that the post-Calamity tidal regularization left poorer but predictable. Footwear and clothing vary by tribe and climate, not uniformly across the people. Governance The High King (Ran) seat rotates among the four allied tribes instead of passing down one house, so no tribe rules the others. x: Home / Kanna / Peoples / The Vorfae The Vorfae The ancestral people of Kanna, born of the life-spirit and the tree-spirit, and the source of every culture on this page. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. Skin #3d251e to #5b3e31, a deep blue-black Before worlds: Hvaengur Before worlds there was Hvaengur. Not a god of nature but life itself: soil, breath, growth, decay and memory in matter. Hvaengur is not a person or a ruler, does not speak or judge, and allows. Four conscious emanations arose from it. Canon Emanation Domain Hvandaer, the Shepherd Guide and protector of living peoples, concerned with continuity, balance and survival. Loves Kanna's forests and seasons, but cannot create alone. Skandaer, the Gate-Maker Guardian of thresholds, paths and limits. Maker and regulator of the Skandaer Gates. Neutral and exacting. Grombaer, the Past-Grower Keeper of memory, decay, burial and transformation. Treats death as return, not ending. Fjarnzaer, the Sister-World A world-spirit of distance, exile and elsewhere. Later linked with Earth. Kresyva and the birth of the Vorfae Hvandaer loved Kanna but had no equal to share that love with. Hvaengur let a partner emerge from the trees themselves: Kresyva, the Tree-Mother, masculine in form but able to bear children, and an equal to Hvandaer, neither servant nor ruler. From their union came the Vorfae. Sex combinations at birth are fluid, and intersex births are common and sacred. They attune naturally to ley lines, can shape technology without cutting themselves off from nature, and are long-lived and cyclical rather than immortal. They spread across Kanna into communes, groves, cities and finally advanced societies. Grombaer's teaching The dead return to the soil. From their burial grow plants, the plants bear fruit, and eating the fruit returns memory, strength and belonging. This is the root of sacred groves, ancestor continuity and communal identity. Death is circulation, not loss. It is also literal: every death releases the ley a body carried back into the ambient flow, and every birth draws from it. That is why the rite appears in every surviving descendant people. Canon The Skandaer Gates As the Vorfae advanced, Skandaer revealed the Gates: passages between worlds, usable only when the twin moons align, dangerous and limited. They were meant for preservation, not conquest. The Hvaena, the most skilled among the Vorfae at willed-construct work, were trusted to attempt gate travel during the Calamity, since construct mastery was the qualifying skill for the role. Canon After the Fall Skandaer bargained with Lioshe and shaped the gates of Ishphaeno as contained architecture. The oath that sealed it, and the oathtree Ndajihvane, are on the Lioshe page . Decided Age-bands Age shows as band-like tattoo markings that begin at the wrists and climb. A thin ring forms every 10 years. Every 100 years a connecting mark ties the last ten rings together, a century bound. Canon Century-bind style Look Meaning Fits Vine-Spine A thin vine running upward, touching each of the ten rings Roots connecting seasons; memory braided Grove communities Knot-Seal A small knot at the outer forearm with stitches to each ring Oath completed; identity declared Courts, clans, hierarchy Gate-Strike A clean vertical line crossing the ten rings like a post through fence slats Crossing survived; century earned Travelers, scouts, way-folk The Kannafê keep fewer bands, with longer gaps between them. The Fjarafê usually grow a single band, because so much human interbreeding diluted it. Purer individuals can reach two to five. The Rejfê have none at all, the most ritually diluted of any descendant people. Ley and magic Every Vorfae-descended people can sense the ambient ley field to some degree. The strength of that sense sets a subconscious base tier of magic (frost, light, fortune, wind, trap): personal and temperament-driven, not assigned by tribe. A rarer elevated tier, willed constructs, belongs only to dual-set individuals in every descendant people. That matches a belief shared everywhere that having both reproductive sets is sacred. The system runs on conservation of energy. Nothing is created, only borrowed and returned. “Dual-set” means both reproductive sets are present. It describes anatomy only. Words like bisexual are kept for who someone is attracted to. Canon The Crisis and Kresyva's sacrifice Through dreams and omens Hvaengur warned Hvandaer, who warned the Vorfae. Skandaer opened paths, but not for everyone. To buy time, Kresyva sacrificed themself, holding Kanna steady long enough for the convoys to escape. Hvandaer and Grombaer stayed behind to preserve Kanna and prepare it for return. Kanna did not die. It slept, scarred. Canon The science behind it is on The Calamity . The core truth, and how they lived In the Vorfae's own words: life is not created once. It is guided, returned and allowed to continue. They carried that faith to Earth, into exile, and eventually back to Kanna. Kinship is a strong web. Cousins are treated like siblings, and marriage and mixing are fluid and not especially taboo in small communities or among elites. Death is an honor, and when population is low a necessity. The Vorfae live long and are not eager to die, so the honor is heavy, not casual. Still to decide Do the Mylzhfã or the Dorrwfø keep any form of the age-bands, or did it not survive their independent evolution? Two candidates exist: Staenvaern for a mined focus-talisman and Skvendaru for the discipline. Lock one, both, or leave the true name lost. That one fact colors the whole biosphere. Canon The star takes its name from Hvandaer, the Shepherd, the first of the four emanations. On Earth, the Nok-speaking people, the first descendants of the Vorfae there, gave it its name in their own tongue: Lòbárạmün. A hot world, not a temperate one Property Kanna Compared with Earth Mass 0.892 0.89 times Radius 0.935 0.94 times Surface gravity 10.02 m/s² 1.02 g Axial tilt 26° 23.4° Day 26.43 hours 1.10 times Year 211.45 days 0.579 times Mean surface temperature About 29°C 15°C Atmospheric oxygen 30% 21% Kanna sits only 0.025 AU outside the moist-greenhouse limit. It hugs the inner edge of its habitable zone rather than sitting comfortably in the middle. A bare rock at that distance would sit near −21°C. About 50°C of greenhouse warming lifts it to the mean, roughly 1.5 times Earth's, which fits 20 to 30 times Earth's carbon dioxide plus extra water vapor. Ley damping, the sky's stabilizer Kanna's ley field acts as a damping medium that keeps the moons' orbits from growing more eccentric. It is a magical amplification of real tidal damping, so no one has to change gravity. Ley is a finite reservoir that refills at a natural rate. The Vorfae were the most ley-active civilization the planet produced, through everyday construct-work and above all through opening and sustaining gates to other worlds. Over hundreds of thousands of years that drew the field below the level needed to hold the moons steady. The Vorfae destabilized their own sky through the ordinary running of a magical civilization that had no way to know what it was spending. The twin moons, before the Calamity Kiruvyn (Khùzú), Order Kiravin (Khùzí), Chaos Mass 0.20 Luna 0.18 Luna Distance 261 Mm 414 Mm, ranging 311 to 518 Mm Eccentricity About 0.01 0.25 Orbit 16.26 days (17.62 days phase to phase, exactly 16 local days) 32.5 days, in a 2:1 resonance In the sky 0.45° across, never changes 0.22° to 0.36°, swelling and shrinking 1.67 times each orbit Tides 0.64 times Luna, steady 0.07 times at its farthest, rising to 0.34 times at its nearest Kiravin visibly breathes across her cycle. Kiruvyn never changes. The theological split between Order and Chaos is not symbolic: it is what anyone can see by looking up. The pair are held in place by ley damping, not by geometry. Canon The calendar, before the Calamity A year was exactly 192 local days, in four seasons of 48 local days each. Canon The calendar belonged to the moon: 12 months of 16 days, each month one full Kiruvyn phase cycle, with no drift. Canon The week was four days, so each month held four weeks, each season twelve, and the year forty-eight. Decided Kiravin's cycle is 34.9 local days and deliberately does not divide the year. That produced a wandering ritual calendar running beside the fixed solar one. Canon Climate and seasons The tropics reach ±26° and the polar circles ±64°, so the polar regions are much larger than Earth's. At the poles day and night can each last up to 96 local days. Seasons turn about 1.7 times faster than Earth's. Latitude Zone Temperature range 0 to 18° Equatorial, the Burnt Belt +38 to +44°C 18 to 30° Tropical and transitional +33 to +40°C 30 to 38° Subtropical desert belt +28 to +38°C 38 to 55° Warm temperate, the prime habitable band +16 to +30°C 55 to 64° Cool temperate +4 to +20°C 64 to 90° Polar −17 to +6°C The Burnt Belt The Belt covers 0 to 18° in both hemispheres and touches inhabited land directly on each side. It is not a desert. Lethal wet-bulb heat needs humidity, so the equator is a steaming rainforest under a permanent cloud band. The true deserts sit at 30 to 38°, where dry air descends. Coasts and island chains stay passable because the ocean softens the heat. The continental interior does not. Fire as a season At 30% oxygen, fire catches in damp fuel and spreads almost unchecked. Above about 25% wildfire becomes near-continuous, and 35% is the usual ceiling before forests cannot survive at all. Fire is as regular and expected as winter, and every land ecosystem is built around surviving it. Canon The living world The biosphere is dark. With little blue light, photosynthesis broadens into red and infrared, so foliage runs deep red, bronze, maroon, rust and purple-black. A green plant would be a conspicuous oddity. Fire adaptation is mandatory: thick insulating bark, underground storage organs that resprout within days, seeds that need heat or smoke to wake, wet riverside refuges, and fast post-fire opportunists. Many plants carry two leaf forms. Small, thick, dark leaves handle the summer. Larger, thinner leaves catch the weak winter light. The same forest looks very different between seasons. The coasts follow two moons. Kiravin's changing distance made tides irregular, which allowed huge intertidal forests, salt-tolerant reedlands, and creatures that spawn only on rare deep-conjunction tides. Boskamyra: the armored cat, jaguar-sized with pangolin scales, living on the coastal jungle fringe. Once a trophy hunt, now the Dorrwfø rite of passage. Still to decide Ocean temperature gradients are not modeled yet. Cold upwelling in the west and warm poleward currents in the east are plausible. Open Ronaer, Skaedine and the Vrendar dust belt are undeveloped. Open The warm world at 0.8 to 0.9 AU, proposed as home of the hostile species that killed Vorfae gate-scouts, is not yet placed. Open

x: Home / Across the realms / Languages / Mouane Mouane A cipher daughter of French, with a Duala substrate, made by Black and Indigenous witch communities in the French colonial Americas. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. What it is Mouane was born in the French colonial Louisiana and Caribbean of the 18th and 19th centuries. The Black and Indigenous witch communities there needed a shared tongue that was not French, not Bantu and not any single heritage, something forged in the space where all of them met. Decided Its skeleton is French sound and spelling. Its substrate is Bantu, mainly Duala, a language of coastal Cameroon with its own long history of contact with French. Its cipher is the community’s own act of creation: a fixed set of changes to French that you can only apply correctly if you already know French. The name comes from the Duala word muna , “child” (plural bana ), respelled through French convention as Mouane . It names what its speakers are: children of more than one world. Regular derivation would give Mouna , but the name stays Mouane by decree of the community. It is the only word treated this way. Decided Two registers Register Also called Used for Character Mouane Fort Fort Formal, written and academic speech The full cipher and full French grammar. The prestige standard. Mouane Léger Léger Everyday speech, film and music Simpler tenses, Duala and French fused pronouns, no grammatical gender. The two are mutually intelligible. A Fort speaker always understands Léger. A Léger speaker can follow Fort but may not produce it correctly without formal study. The relationship echoes standard Canadian French and its spoken vernacular: the academy prescribes Fort, and Léger is what lives in the community. How the cipher works Every content word is derived from French in six steps. Proper nouns and Bantu-origin words skip the sound changes and keep their spelling. Step What happens 1 Classify the word. Content words follow their sound. Proper nouns and Bantu words follow their spelling. 2 Write down how it sounds: split any word with a tréma, resolve digraphs and vowel units, drop silent letters, apply the e caduc rule, and flag nasals. 3 Mark the nasal syllables as anchors. They never move. 4 Reverse the order of all the other syllables. 5 Shift the vowel of the new final syllable one step along its chain. 6 Write the result in French spelling. The four vowel chains Chain Sequence Main a, o, è, i, é, back to a Back rounded ou, oi, ui, œ, eu, back to ou Front rounded u, ey, ay, euy, back to u Y-glide yé, yèr, yèl, yeur, back to yé Open vowels (è, ê, ô) do not shift. A word with one syllable is augmented before ciphering: Fort adds the ending -é and Léger adds the prefix ma- . A word that is only a nasal anchor is left alone. Verbs are ciphered in the infinitive and then take ordinary French endings. The irregular verbs être, avoir, aller, faire, vouloir, pouvoir and savoir are protected. Decided Stress The shifted vowel of the last syllable carries the main stress, marked with an acute accent, and the original French stress stays as a weaker second stress. When the shift lands on a glide chain result, the accent goes on the first letter of the pair (ói, óu, óe), except ui , which takes it on the i (uí). Bonjour becomes bonjóir and bonsoir becomes bonsuír . When the last syllable is a nasal anchor, the shift lands on the last free syllable and the accent goes on that vowel, as in talmán for tellement. Decided A sample sentence Register Sentence French Je suis tellement ravi, j’ai créé une nouvelle langue avec le français. Fort Je suis talmán viró, j’ai ékrá une vèyní lang vèkó le fransè. Léger Ja suis talmán ravi, ja’i créé une vèyni lang vèka le fransè. In English: I am so happy, I made a new language with French. Léger pronouns English French Léger Duala source I je ja na you tu to o he, she, it il, elle ila, with no gender a we nous ndi di you (many) vous vlo lo they ils, elles ebá bá Fort keeps the French pronouns and the il and elle distinction. Léger dropped grammatical gender early, as real creoles did, and its one definite article is la , whose final -a matches the noun class markers of many Bantu languages. Decided Negation and questions Meaning Fort Léger not ne ... épo épo no more ne ... éplèy éplèy never ne ... mèzhó mèzhó nothing ne ... ryiná ryiná neither ... nor ne ... éné ... éné éné ... éné Fort keeps ne and wraps it around the ciphered word. Léger drops it. A question can be made by rising intonation alone in both registers. Fort marks a question with skè or with full French inversion, and Léger uses est-ce que or the particle bè , which comes from a Duala sentence-final particle. Decided Tenses Tense Fort Léger Present Ciphered stem with French endings The same, kept for practice Past with an auxiliary avoir or être, then the ciphered participle The same Imperfect French imperfect endings on the stem Drop the stem’s last vowel and add -èg Simple past Exists, as a mark of formal writing Does not exist Future French future endings on the stem aller then the ciphered infinitive Conditional French conditional endings The prefix nórè- Subjunctive que with the prefix nó- que with the prefix nó- The prefixes in nó- and nórè- come from the Duala particle nó , which marks hypothetical and aspect meaning. Decided Numbers Mouane counts with a mixture. The numbers one to ten are Duala. Seventy, eighty and ninety are Duala tens, which removes the French soixante-dix, quatre-vingt and quatre-vingt-dix. The numbers 17 to 19 join the Duala ten dôm to a French unit. Everything else is French: 11 to 16, 20 to 69, and 100 and above. Léger leaves the French numbers plain, and Fort ciphers them. Decided Number Duala Mouane spelling 1 ewɔ́ ewô 2 ɓébǎ béba 3 ɓélálo bélalo 4 ɓénɛ́j bénèy 5 ɓétánu bétanou 6 mutóɓá moutoba 7 sǎmbá samba 8 lɔmbi lômbi 9 dibuá diboua 10 ɗôm dôm 70 mǔsǎmbá mousamba 80 mǔlɔmbi moulômbi 90 mǔdibuá moudiboua French number Léger Fort douze (12) douze zédói treize (13) treize zétrè quatorze (14) quatorze torzó seize (16) seize zésè 17 dôm-sept dôm-tésè 18 dôm-huit dôm-téhóe 19 dôm-neuf dôm-féneu 40 quarante koránt 60 soixante suisánt Onze, quinze, vingt, trente, cinquante and cent have only a nasal or an open vowel to shift, so they are left as they are. The French “et un” is kept for 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 and 71, but not for 81 or 91. Examples: 22 is vingt-deux in Léger and vingt-édóu in Fort, 72 is mousamba-deux or mousamba-édóu, and 88 is moulômbi-huit or moulômbi-téhóe. Decided Duala words Duala English muto woman mome man muna child bana children byala words deba, madeba water veya fire mbua rain vei sun ngondé moon, also month bongo tree mbo dog sue fish enon bird deri to eat ñuri to drink yae to come en to see sengi to hear makoyo to sleep Bantu-origin words are spelled by their own letters, with these changes: mw becomes mou, ng becomes ngue, and nj becomes gni. Decided Real languages behind it Verlan, the French argot that reverses syllables, is the main inspiration for the cipher. Michif, the Métis mixed language of French and Cree, is the closest real parallel. The loss of grammatical gender follows what happened in Haitian Creole and Louisiana Creole. Camfranglais, the street speech of Cameroon, and the code languages of the Gullah Geechee are further parallels. The Duala forms come from published Duala word lists and grammars. Open questions Whether the sound of am, om before b, as in samba, lômbi and dôm, should read as nasal in French spelling. It is accepted for now. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. At a glance Property Detail Also called Witch-tongue Where it is used Every school of the Witches of Mephis. A text written in Selo is official, and a text only in a regional tongue may be a copy. Vocabulary Built on Latin seeds, reshaped to Selo sounds. Latin aqua , water, becomes kwa . Syllables Every syllable fits the pattern (C)(w or y)V(N), with an optional nasal closing it Tones Tonal. Tones are written as numerals or accent marks. Sounds Group Sounds Stops p, t, k. The voiced b, d and g appear between vowels. Affricate ch Fricatives f, s, z, sh Nasals m, n, and ng at the end of a syllable Liquids and glides l, r (a tap), w, y Vowels i, e, a, o, u, and a short ə in unstressed particles. There is no vowel length. Tone Tone does grammatical work in Selo. Elevating a noun to a formal register means giving it tone 1, so se¹ is “star” in the elevated register. Polite particles all carry tone 1, a neutral root such as lo³ , speak, carries tone 3, and commands in the examples carry tone 6. The full tone stack is not summarized here. Called Grahne by the Lyndfe and Grejns by the Rejfê. Earth branch Lyndfê̂n The Earth Lyndfe language. Script: Lifetega, the flowing leaf-hand. Earth dialect Sharafên The Fjarafê dialect. Conservative, and keeps the Lyndfê̂n ablaut chain unchanged. Kanna dialect Kannafên The Kannafê dialect. Shaped by Rejfê contact: hvane becomes vanje, and the ablaut diphthong shifts to øj. Kanna branch Rejfên The Kanna Rejfê language. Script: Skoentega, the runic gate-hand. Kanna, independent Mylzhfã The underground language, shaped by cave acoustics and Yoruba contact. Kanna, independent Dorrwfø The southern continent language, with Icelandic-leaning conservative consonants. Mylzhfã and Dorrwfø are not daughters of Stamfaen in the way Rejfên and Lyndfê̂n are. They evolved independently on Kanna during the long absence. Canon How well can speakers understand each other? At a glance Property Detail Names Urhmauuri in keyboard spelling and Uʁmaʉɾi in the formal spelling. The people call themselves Urhmauua. Outsiders say Urhmaiia. Word order Subject, object, verb Structure Agglutinative. Suffixes carry tense, case, aspect and politeness. Plurals Words do not change for number. Context shows it. Verbs No conjugation. Verbs keep one root and take only a politeness ending. Vowels Vowel harmony, matching vowels by backness, height and roundness Nouns Suffixes mark case, possession and location. Adjectives take the same cases. Script Urhtsorna, an abugida with a wave crown stroke. See Writing systems . Sounds There is no w, v or q. Syllables follow the shapes CV, VCV, CVV and V, and the only consonant allowed to close a syllable is rh. The language has two valid ways to write certain sounds: the formal spelling uses the real IPA symbol, and the keyboard spelling uses a simple stand-in such as rh for ʁ. Neither is more correct. The five politeness levels The ending of the main or final verb sets the level for the whole sentence. A speaker who opens in one level carries it to the end. Level Verb ending Used for Plain polite -o Standard address in most formal or polite situations Informal none Friends, peers and equals Intimate -e A mate or life partner only Respectful -i Someone of higher status or age Royal -u Those who hold royal titles only Pitch backs up the level. Plain and informal speech ends flat or gently falling, the intimate level lowers and softens, and ritual speech uses a slow, low fall. Do not confuse these levels with the six religious-name registers, which govern which name is used for the creator and not how politely someone is addressed. See Gods and faith . An example Level Sentence Meaning Plain polite Naʉa leruʁa maiteo anetao I like to walk on the shore. Respectful Naʉa leruʁa maitei anetai I like to walk on the shore. Informal Naʉa leruʁa maite aneta I like to walk on the shore. Word building The agent suffix -ii turns a thing or action into a person tied to it. Zoruii, a vent-brewer, comes from zoru, vent or pressure. Two near-synonyms can split by scope: Lera is the earth as a planet, a force or nature, while zekha is the earth as dirt and ground underfoot. More Time units are on Calendars . The people, castes and places are on Urhmaiia , and the older summary is on Language and time . Dialects The branch for dialects of Urhmauuri. Work in progress. in progress Open questions The Royal level has no recorded ending beyond -u in the glossary. Open

x: Home / Across the realms / Languages / Vatrahu and Vatraxu Vatrahu and Vatraxu Vatrahu is the language of Aempaera. Vatraxu is what it became among the fallen. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. The two languages Vatrahu is the speech of the Vatrajarə. Its name means the voice or language of trust ( vatra is trust or voice and -hu is language). Vatraxu grew from it in Ishphaeno, among the fallen and their children, and it is the working language of the Infernal realm. Names in the almanac are given in Vatrahu unless a Vatraxu form is named. How Vatraxu differs Feature Vatrahu Vatraxu Pharyngeal sounds ħ and ʕ Present Absent. They become x. Schwa Stays ə Becomes o The letter s Not allowed. Sh /ʃ/ is used instead. Allowed The letter v May begin, sit in or end a word Standard position rules Definite article O- Te- The sound w Absent. It becomes v. Absent Final r Not allowed. Names ending in r take a vowel, so Aethaar becomes Aethaari. The same Vatrajaħu in Vatrahu becomes Vatrajaxu in Vatraxu through these rules, and the ending ra is dropped in some Vatraxu forms. Mikael carries the title Uthaartraal, from uthjaar , leader, and traal , prince. See The Holy Princes . Mottos Whose Language Words Meaning The Ashraatraal Vatrahu Taal vatra lan We trust in him. Believers, as a prayer Vatrahu Taal vatra Jangshe We trust in Jangshe, or we believe in the One. The princes of Ishphaeno Vatraxu Veth kol taalun Bow before us! Vatra on its own is a bare verb meaning trust. Taal is the exclusive “we”, and lan is “him” as the object. Canon Pronouns in Vatraxu Person Subject Object Possessive I (excluding the listener) ta tan talu We (excluding, many) taal taalun taallu We (including, many) tuxaem tuxaemun tuxaemlu You (one) ra ran ralu He or she (animate) la lan lalu It (inanimate) ka kan kalu The object form adds -n after a vowel and -un after a consonant. The honorific prefix is sha-. Vatraxu also has dual forms. Canon Writing Both languages are written in Latin letters for now. See Writing systems . x: Home / Across the realms / Languages / Writing systems Writing systems How each language family is written, with the script details recorded so far. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Kanna reference documents. Tags mark anything less settled. At a glance Family Language Script Type Stamfaen Lyndfê̂n Lifetega, the leaf-hand Flowing Stamfaen Rejfên Skoentega, the gate-hand Runic Stamfaen Kannafên, Sharafên, Mylzhfã, Dorrwfø Written in Latin letters with plain-text conventions Romanized Nọk Nọk and its four dialects Standard script, with a Latin romanization Alphabet with accent marks Urhmauuri Urhmauuri Urhtsorna Abugida with a wave crown stroke Vatrajarə Vatrahu Latin romanization with IPA letters Romanized Vatrajarə Vatraxu Latin romanization Romanized Selo Selo Glyph script, helper syllabary and romanization Logo-syllabary Mouane Mouane Fort and Léger French orthography Romanized Stamfaen family Lyndfê̂n is written in Lifetega, the leaf-hand: a flowing script. Rejfên is written in Skoentega, the gate-hand: a runic script. Canon The other daughters have no script recorded yet, and are written in Latin letters with a plain-text spelling for typing and search. Open Plain-text spellings Language Conventions All è is a stressed /ɛ/. ê marks the ae to ê reduction in the daughters. Stamfaen always keeps the full ae. Mylzhfã sh = ṣ, rn = ṇ, rd = ḍ, rt = ṭ, gh = implosive g, bh = implosive b, yh = palatal fricative, lh = voiceless lateral, ll = dark l, zh = voiced postalveolar, hq = ħ. Dorrwfø w = ɯ, rr = uvular trill, rh = voiceless r at the end of a word, lh = voiceless lateral at the start of a word, lf = dark l at the end of a word, hh = pharyngeal ħ, hq = epiglottal ʕ, a plain apostrophe = glottal stop. Example images to be added. Placeholder Nọk Nọk is written in Latin letters with accents and under-dots. It has ten vowels, four diphthongs and seven letter pairs (kh, ch, ny, kw, zh, sh, ng). An accent changes a vowel’s quality, and a dot beneath shortens it. Each dialect adds its own letters: the Northern dialect adds nd, br, st and nk and uses c at the start of a word, the Western adds mbg, mb and l, and the Southern adds ts, tsh, nd, hw and mb. Details are on Nọk . The first formal writing system was devised long after the faith began, by a scholar who drew on Latin and Greek script and built something new to suit an agglutinative language. It was later simplified into the standard form that Sekh-funded schools teach today. Canon Example images to be added. Placeholder Urhmauuri: Urhtsorna Urhtsorna is the Urhmauuri writing system. The name is a sacred archaism: its rn cluster is a deliberate fossil from the oldest register of the language, so the word for writing sounds ancient. It is an abugida with a Kannada-influenced look. Decided Feature Detail Crown stroke Every consonant begins with a wave sweep that curls at the right end. The crown alone is a null vowel carrier. A bare crown reads as /a/, and a crown with a diacritic is a vowel-initial syllable. Stops An open oval body. The angle of the exit stroke tells p, b, t, d, k and g apart, and a mark on the exit stroke shows voicing. Uvulars (rh, kh) A downward teardrop, the sacred direction. Kh adds a horizontal strike through it. Fricatives (s, z, sh, h) An open crescent. S has a straight exit, sh a curved one, and h is the most open. Affricates A closed stop body with a curved fricative-style exit. Nasals A fully closed rounded loop, told apart by the direction of the tail. Laterals (l, lh) A forked, split body. Flap and trill (r, rr) A crown with a flutter hook for r, and a doubled zigzag for rr. Glide (y) The crown stroke alone, with no body. Glottal stop A single small mark with no crown. Clicks Angular geometric marks with no crown, used in the sacred Haulorai register only. Vowels None for /a/. A hook above the crown on the left for /i/, a dot above the crown on the right for /e/, a double hook below for /uu/, a circle below on the right for /o/, a hook below on the left for /u/, and a dash through the body for /ii/. Diphthongs The second vowel is written on a following crown carrier. Ceremonial marks A nasal overlay, and a whistle pitch mark for the Royal level only. Punctuation Full stop, comma, question mark, quotation marks, ellipsis and dash. The exclamation mark shows emotion, not a command, because a bare verb form already gives commands. Three registers Register What it is Shell, handwritten The full flowing forms, for everyday literacy. Stone, public The same letterforms carved more deliberately. There is no separate simplified alphabet. Coral growth, Urhtsorna Hausonai Stone forms act as an armature, and coral colonizes them under the guidance of an Urhmauuka’s Ruala. Vowels are encoded by color and by the direction of growth. Each manner of articulation shares one base shape, so a building can be marked by its dominant glyph family. Glyphs carved into young coral grow raised and weathered as the coral hardens. Proposed The number system, Urhzorna Urhzorna counts in base 28, the length of the lunar cycle, which is one laza . Its organizing unit is the baula , which is 28 squared, or 784. Decided Example images to be added. Placeholder Vatrahu and Vatraxu Both are written in Latin letters for now. Vatraxu has 19 consonants and 7 vowels. Ph is the f sound and is never written as a plain f. Sh is ʃ, ng is ŋ, a doubled vowel is long, q is an ejective, and an apostrophe marks a break between two vowels. Vatrahu uses the IPA letters ħ, ʕ and ə, with “uh” as the working stand-in for the schwa, and marks its ejectives with a caret, as in p^, t^ and k^. Details are on Vatrahu and Vatraxu . Canon Native scripts for both are not yet designed. Open Example images to be added. Placeholder Selo Selo has the most complete native script, in three layers plus a way to read it aloud. Every syllable is one written block, (C)V(N) plus a tone. A final /ŋ/ is always written ng, /tʃ/ is ch, /ʃ/ is sh, and there are no silent letters. Stress for chanting falls on the first tone-bearing syllable, unless a tone 6 syllable appears, and tone 6 syllables are always stressed. Decided Layer Selo name What it does Glyph script sin¹ si³ A logographic script like kanji. It combines radicals into glyphs that carry meaning, and one glyph can stand for a root or give a syllable. Helper syllabary yu¹ si³ A syllable script like hiragana. It spells particles, inflections and phonetic hints. Any word can be spelled entirely in it, though nuance is lost. Romanized writing ro¹ si³ Latin letters with tone numbers or accent marks, like Pinyin. Reading aloud do¹ lo³ The native pronunciation attached to a glyph, like the kun reading of a kanji. Example images to be added. Placeholder Mouane Mouane has no script of its own. See Mouane . Fort and Léger are written in French orthography. Fort drops the tréma on split vowels and Léger keeps it as a learning aid. Decided Open questions Native scripts for Kannafên, Sharafên, Mylzhfã, Dorrwfø, Vatrahu and Vatraxu. Open Images of each script, which Éné will supply. Open Whether Nọk’s standard script has a name in the language. Open

x: Home / Ishphaeno / Materials and Craft Materials and Craft What Ishphaeno’s people wear, build, forge and trade in. Almost every fibre, hide and ornament comes from creatures and plants already in the living things pages. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Ishphaeno garments and material culture reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Clothing is on its own page, and so is music. Clothing and Regalia Draping, the rank wraps, the ring and the circlet. Instruments and Music Skull drums, wing-bone harps, crystal chimes and the three court ensembles. The logic of cloth Fur and hide are common, because nearly anyone can obtain and work them. Flawless woven cloth takes generations of specialised craft, and that is what makes it the true luxury marker, not the rarity of the raw material. A Lamqa in impeccably woven fabric displays civilisation itself. A frontier soldier in beautifully worked Ruqorith hide displays competence, not poverty. Neither reads as lesser. They are different registers of one value system: mastery over mere possession. Fibres and cloth Material Source What it is used for Kelnith fiber Kelnith, the herd insect that shares Ruqoravael with Zelnith. It sheds fine plant-processed strands in its molt. Coarse, breathable cloth, closer to linen or raffia. The everyday cloth of Ishphaeno, worn by soldiers, servants and common households. Vulqorith wool The shed or sheared coat of the Vulqorith, the mammoth-elephant war mount bred by House Vulqaq. A harvested fibre that sits between Kelnith fiber and Ruqorith leather. The soft underwool makes fine cloth, and the coarse guard hair makes rope, felt and padding. See Working Mounts . Qalthiq Fibrous strands drawn from Qalthorut, the obsidian-plains succulent. Rope, coarse cloth, baskets and sandals. Ishphaeno’s hemp, and an everyday export of Xathhona. Mresovel Fungal sheets grown naturally in Mresibooshle. Waterproof, soft, nearly velvet. Boots and travel clothing, favoured by anyone crossing the borderland forest. Luthaevel Cocoons of Luthorun, a giant moth relative of the ordinary Luthveli butterfly. The true luxury textile and the only equivalent to silk. Lighter than silk, nearly liquid in drape, and it shifts colour with the Toluqavel aurora. It cannot be mass produced. See Luthorun . Sobraevit wings Shed wings of the crystal cicada of TeDrona. Layered into translucent, stained-glass-like fabric for veils, sleeves and ceremonial cloaks. Hides, feathers, shell and crystal Material Source What it is used for Ruqorith hide The Ruqorith herds, which range across every quarter. Thick armour leather, buttery ceremonial leather, suede and embossed leather. Horn doubles as an ivory substitute. The backbone of practical leatherwork. See Ruqorith . Xathelun fur The tiger-wolf apex predator of Xathdrubooshle. Dangerous to obtain, so ownership is a status marker, like tiger or snow leopard fur. In practice restricted to the Lamqa, the Veshaelja and military honours. Miravun shell Scutes naturally shed by the flying turtles that nest beneath the inverted mountains. Layered breastplates, hair ornaments, combs and ceremonial shoulder guards. A southern luxury tied to Belishael and Zarazael’s territory. Vorunith feathers Flight feathers shed naturally by the large flying predator that nests atop Mamon’s floating islands. Fans, capes, collars, headdresses and ceremonial standards. Collected without harming the animal. Qorazil quills The hollow-quill mice and their rattling spines. Worked into living fringe rather than sewn flat, so walking makes the garment softly chime. Some families tune their quills on purpose. Others cultivate silence. Mresorak elytra Wing covers of the cattle-sized beetles of the fungal forest. Belt plates, pauldrons, fans and decorative scale-work. Iridescent armour that is not metal. Contested, because Mresibooshle is unclaimed borderland. Sobraevael Flexible tendrils from the living crystal formations of TeDrona. Braided into belts, jewellery, corset frames and collars. It keeps growing slowly after it is cut, so the jewellery is, in a small way, still alive. Who governs which craft Material or craft Governing house Fine weaving and garment design House Kaelithael (Zarazael), Aesthetics and Fashion Crystal inlay and finished luxury pieces (Sobraevael) House Shinael (Zarazael), Ornamentation and Luxury Goods Vorunith feather collection House Vorunaq (Mamon), Floating Islands Kelnith fiber House Vulqaq (Lamjamon), alongside the Ruqorith manure export Mresorak elytra and Mresovel leather Contested. Belzevuv, Belishael and Zarazael all hold a stake, as they do in the forest itself. Sovoq House Sovoq, at the Sovulquk Sobi and sovoq Sobi is crystallised emotion, and its states run from raw crystal through ore, powder, shaped currency, glass and liquid to forged steel. Metal is precious on Ishphaeno, and sovoq is the unique metal. Form Term Raw soul crystal sobi Ore sobimae Ground powder sobis Shaped currency Sobik Vitrified glass sobimael Liquid sobil Forged weapon-steel sovoq Sobi from Colour and quality Fear Pale, almost clear, and dense. Grief Deep violet, medium density. Rage Dark red-black, the densest, and the best for weapons. Despair Smoky grey and brittle. Hope or love Anomalous. It does not forge. Sovoq is graded by the emotion it came from. Prime sovoq is made from rage-sobi, common sovoq from mixed sobi, and poor sovoq from brittle despair-sobi. Decided The currency tiers are value labels, not metals. Canon Currency tier Material “Copper” tier Pheluq, shaped resin from Xathdrubooshle “Silver” tier Veluphe, volcanic crystal shards from the western mines, reachable only in the Veluphe and Pheluvorath season “Gold” tier Sobik, shaped soul crystal Metals Copper (Ruqoluth) and iron exist naturally in lesser amounts, scarce and patchy. Copper is a working metal sold by weight, for wire, fittings and cookware, and it is valued below the currency tiers. Copper-stained rock in the volcanic west is a source. Decided Iron comes from ironsand (magnetite), bog iron in the swamps and red volcanic soils. Its Vatraxu name is left for the naming session. Decided Smiths mirror Mafa smith techniques from the Mandara Mountains of Cameroon. Decided In practice that means a tall down-draft furnace fed with magnetite ironsand, smelting hot enough to make carbon-rich cast iron, a second hearth that burns the carbon off with blown air to make workable steel, then hand forging. Proposed There is no native gold or silver. They exist only as imports from Earth, and they are exotic luxuries and trade curiosities, not currency. Decided There is no tin, so no bronze, and titanium is left out. Proposed A possible clad blade has an iron core with a sovoq edge. Proposed Fire-gifted Vatrajaxu and Vatrajaxo are skilled artisans, not a labour pool. Decided Salt Salt is sacred. It is a flavouring, a ritual ingredient and an everyday implement. Decided It purifies transitions: union ceremonies such as marriage, contract and christening, and funeral or ending rites. Decided Salt is mixed into the road composition. Decided Vamihona’s salt flats form by evaporation of Xatheloru water on the dry side of the mountains, and Tovuvami is the city of salt. Canon Contracts may be sealed with salt. Proposed Glass Glass is raw and impure, milky or greenish, never perfectly refined. Decided Sobimael windows stay, but they are raw and tinted by emotion. Decided Slag glass and glass frit may go into the road mix and glazes. Proposed Sand, stone and ground TeDrona’s sand is bone-white and granular, with coloured veins by emotion type, and some dunes sing or squeak. Bodies left there slowly turn to sand. Decided Qaelvaelvo’s black beach is volcanic glass and basalt sand with a magnetite fraction at the waterline and a little ground sobi. Decided Clay for roads may come from weathered volcanic ash. Proposed Compasses are very unreliable and get worse toward the centre. Decided Soils by region are on the soil map . Open questions The Vatraxu name for iron. Open Which mining house works under Zamodes now, and whether a new lesser house is created. Open What stone the heat cores are made of. This page lists places only. Who the princes are, what they are called among mortals and how they relate to one another is not published here. The four quarters Quarter Gate Keeper Princes Character North Naethvatael Hashaeqa Mephithoveles, Lamjamon The most politically central quarter and the oldest trading hub, closest to the capital. East Haelvatael Naevoshi Belzevuv, Dagan Water-rich, the shipbuilding capital, with misty cave systems. West Jaeshvatael Zaelith Zamodes, Mamon Floating islands, cliff terrain and mineral wealth, with an ongoing land dispute. South Taepvatael Pholaeth Belishael, Zarazael Inverted mountains, salt flats, the heat zone and the judgment facility boundary. Each gate is held by one of the four original succubi. They are gate wardens and regional administrators, not commanders over the princes. Their authority runs parallel to the princes’ and their estates sit near their gates. Princes hold wide territories, and estates sit within them rather than at the edges. Every prince has seconds and feudal chains for day-to-day work, and commands their own army. x: Home / Across the realms / Calendars Calendars How each realm and people counts time: a day without a sun, a year that wanders, and a moon that keeps the seasons. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the reference documents for each realm. Tags mark anything less settled. Numbers worked out from canon are marked as such. At a glance Realm Day Week Year How people keep time Earth (Nok) 24 hours Six days 12 months of 30 days, then 5 sacred days A calendar that follows the Gregorian year closely Ishphaeno 8 periods, which is 48 Earth hours Eight days, which is 16 Earth days 49 to 62 weeks, about 2.1 to 2.7 Earth years The Xathaeli, a living clock, and the six aurora seasons Aempaera One Torusheva cycle, 24 Aempaera hours (4 Earth hours) Decided Six days, which is one Earth day Decided Two seasons that follow Jangshe’s energy, counted in weeks The Shorumael shadow dial and the wind Kanna 26.43 hours Four days before the Calamity, six days in civil use after Decided 192 local days, 211.45 Earth days Civil: eight 24-day months. Religious: twelve 16-day months, once set by the twin moons Urhmaiia The Aldisha, 24 Orhdusha, about 36 surface hours Decided Five Aldisha Decided Twelve moon months in three seasons, thirteen when the watch of Antares calls for it Decided The moon, the scribes’ tables and the yearly watch of Antares Earth Almost everyone on Earth uses the ordinary Gregorian calendar. The Nok keep their own, built to map onto it. It has twelve named months of thirty days followed by a five-day sacred month, six days in a Gregorian leap year. The week has six days, and the year opens in February. The epoch is 379 BCE. The full tables, the festival year and the name-day tradition are on Calendar and festivals . Nok seasons Because the Nok year starts in February, their four seasons fall a little differently from the usual Northern ones. Season Nok name Typical months Meaning Spring Kwózọnyí March and April First growth of nature Summer Büng’òyé May to August Hot joy Fall Khètufẹnírẹt September to November Big harvest or feast Winter Zhömùyi December to February In the Nok homeland, which lies mostly on the equator, there are only two tropical seasons: Féfésheinona, the wet season, and Shíshísheinona, the dry season. The Nok word for the calendar is gbasídíma or gbasíméjídíma , “record of days.” The Name Calendar is Khínai’gbasídí . Decided Ishphaeno Ishphaeno has no sun and no moon, so its day is kept by a living clock and its year by the sky. Time also runs slower there than on Earth. One Ishphaeno hour is six Earth hours. Day, week and year Unit Length In Earth time Period (an Ishphaeno hour) One of eight in a day 6 Earth hours Day 8 periods 48 Earth hours, or 2 Earth days Week 8 days 16 Earth days Shortest year 49 weeks About 784 Earth days, or 2.1 Earth years Longest year 62 weeks About 992 Earth days, or 2.7 Earth years A typical year is roughly two to 2.7 Earth years long whatever order the seasons come in. The Xathaeli The Xathaeli is a native organism that looks like an anemone, kept in an open ceramic or stone pot in homes, shops, government buildings and ships. It cycles through four colours, one for each quarter of the day, and its pulse tells you how far through the quarter you are. Read it from the corner of your eye, the way you notice a ceiling fan slowing down. See the Xathaeli for the animal itself. Colour Quarter Earth-day feel Warm amber First Morning Soft white Second Midday Cool blue Third Afternoon and evening Deep violet Fourth Night Each colour lasts two periods, which is 200 minutes. The first half is still. The second half pulses, slowly at first, then faster and faster, until a long, slow bloom of the new colour arrives, like an exhale. Phase Length Pulse Steady 100 minutes None, completely still Regular pulse 75 minutes About 10 seconds a cycle, slow and languid Accelerated pulse 25 minutes About 6 to 7 seconds a cycle Peak tempo 5 minutes About 4 seconds a cycle. The change is imminent Colour shift About 10 to 15 seconds One long bloom pulse, then it settles Wild Xathaeli are erratic and make poor timekeepers, so households keep cultivated ones, bred for a steady pulse and brighter colour. A dying or irregular Xathaeli is deeply disorienting. Households whose Xathaeli dies during Qoruvrak, when replacements are hard to find, feel real anxiety. The pot is watered and sprinkled with ash twice a week. The tables count 100 minutes to a period, so the period is also an hour of 100 minutes. Proposed The six aurora seasons The sky is lit by the Toluqavel, Toluqavadoth’s inner state made visible. Its colour sets the season. There is a most-common order, followed about 85 per cent of the time, but Toluqavadoth is Primordial Chaos and the order shifts. The lengths vary within the ranges below. Almanac scholars and diviners make probabilistic predictions, and none can ever be fully accurate. See Toluqavadoth and the sky map . No. Colour Casual and formal name Length Character 1 Deep crimson Xathruq / Ruxathos 13 to 15 weeks War, heat and activity. The most militarily active season. Contracts signed in blood carry extra weight. 2 Sulfur yellow-gold Veluphe / Pheluvorath 11 to 13 weeks Trade, harvest and abundance. The sobi mines are busiest and the black market peaks. The sky turns the colour of money. 3 Pale silver-white Seluphera / Phereluthosel 6 to 8 weeks Rest, negotiation and contracts. Major agreements are formalized, with aurora contingency clauses. 4 Toxic green Zeluth / Voragelu 4 to 6 weeks Growth, transformation and dangerous magic. Mresibooshle becomes genuinely dangerous and things grow faster than intended. 5 Violet-black Xaelshe / Xaelmavorath 13 to 15 weeks Death rites, mourning and remembrance. The sky is practically black over much of the realm. 6 Cobalt blue Qoruvrak / Qoruvrath 2 to 5 weeks The liminal disaster season: earthquakes, eruptions, tidal surges and higher chaos. The six ranges add up to a year of 49 to 62 weeks. The shift from season five to season six is deliberate, and the cosmology has a reason for it. The most feared event is Qoruvrak twice in close succession. It has happened at least once, and it became a legendary catastrophic era. Each season has one colour, and its shade varies subtly through the season. The Toluqavel crosses the sky like a very wide sun, on a daily rhythm that wanders, so it is not reliable enough to tell time. Decided The tides The Xatheloru tides are Toluqavadoth’s breathing. They are used for coastal navigation, reading its mood and omens, and never for telling time. A suddenly irregular tide means something is disturbing its rest, and in Qoruvrak it breathes harder, with storm surges and flooding. Aempaera Aempaera has no night. Torusheva, the luminous orb Jangshe made, hangs above the realm and never sets. Over a long cycle it slowly bleaches from full brightness to a dim moonlight, then brightens again. When it is dim, the stars come out, the same stars seen from Earth from another angle. See Aempaera and Jangshe . Phase Torusheva Stars Full brightness At peak Not visible Gradual dimming Bleaching slowly Partly visible Moonlight level Dim Visible and blazing Gradual brightening Returning Fading The Shorumael and the wind Because the orb never moves across the sky, shadows always point the same way, so a normal sundial is useless. What changes is shadow length. The Shorumael is a vertical post or obelisk with rings marked at measured distances on the ground around it. A bright orb gives a short shadow and a dim orb a long one, so the shadow on the rings gives the broad period. Wind gives the finer reading. Light, frequent gusts mean the morning equivalent, strong longer gusts the afternoon, and gentler medium gusts the evening. Brightness and wind together give complete timekeeping. A Vatrajarə who is blind or has impaired senses can tell the time by wind alone. Day and week Torusheva’s brightening and dimming is the nearest thing Aempaera has to day and night. One full cycle, from full brightness through moonlight and back, is one day. Decided A day is 24 Aempaera hours. Because an Earth hour holds six Aempaera hours, a day lasts 4 Earth hours. Decided The week is six days, which is exactly one Earth day. Decided The two seasons are counted in weeks. Hevatoru has more moonlit days than Romatoru. Decided How many weeks each season lasts is not set. Open Names of the units Unit Vatrahu Vatraxu Meaning Day tarə taro From tarə , light. A day is one cycle of the light. Decided Week jarə jaro From jarə , breath or life. Six days make one Earth day, so a week is one breath of the realm below. Decided Calendar tarəkoom tarokoom Count of light. koom is “count.” Decided Vatraxu turns the schwa into o , so the Vatraxu forms follow from the Vatrahu ones. The Vatraxu forms are given here for comparison. The names for Ishphaeno’s own day and week are not set. Two seasons Aempaera’s two seasons follow Jangshe’s own capacity, not the weather. The names are Vatrahu. Season Meaning Torusheva Effect on the Vatrajarə Romatoru The alive season. Jangshe at full capacity and everything vibrant Stays bright with minimal dimming Aethaari replenishes faster, markings show more and wings glow Hevatoru The rest season. Jangshe at slower capacity and everything quieter Dims to moonlight more often, and the stars show longer Aethaari replenishes slower, a natural period for meditative stillness Vatrahu roma means strong or vital and heva means slow or dimming. The ending -toru means domain or eternal realm. Kanna Kanna circles its orange star Hvan once in 211.45 Earth days, which is 192 local days of 26.43 hours each. Its year is 0.579 of an Earth year, and the 26-degree axial tilt turns the seasons about 1.7 times faster than Earth’s. See The Hvan system . Before the Calamity The old calendar belonged to the twin moons. A year was exactly 192 local days, with no drift. Unit Length Set by Month 16 local days One full Kiruvyn phase cycle, exactly Year 12 months, 192 local days Twelve Kiruvyn cycles Week 4 local days Four to a month, twelve to a season, forty-eight to a year Season 48 local days, four to a year The solar year The wandering calendar 34.9 local days Kiravin’s cycle, which deliberately does not divide the year Kiruvyn, “Eye of the Ebb,” keeps a nearly circular orbit and never changes in the sky, so it is the fixed calendar moon. Kiravin, “Eye of the Flow,” moves in an elliptical orbit and visibly swells and shrinks, so its cycle drifts against the year and produces a wandering ritual calendar beside the fixed solar one. In Nok the moons are Khùzú and Khùzí. After the Calamity The moons collided and merged into one, Sidlosa, also called Khùm. The new sky holds 8.886 moon-months in a year, which is not a whole number. Every descendant culture still keeps the twelve-month year as its religious calendar, out of reverence for a sky none of them has seen, so they count twelve months while the moon above them keeps a different rhythm. Civil life uses a solar calendar of eight months of 24 days with a six-day week, thirty-two weeks to the year, which the broken moons cannot disturb. The tides also changed, from an irregular two-moon beat to a steady one. See the Calamity . Names for the time units These are Stamfaen roots, with the forms the daughter languages give them. Decided Meaning Stamfaen Rejfên Lyndfê̂n Day daf daf daf Week fika fika fika Moon, month gonde gode, and gonde in ceremony ngonde Year lar lar lar Count tal tal tal Names of the calendars Calendar Stamfaen Rejfên Lyndfê̂n Meaning Calendar in general Daftal Daftal Daftal Day-count The civil, solar calendar Kèltal Kèltal Kèltal Sun-count The religious, moon calendar, also the pre-Calamity one Gondetal Godetal, and Gondetal in ceremony Ngondetal Moon-count Kiravin’s wandering calendar Faeskital Feskital Festal Walking-count The other daughter languages build theirs from the same roots by their own sound changes. Decided Urhmaiia The Urhmaiia live under the sea, so their calendar follows the ocean and the moon. Their year has three seasons and twelve months, and the months follow the lunar cycle, with a thirteenth month added when the sky calls for it. The Gregorian months below are only the nearest surface equivalent. See the Urhmaiia and their language . The unequal split is deliberate and follows the standard depth of Urhmaiia dwellings. Decided Week, month and year Unit Length Notes Week 5 Aldisha Four to a month, so 48 to a year. Decided Month (Ilesha) 20 Aldisha, the last one shortened Nineteen full Aldisha and a short day of 16½ Orhdusha make 708.75 surface hours, or 29.53 days, within about a minute of the real lunar month. Decided Season 16 weeks, four months Counted in weeks. Decided Year (Alesha) 12 months, or 13 in a leap year Twelve months is about 354 surface days, and a leap year about 384. Decided The short day The last day of every month is shortened so the calendar stays true to the moon. The short day at the end of the twelfth month lasts about 24¾ hours, almost exactly one surface day. It is the one day when Urhmaiia time and surface time nearly match, which is why the yearly watch happens on it. Decided The watch of Antares Twelve moon months fall about eleven days short of the solar year. To keep the seasons in place, every year on the short day of the twelfth month a scout goes up to the surface before dawn to look for Antares, the red star in the south, on the first dawns it can be seen after being lost in the sun’s glare. The Urhmaiia have their own name for it, meaning a parent’s love. Decided The scribes. Keepers of the 19-year table predict each year’s leap month well ahead, seal the prediction in front of witnesses at the start of the short day, and open it after the sighting. If the scout and the scribes disagree, the sighting wins, and the quarrel becomes an omen or a scandal. Decided The scout. Certain families train for the honour and nominate candidates. The priests choose one each year. In custom only an Urhmauuka is chosen, because they are fully amphibious. An Urhmate could technically do it. The scout may come ashore to watch if they wish, but the sighting can be made from the water’s surface. Decided The ascent. From the deepest cities about one and a half to two hours, with a pause near the surface and a slow rise at the end. The whole trip is about seven hours. Proposed The watch. The scout surfaces in the dark and treads water, facing the south-east corner of the sky. Antares rises about 45 minutes before sunrise. Its return to the dawn sky falls between about 23 and 28 December by the surface calendar. Decided Star clear and bright. The year opens on time. Decided Star hazy, pale or deep red. Each is read as an omen for the season. Decided Sky clear and no star. The year is not finished, and a thirteenth month is added. A leap month is a full month of 20 Aldisha. Decided Clouded out. The scout may try again at up to three more dawns, treading water, with those days counted outside the year as sacred days. Decided Over 19 years. The leap months average seven in 19 years, and the new year slides within about a month after the star first appears. Proposed Sunrise and sunset time at the surface, and how the scribes work out the star’s hour without a sun, are not yet set. Open Converting between realms Earth is the neutral baseline for every conversion. Ishphaeno time runs slower and Aempaera time runs faster, which gives these rates. Conversion Rate 1 Ishphaeno hour 6 Earth hours, or 36 Aempaera hours 1 Earth hour 6 Aempaera hours 1 Aempaera hour 10 Earth minutes (worked out from the rate above) 1 Ishphaeno day 8 periods, 48 Earth hours 1 Ishphaeno week 8 Ishphaeno days, 16 Earth days Earth sits between Aempaera and Ishphaeno in how time flows. Guards of the punishment facility Zashraaxomavel serve their rotations measured in Earth years, because both sides need a common reference. One standard rotation is 60 Earth years, a full human lifetime on purpose. An Ishphaeno year is 2.1 to 2.7 Earth years, so that is about 22 to 28 Ishphaeno years, or about 360 Aempaera years at six to one. Open questions How many weeks long each Aempaera season is. x: Home / Across the realms / Cosmology and timeline Cosmology and timeline The two families of myth and power that share one universe, and the order in which their great events happened. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the reference documents for each realm. Tags mark anything less settled. Numbers worked out from canon are marked as such. Two cosmological families The universe runs on two separate families of myth and power. They are not meant to interfere with each other. Decided The Dream family The Order and Chaos family Rooted in Kanna and the Hvan system, above all its twin moons, Kiruvyn and Kiravin The two primordials: Jangshe, who is Order, and Toluqavadoth, who is Chaos Realms Kanna, and on Earth the Nok homeland and the Urhmaiia sea Aempaera inside Jangshe, and Ishphaeno inside Toluqavadoth Peoples The Vorfae and their descendants, the Nok, the Sekh and the Anu, and the Urhmaiia, who name the same divine balance in their own tongue The Vatrajarə and their fallen, the Lamiae, the Witches of Mephis, and the infernal princes Faith Nẹránamün, the Nok faith, and the Vorfae traditions of Kanna The Ashraama faith, which human scholars know as Abrama Human origins The Nok trace to Lyndfe settlers who blended with humans Jangshe made the first humans on Earth Decided Earth is where they meet. The Sekh and the Anu follow the Dream family’s framework, and the Lamiae and the witches follow the other. The war in Aempaera and the Exodus from Kanna are separate events, and the timeline below keeps them in one list so you can see which came first. On the Dream side, see Kanna and the faith . On the other side, see Aempaera , Jangshe and Toluqavadoth . The order of events Order is firmer than dates. Where no date is given, the sequence is what is settled. Kanna and the Exodus These events are firmly ordered. The Calamity’s lengths are calculated, and the rest are in sequence only. When What happens See Before worlds Hvaengur, life itself, exists. Hvandaer, the Shepherd, and Kresyva, the Tree-Mother, are joined, and from their union come the Vorfae. The Vorfae About 1,000,000 Earth years The Silent Drift. Gate-working draws down the ley field that holds the moons steady, too slowly for anyone to notice in a lifetime. The Calamity About 9,000 Earth years The Visible Collapse. The sky misbehaves within living memory, the moons lose their calendar and the tides run wrong. The Calamity The impact Kiruvyn and Kiravin collide and merge into Sidlosa, also called Khùm. A fragment strikes Kanna with about twice the energy of Chicxulub. Kresyva’s sacrifice buys the convoys time to leave. The Calamity Around the impact The Hvaena, Staenhild Fjolraen, Nosmaera Svandor and Hjordin Rosvaern, leave through Skandaer’s gates. Vorfae who stay survive in two ways: on the scarred surface, as the ancestors of the Dorrwfø, and underground, as the ancestors of the Mylzhfã. Peoples The first age on Earth No dates are set for these events. The order is what counts. Decided Order What happens See 1 The Hvaena make a first foothold at Khematin, near the Kush and Nile corridor. Humans fear the newcomers and their children, and the fear becomes a planned strike, the Ambush. The Hvaena flee east along the road later called Ostiraej. Peoples 2 The proto-Rejfê are born to the three Hvaena during the Exodus, and the proto-Lyndfe with them. Haelael, a general of Aempaera who has been drawn to Earth by the gate-flare, fathers the proto-Rejfê by all three. Rejfê 3 Hjamblynd (Hajmblynd in Kannafên), the “home-grove,” is founded in the secluded highlands near the Cameroon fault line. It is claimed with Grombaer’s rite, which attunes the people to Earth’s ley field. The grove communities that attune this way become the Lyndfe. The Kannafê later name their Kanna Homegrove Hajmblynd after it. Kannafê 4 The war in Aempaera, Krang Uthjook, is fought and lost, and the Fall follows. The losing side is cast out and changed, and Thamael and Haelael, brothers, take the names Sadok and Lioshe. Haelael stops visiting his children on Earth. Nearly all of the first generation of Lamiae die in it. The war 5 Sadok clears Ishphaeno from the body of Toluqavadoth, with Xathqaelsel as its centre. Skandaer bargains with Lioshe: Lioshe swears to keep the Vorfae hidden and to answer their calls, and Skandaer helps shape Ishphaeno’s gates as a contained system. The oath is said to be sealed in a tooth planted in the earth, and the tree that rose from it, the oathtree, is the record of whether it is kept. Ishphaeno 6 The Return. Word reaches the Earth-descended peoples that Kanna still lives, renewed. Most Rejfê go back, most Lyndfe stay, and a small minority of each cross the other way. Those who go become the four Rejfê tribes and the Kannafê. Rejfê 7 The Great Flood strikes Earth, and it hits those left behind. Some die. The Lyndfe and Rejfê who stay on land interbreed with humans and become the Fjarafê, whose descendants are the Nok. Peoples Nok tradition keeps a distorted memory of the Calamity. Lyndfe settlers arrived on a world with one moon, carrying the memory of a sky with two, and they built a myth to explain the difference: the crashing of Khùzú and Khùzí into Khùm. The Nok call the event Dímakhùm Daimùzónobu. See the faith . The dated record Year What happens See 379 BCE Year 1 of the Nok count. Calendar About 309 BCE Amadi is born among the Kweizimuna of the Bamenda highlands. The Sekh 289 BCE Amadi is reborn at the age of twenty. The Sekh 1725 Hurste is founded by migrating Sekh and their human Zingan followers. Emsehurst 1738 Yírímbo Zonémi is established in Hurste. Emsehurst 1805 Emerson is founded by a settler caravan north of the Emmers River. Emsehurst About 1808 to 1810 The Emerson catastrophe and the founding witch contracts. Emsehurst 1851 The First Night of Mefi. Witch lines 1924 Emerson and Hurste are incorporated as Emsehurst. Emsehurst 1933 The original Pandora’s Pact is signed. The Pact 1964 The Lamiae are admitted through the Pact addendum. The Pact 1968 The interstate is completed. Emsehurst 1970 The Human Coalition’s raid, when it still went by the name Light of Humanity, removes the Somerhalder line from Emsehurst. The opposition The Lamiae are older than the Sekh as a people, and the references give no dates for them. The order of events is what counts. Decided Open questions Dates and durations for everything between the Exodus and 379 BCE. The order is locked, and the spans are deferred. Open How long the war in Aempaera lasted, and when it happened. Open Násítámün needs a Rejfên name. She has only her Nok name for now. Open

Most everyday clothing is biodegradable. Treated leather, reforged metal and status materials are the deliberate exceptions, kept and passed down because permanence is rare. Iron comes from the shed scales of the scaly-foot gastropod (Kohusoa). Music and sound The Urhmaiia’s music is voice. Haulorai, the uvular call speech, is “deep song” or “abyss voice,” used for long-distance communication, mourning calls, mate calls and soothing animals. Its full inventory includes clicks and whistles absent from ordinary speech. The siren call to the water is Goria, and the death or loss call is Zorugoria. At a hatching, the whole community gathers at the Raunutua and contributes its Haulorai, and the vibrations physically help guide the hatchling out. The oldest sacred Haulorai compositions and mourning calls keep an archaic consonant-cluster onset that is no longer a living feature. See the Urhmaiia language page and life and rites . No instruments are recorded for the Urhmaiia yet. Open Kanna Each people has its own dress tradition, drawn from real-world models. Fuller descriptions are on the people pages: Rejfê , Kannafê , Mylzhfã and Dorrwfø . People Dress draws on Kannafê Modified Toghu, the Bamileke royal velvet, as a base tradition. Fjarafê, as a once-distinct people Congolese-inspired. Tavgrirejfê (Rejfê, earth, centre) Ethiopian-inspired. The hooded poncho and Andean-inspired footwear are their general tribal style. Havdèlrejfê (Rejfê, water, coast) Fulani, and Ivorian, Beninese and Guinean traditions. Dhavgrirejfê (Rejfê, fire, south) Chad and Mali traditions. Savkalrejfê (Rejfê, air, north) Basotho blanket tradition with Mongol and Sámi influence. Mylzhfã Georgian, in the Khevsuruli and Mtiuluri mountain-dance style. The base garment is the chokha, a fitted coat with cartridge rows that can carry grove and ancestor motifs. Headwear is adapted for their large ears. Dorrwfø Thai tradition. The Vorfae’s own everyday material culture is not recorded yet. Neither is Kannafê poetry as a form, or any Kanna instrument or music. Open Earth Sekh shifting and clothing: clothes are not part of the soul and do not travel through a shift by default. Old Sekh can extend their soul’s definition of self to include clothing with training and concentration, but an emergency shift strips even ancient Sekh back to soul-claimed items. Most keep spare clothing in cars, lockers and offices. See The Sekh . Nẹránamün practice uses a slow rhythm of drums, flute or chanting in dream-current dance, and a woven or stitched version of sacred cloth marks is sometimes worn at ceremonies, never tattooed or drawn on the skin. Clan memory songs record severed threads as warnings. See Nẹránamün and sacred arts and symbols . Nọk and Sekh music The Nọk dictionary has a music section, so Nọk and Sekh music is partly recorded. The instrument list names mostly West African instruments, plus a few Western ones, and only the drum has its Nọk word filled in so far. Nọk Meaning dórin drum (the one instrument word recorded) dón-dón drum beats, and beat in general (onomatopoeia) úrin music úriná song úrináyí musician úrinákhèt album úrijúmo lyrics dóri beat úrei rhythm dódó pattern Wásei / Ropúmo / Faibérí verse / chorus / bridge púwósí / Pumésí intro / outro tùnípó / íwóyí remix / reverb shímù song or chant. The verb is ng’shímù, to sing or chant. ng’dózé to beat, thump or drum ng’mwutù to blow (wind, a whistle or a horn) ng’kómbaurí to compose (weave) music ng’gímí / ng’bùmé to burst into song / to dance ba, bamai singing sounds The instrument list covers the piano, violin, flute, cello, viola, horn, trumpet (small horn), trombone (long horn), balafon, shekere, djembe, algaita, ngoni, xalam and akontig. Open Their Nọk words are still to be written, except the drum. Lullaby: “It’s okay, baby” A Nọk lullaby adapted from the Yoruba lullaby Orin Iremolekun , which inspired the melody. The refrain is shortened to òtó’à when sung and repeated two or three times as a chorus.
