x: Home / Across the realms / Glossary and names Glossary and names The terms, titles and naming rules of the universe in one place, with a link to the page that explains each. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the reference documents for each realm. Tags mark anything less settled. Numbers worked out from canon are marked as such. How to read the names The universe has many languages, and a name usually tells you which one it comes from. These are the patterns worth knowing. Nok Pattern Means Example -mün A god Háshùmün, Hóshémün -díma A day of the week Háshùdíma, Hóshédíma -mọnai A month Zíngámọnai -khèm A sacred day Zhèmídíyèkhèm Nok spellings use tone marks and dotted vowels. They follow the current reference documents, and the same name is always spelled the same way. Egyptian-looking words in the older documents are ignored unless they name a city or a place. Decided Stamfaen and its daughters Stamfaen always keeps its full ae . The daughter languages reduce it to ê . è is a stressed ɛ. The names of peoples carry the ê: Lyndfê̂, Rejfê, Kannafê, Sharafê. The Vorfae name stays unreduced. The Dorrwfø and the Mylzhfã call themselves by those names, with a plain-text spelling for typing. The full family tree is on Stamfaen family . Vatrahu and Vatraxu Vatrahu is the language of Aempaera and the Vatrajarə. Vatraxu is the language of Ishphaeno. Many names come in a pair, and unless a page says otherwise the first form is Vatrahu. Thing Vatrahu Vatraxu The heavenly realm Aempaera Zaempaera The Infernal realm Ishvaeno (a human corruption of the name gave “Inferno”) Ishphaeno, with an alternate name, Qoruxeja The people Vatrajarə, and Vatrajaħə for the races descended from them Vatrajaxo The holy princes Ashraatraal Zashraatraal The great war Krang Uthjook Krang Zuthjuk The Fall Oshnalani TeSharani The O- and Te- in the Fall’s names are each language’s definite article. The old spelling Oshalani is retired. Decided Both languages allow two spellings of certain sounds. The formal spelling uses the real IPA symbol, such as ə, ħ, ʕ or ʁ. The working spelling uses a plain keyboard stand-in. They are the same sound in different settings, and neither is more correct. The almanac uses the formal spelling. Reading Ishphaeno place names Ishphaeno names are built from small parts. Once you know a few, you can read most of the map. Part Means You will see it in Qael Crown, rulership, gateway Qaeldrael, Qaelvaelvo, Xathqaelsel Sel Seat, council Xathqaelsel Pher Authority Phereluthosel, the formal name of season three Shael Twilight Xaelshe, the violet-black season Luth Becoming, transformation Zeluth, the toxic green season Qoru and Vrak Explosive burst and rupture Qoruvrak, the cobalt disaster season Xael Dark void Xaelshe, Xaelmavorath Rath Period or great, a formal suffix Pheluvorath, Xaelmavorath Vroth Weathered, established Tholvroth, a frontier city Drath Heavy discipline, force Drathmizul, Qordrathxael Tholu Deep hollow, cave Tholuvex, Tholvroth Baengli Flowing lust Baenglivael, Baenglishelu Ze, Zeli Active, rapid Zeluth, Zelivrrutes Malo Strong, heavy Malovrrutes, the strong river Vrrutes River Malovrrutes, Zelivrrutes Vaemi Beach, shore Jaeshvaemi, Haelvaemi Phol Lake Sheluphol Pharu Burning, heat Pharuhona, the heat zone Drona Desert, wasteland TeDrona, the crystal desert -hi Plural Vaethpojahi, Ruqorejahi -jane A system or collective Vaethpojane, Ruqorejane Toru Domain, eternal realm Romatoru, Hevatoru Roma and Heva Strong and vital, slow and dimming The two Aempaera seasons Urhmauuri Every syllable is one of four shapes: a consonant and a vowel, a vowel, a consonant and two vowels, or a vowel, a consonant and a vowel. Words almost never end in a consonant. The exception is -rh . There is no w, v or q. Old words that had them were changed to sh or ny , depending on their vowels. kh is one sound, not two. The same is true of rh , which has a formal spelling with ʁ. The ending -ii turns a concept into a person: Ezil plus -ii is Ezilii. An apostrophe marks two vowels that are not blended, as in Vo’im , which is two syllables. Two names exist for the same people. Urhmauua is what they call themselves, and Urhmaiia is what outsiders call them. The almanac uses Urhmaiia. Urhmauuri speech has five politeness levels. They are marked on the final verb, and the almanac names them here. Level Ending Used for Formal or polite -o Standard address in most formal situations Informal None Friends, peers and equals Intimate -e A mate or life partner only Respectful -i Someone of higher status or age Royal The fifth level Separate from these, the names of the gods have six registers of their own, from the formal high canon form down to the casual vernacular. Do not confuse the two systems. See the language page . Earth Term Meaning See Sekh The immortal people made by the Flame Queen, ‘Èn’zíngámün. They are reborn through a ritual, cast no shadow, and carry the moon-star mark. The Sekh Zingan (Shùkízíngámùna) A human devotee of the Flame Queen. Zingan replaces the older word “Sekhmetian.” “Sekh” stays as the one holdover. Decided Zingans Rebirth The initiation that makes a Sekh. An Initiator guides it, and the Initiator or a senior clan member names the new Sekh afterwards. Rebirth Khùnaimímaké The moon-star mark that appears on the skin at Rebirth. The Sekh Khùzí and Khùzú The two moons of Kanna. In a Sekh, the paired expressions of the two souls: Khùzí for the land-self and Khùzú for the aerial self. The faith Khùm The single moon of Earth, the unified moon. It remembers both the twin moons, Khùzí’s fire as it waxes and Khùzú’s memory as it wanes. The faith Zhèmuno The Original Clan: the nine founding members, each also the head of a clan of their own. Sekh society ‘Ạmázingamün The title of the Head Priestess. The older form ‘Amásekhmün is retired. Decided Sekh society Makésho The sacred arts, open to Zingans and Sekh alike. Fùmamaké is sacred ritual tattooing. Zingans Nẹránamün The Nok faith and its divine balance. Its 30 Threads are its moral code. The faith Nyámün The divine parent of the Nok gods. House of Ash loyalty is to Nyámün alone. The pantheon Anu People organised in packs who walk the Dream. Every mature Anu wears a thread, and they call the Sekh “Thread-runners.” The Anu Rï’zháma Initiation Day, for the Anu and for the Sekh name-days. Anu rites Zhíkhaidu Shadow entities: ghostly beings that slip through cracks in reality. Their canon status is still open. Open House of Ash Pandora’s Pact The treaty that protects humans in and around Emsehurst. In practice only the Sekh enforce it. Lamiae trafficking of humans is a breach. The Pact Bedien A human in a relationship with a Lamia: addicted, contracted or born into it. Bediens and Servi Servus (plural Servi) A human formally blood-bonded to a Lamia master through a short but permanent ritual. Bediens and Servi Lamia and Lamiae The Greek names for the Lamike, and the two are interchangeable. Lamike is one, Lamikehi is many, and the Sekh say KauNamä’i in Nok. Decided The Lamiae Verdoem The old word for the races of the Vatrajarə line, the Lamiae included. “Verdoem” always means Vatrajaħə, Vatrajaxo in Vatraxu. Decided The Lamiae Shòní and Kishòní The Nok year count. Year 1 is 379 BCE, and Kishòní marks the years before it. Calendar Aempaera Term Meaning See Vatrajarə The people of Aempaera, its soldiers, messengers and citizens. They speak Vatrahu. The Vatrajarə Vo’im The children of Vatrajarə and humans. Krang Uthjook Ashraatraal The holy princes. Their council is the Ashraakaenru. The Holy Princes Aethaari The energy of Aempaera. It fills the hollow feathers of every Vatrajarə’s wings. The Vatrajarə Aethjarə The aura, the environment of Aempaera leaking from the body at all times. The Vatrajarə Kraethjarə The aura flare, pushed outward as a weapon. In Vatraxu, Kraethjaro. Decided The Vatrajarə Aethmaale Holy steel forged from aethaari and inscribed with runes, made to kill the fallen and their children. Fatal to Lamiae. Lamiae Jangshe The primordial of Order, who made Ashraaha and, with her, the Vatrajarə. Order is not the same as kindness. Jangshe Ashraaha The mother of the Vatrajarə. She was made by Jangshe and is not a primordial. Jangshe Torusheva The luminous orb that lights Aempaera and never sets. Calendars Shorumael The shadow dial, a post with rings that gives the broad time of day. Calendars Romatoru and Hevatoru The alive season and the rest season of Aempaera. Calendars Ashraama (Abrama) The faith of Aempaera. Human scholars know it as Abrama. Aempaera Krang Uthjook The great war of Aempaera. Uthjook is “war.” Older documents call it the Krag War. Decided The war The Fall The defeat of Thamael and Haelael’s side, when the losers were cast out of Aempaera and changed. They took the names Sadok and Lioshe. The war Ishphaeno Term Meaning See Toluqavadoth The primordial of Chaos. Ishphaeno lies inside its body. Toluqavadoth Toluqavel The aurora of the false sky, Toluqavadoth’s inner state made visible. Its colour sets the season. Toluqavadoth Toluqael and Velqael A star of the false sky, a mineral growth from the membrane, and a constellation used for finding your way. The sky map Xathaeli The living clock: an anemone-like organism that changes colour through the day. The Xathaeli Xathqaelsel The capital city and palace at the centre of Ishphaeno, on the obsidian plains. Ishphaeno Zashraaxomavel The punishment facility, in the crystal desert TeDrona. Ishphaeno Sobi The main material resource of Ishphaeno, formed from crystallised suffering, fear, anger and grief. Materials Sobik and Pheluq Gold currency and copper currency. A sobik is shaped like a soul crystal and is the highest value. A pheluq is a common resin piece. Materials Sovoq Infernal steel, forged to counter Aethmaale. It can hurt a Lamia far less than Aethmaale does. Decided Lamiae Raqal The heart-stone of Infernal bodies. Whether the heart-stone of the Lamiae counts as one is still open. Open Lamiae Qoruvrak The cobalt aurora season, a liminal disaster season of earthquakes and surges. Calendars Kanna Term Meaning See Vorfae The ancestral people of Kanna. The four living peoples, the Rejfê, Kannafê, Mylzhfã and Dorrwfø, descend from them or evolved alongside them. The Vorfae Stamfaen The ancestral Vorfae language. The Lyndfe call it Grahne and the Rejfê call it Grejns. Languages Hvan and Hvandaer The orange star of Kanna’s system, and its divine name. In Nok, Lòbárạmün, the Sun King. The Hvan system Kiruvyn and Kiravin The twin moons of Kanna: the steady one and the restless one. In Nok, Khùzú and Khùzí. The Hvan system Skaedine The gas giant beyond Kanna, whose name echoes the gate god Skandaer. The Hvan system Hvaena The three Vorfae trusted with gate travel during the Calamity: Staenhild Fjolraen, Nosmaera Svandor and Hjordin Rosvaern. Cosmology and timeline Lyndfe, Kannafê and Fjarafê The Lyndfe are the parent people who took root on Earth. The Kannafê are the Lyndfe who went back to Kanna. The Fjarafê are the Lyndfe and Rejfê who stayed, interbred with humans and dissolved into the general population. Peoples The Exodus and the Return The Vorfae’s departure through the gates during the Calamity, and the later journey of the Earth-descended peoples back to a renewed Kanna. Cosmology and timeline The Calamity The catastrophe in which the Vorfae drained the field that held their sky together, and the moons collided. The Calamity Urhmaiia Term Meaning See Urhmauuka The lineage-born Urhmaiia, whose names invoke lineage. Life Urhmate Those whose names describe a trait. Life Urhmake The called back, born human, whose names reach forward. Life Ezilii, Izilii and Arhtsilii Neutral, receptive and insertive. All Urhmaiia are born Ezilii. Life Ruua The sacred breath or current that connects all water. It is not personified. Gods and faith Urhaha The Chooser of Tides, the divine progenitor of the Urhmaiia. Gods and faith Maubuʁ The deep interior where the dead are remembered, and the heart of the realm. Cities and the deep Kautsorii The messengers and scribes of the Sofa current. Language Ejasantunua The political whole of the realm, ruled in name by the crown. Cities and the deep Open questions The Vatrajarə abilities table now uses ə spellings (Aethjarə, Kraethjarə) to match the other pages. The keyboard spellings are Aethjaruh and Kraethjaruh. h: What it does to Ishphaeno Open questions
x: Home / Ishphaeno / Toluqavadoth Toluqavadoth Primordial Chaos. Every realm of the infernal side lies inside its body. This section follows the Aempaera and Ishphaeno reference documents. Lines without a tag are settled. Tags mark anything less settled. Names are given in Vatrahu unless a Vatraxu form is named. Name Toluqavadoth in Vatraxu, Toluk’avadoth in Vatrahu. The older forms Torqavadoth and Torqavel are retired. The root toluq means chaos. Nature A primordial: a generally formless cosmic being, and the force of Chaos. It contains every possibility. It gives off the same atmospheric gases as Earth. Body Ishphaeno exists within it. Each realm technically lies in its body. Beyond the borders of Ishphaeno lies the unmapped, ungoverned wilderness of Toluqavadoth itself. Temper Neither good nor evil. It takes a quiet pride that so much civilisation, complexity and suffering lives inside it. Counterpart Jangshe , the primordial of Order. What it does to Ishphaeno Sign What it is The tides The tides of the Xatheloru sea are Toluqavadoth’s breathing. They are used for coastal navigation, reading its mood and omens, and never for telling time. A suddenly irregular tide means something is disturbing its rest. In the Qoruvrak season it breathes harder, with storm surges and flooding. Toluqavel, the aurora Its inner state, made visible as shifting coloured light across the false sky. There are six seasons marked by colour, in a most-common order that holds about 85 percent of the time. Because this is Chaos, the order shifts and season lengths vary within ranges. Almanac scholars and diviners can only predict by probability. The most feared case is Qoruvrak twice in close succession, which is said to have happened at least once in recorded history. Ways in Unlike tightly controlled Aempaera, Ishphaeno has many ways in: gates, cracks, bargains, death and accident. The false sky, the aurora seasons and the tides are covered on the sky map and in The Realm . The realm itself was cleared from Toluqavadoth’s body by Sadok, with Xathqaelsel as ground zero. Open questions Whether Toluqavadoth has an avatar like Jangshe’s, or any way of speaking Open What lies in the unmapped wilderness, which is deliberately left open Open

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Castes and bodies Castes and bodies Three castes share a body plan and a language. Where they came from, and how long they can stay on land, decides most of what follows. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. Caste Meaning Origin Children On land Urhmauuka Water-born Made directly by Urhaha, or descended from those who were. Born intersex. Can have children. Fully amphibious with no limit. Urhmate Water-made Transformed by Dagan, or descended from humans he transformed. Each is melded with a fish species. First-generation transformed Urhmate cannot. Those born to the caste can. About 14 hours before madness sets in. Heavier fish traits mean less time. Urhmake Called back Human descendants of the Urhmaiia with latent traits. Can after ocean exposure. Cannot live out of water after awakening, and must adapt for one to two years submerged. An Urhmauuka with natural and ceremonial markings. Concept image. An Urhmate with dense reef-fish traits. Concept image. An Urhmate with few visible fish traits. Concept image. An Urhmake after awakening. Concept image. Body systems System Urhmauuka Urhmate Urhmake Breathing Lungs and throat gills, adaptable to air or water. Mostly gills. Lungs are vestigial. Human lungs at first. Gills form after awakening. Mind A resonance cortex, telepathy organs and dream-linked memory. A neural meshwork with marine structures. Awakening wakes latent resonance centres. Blood Iron-rich and pressure-adapted. It may glow with resonance. Multi-chambered hearts or a slowed pulse for deep pressure. Shifts from human to ocean-adapted blood under high stress. Voice A full larynx, a resonance plate and a Haulorai sac for speech, chant and harmonic projection. No larynx. They speak through cranial clicks, limb resonance and gill pulses. Voice collapses during change, then develops internal vibration sacs. Digestion Omnivorous. Omnivorous. Some deep-caste Urhmate live on resonance, detritus or symbiotic algae. Rejects land food after the change and adapts to marine food. Abilities shared by all Telepathy. The main way to speak underwater. It needs touch with non-telepaths, and some humans cannot receive it. Haulorai. Uvular call speech for long-distance calls, mourning and mate calls, and soothing animals. It includes clicks and whistles not found in ordinary speech. Geomagnetic sense. An inner compass. Strong sight. Wide pupils for deep water and a nictitating third eyelid that protects the eye and aids diving. Speed. Urhmaiia are the fastest swimmers except for the fastest fish. Hearing. On land, the loss of water tension makes sound painfully loud. They must actively block hearing to cope. This is a vulnerability. A land gait. A faint bouncing step, like pushing off the seabed. It fades with practice but never quite disappears in the first generation. Caste-only abilities Urhmauuka: Ruala, the magic craft. It covers water control, fish command, invisibility and electrical pulses through fluid. Only Urhmauuka can learn it. They also have healing tears, though most never notice, because tears vanish underwater. Urhmate: traits of their fish species, such as scales, fins, glow, chameleon colour or command of that species. They have no full Ruala, but their fish gifts make up for it. Lifespan and ageing The model is the Greenland shark: slow to grow, very late to mature, and centuries long. Ruua density matters. Urhmaiia in the undisturbed current of Maubuʁ live measurably longer than those in fringe cities. Heavily fish-featured Urhmate may begin to decline closer to 150. Weaknesses include fire and guns. Age Looks like Phase 0 to 2 Infant to young child of five or six Rapid growth: the nameless window 2 to 20 Child of eight to ten Slow juvenile 13 to 30 Changing The standard Haza window 30 to 60 Changing Late Haza, increasingly dangerous after 60 60 to 150 Young to mid adult, about 25 to 35 Prime 150 to 200 Mature adult, about 40 to 55 Gradual slowing 200 and up Visible ageing The body breaks down Sleep Urhmaiia sleep follows real fish breathing, not land-mammal unconsciousness. Buccal pumpers (Urhmauuka and most Urhmake) pump water over their gills with throat muscles and can lie truly still, anchored by an Amailini so they do not drift. Ram ventilators (most Urhmate, especially those melded with shark or tuna) must keep moving to breathe. They drift in slow circles while asleep, and the Amailini limits the radius. Anyone who knows the biology can tell the two apart at a glance by watching how someone sleeps. Unihemispheric sleep is the fallback in open water. One half of the brain rests at a time. It is the least restful. True unconscious sleep is possible only in a dry chamber, where the lungs take over. Access to a dry room is a genuine luxury. Open questions A few trait numbers in the physiology draft (gestation, for example) differ between the physiology section and the birth rites. Gestation is given as 6 to 9 months in one and tied to the season in the other. Open

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Gods and faith Gods and faith The Urhmaiia name the same divine balance as Nẹránamün in the Water-Echo tongue. This is the Urhmauuri pantheon, the origin myth and the words of belief. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. The divine layers Layer Urhmauuri Meaning Built from All-Creator Urhaha The Deep One, Source-of-Water urh- water, -aha origin Time (dual) Urhuloraia Flow-and-Ebb, Twin Tides urhu- deep flow, lor- cycle, -aia sacred pair Urhulagoi Waning Tide, Memory Current lag- fall, -oi honorific Urhulazoi Waxing Tide, Rising Current laz- rise, -oi honorific Order Zorunaia Harmonious Design, Patterned Path zor- order, -unaia sacred flow. It shares a name with the Storm Shepherd creature on purpose. Chaos Daraunaia Shattering Forge, Unmaking Flow dar- break, -aunaia active force Death River Urhkatenaia River-Gate, Passage Waters kate- cross Veil of Souls Urhzeloraia Flowing Veil, Watery Divide ze- veil or mist Serpent Guardian Silehaunaia Wound-Guardian, Tide Watcher si- serpent, leh- guard Wisdom Tokhaunaia Mind-Sea, Depth Thought tokh- thought Ancestors of mortals Garorhumaia Those-Who-Stayed, Echo Kin gar- rooted, rhu- echoed water, -maia people Other spirits and powers Role Urhmauuri Meaning Opener of Ways Zekataunaia Path-Opener, Crossing Guide Ocean Mother Urhaina Great Water, Ocean Source River Spirit Urhazina Small Flow, Wandering Song Sea Spirit Urhataunaia Living Sea, Breathing Depth Earth Mother Leranaia Land-Allmother Star Goddess Iziloaunaia Guiding Light, Star Flow Sun God Elunaia Radiant Circle Storm Flame Queen Sorazanaia Flame-Wind Queen Protector Lerunaia Shieldpaw, Home Guard Fertility Maeluaia Blooming One, Joygiver Civilizer Ulorunaia Builder of Homes Lera and zekha. Both mean earth. Lera is earth as land, nature, terrain and the planet as a force. Zekha is the ground underfoot: floor, soil, dirt. A temple built into the lera is built into the natural world. A temple with a zekha floor just has a dirt floor. Animal spirits These are land animals, kept on purpose. The first Urhmauuka came from Rejfe-descended humans who carried their land-dwelling symbols into the sea, much as real diaspora communities carry the symbols of one continent into another. Canon Animal Spirit Meaning Gorilla Rakhuma Stoneback Eagle Haoluma Skywatcher Lizard Keluma Flickerhide Chimpanzee Momuma Mirrorhand Dog or wolf Noluma Heartfang Leopard Dakhuma Shadowcoat Lion Soruma Sunclaw The common eel is sileuma , a lesser echo or child of the Serpent Guardian, and the source of eel leather and sinew in Urhmaiia craft. Urhaha and the Ruua Titles The Chooser of Tides, Sacred Voice of Water, Guide of the Deep Breath. Role Divine parent of the Urhmaiia. Gives resonance and form. Patron of change, cycles and memory. Shows itself as Tide-song, whirlpools and glowing resonance in Maubuʁ. Appears in dreams to Ezilii children. Epithets Aldarhuha, “Shifting Urhaha,” invoked for change. Amairhuha, “Calm Urhaha,” invoked for comfort or protection. Tone Willing and close. Invoked like an elder, remembered and spoken with, not an abstract force. Ruua is not a god. It is the breath or resonance that runs through everything Urhaha touches. “Ruua flows in you” is a blessing. “The Ruua has dimmed” means someone is dying or in spiritual crisis. “Ruua-sent” describes a person acting with divine purpose. When an Urhmaiia dies, their essence goes back into the Ruua and is remembered in Maubuʁ. Death and memory belong to the Ruua itself, not to Maubuʁ as a land of the dead, though the Ruua is thickest there and ancestral memory is strongest for those who live in it. Urhaha did not make the ocean. They gave it direction, form and invitation. “Urhaha was not the sea. They were its mind, its song, its choosing.” The origin myth “We came not from one sea, but from every flood the world tried to forget.” Before the world had names there was breath, and the breath was Ruua: not wind but resonance, a deep vibration from which all water draws memory. From it came Urhaha, the Chooser of Tides, recognised by the Ruua as its will. Urhaha was the first to listen. When the land cracked and the sky bled ice, the people scattered. Some stood still, sang to the soil and were buried. Others turned to the water and wept, not from weakness but as an invitation. Urhaha answered. From flooded canyon mouths and the bones of drowned forests, Urhaha shaped the first Urhmaiia, to keep a promise that no song sent to the sea would go unheard. Caste How the myth says they came to be Urhmauuka The firstborn: resonance given form, with eyes for light, lungs for breath and skin for tide. They were Ezilii at birth, whole and fluid, and carried the Ruua in their marrow. Urhmate Late prayers, exiled children and swallowed caravans. Some were reshaped through grief, others through blood rites whispered by those who had lost Urhaha’s voice. Water-made and shadowed by separation, but no less real. Urhmake The called back. They wake long after the old seas have drawn back, born human with the Ruua stirring in them like a second heart. They do not remember the sea, but the sea remembers them. “To be Urhmaiia is not to be born. It is to be answered.” The myth says the Urhmate came through blood rites by people who had lost Urhaha’s voice, while the caste page says Dagan transformed them. The two may be reconciled as one story told from two sides, or one may be revised Open Six names for the faith The faith has a different name for each register. This system is separate from the five verb-ending politeness levels. It is easy to confuse the two. Register Name Meaning Used for Formal, high canon Urhahaureiara Way of Urhaha’s Balance Temple inscriptions, ceremonies, elite teaching, historical scrolls Everyday, cultural Urhaiiza Tidepath Daily talk, prayer, communal chants, teaching the young Colloquial, intimate Naturhzaia The Breath We Swim Family, mourning songs, weddings, stories for children Philosophical, poetic Huziloauna Path of Remembering Light Dream theology, epics, prophetic chants, elders’ reflection Mythic, symbolic Ilorumaiua The Song Beneath the Sea Moral parables, seasonal rites, identity songs, transformations such as Haza Casual vernacular Urhzakoa Way of the Flow Common speech, young initiates, market slang, secular Urhmaiia Words for believers Term Meaning Urhmizaia Dreamer or intuitive believer: “tide-bound,” in tune with the currents of Urhaha and memory. Haiizaia True believer or initiate: “one who breathes the sacred tide.” Naharhmizaia A departed or lost dreamer: “one pulled from the tide.” Ulakaiia Awakened rebel or dissenter: “breaker of currents.” Used with respect and with criticism. [Deity]-zaiina A zealot of one deity. Urhaha-zaiina is “one devoted to Urhaha.” Garomaia Humans, in the formal and mythic register: “root-people, our echo-kin.” Everyday speech says gizo. The older human name “Zea” for Urhaha is retired entirely. It does not appear in any context, human or Urhmaiia. Decided

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Creatures and plants Creatures and plants Every creature is two or more real animals fused, with one trait pushed past what nature allows. They skew toward Pacific, Indian Ocean and Southern African coastal fauna. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. The source animals are real, so this page is a good place to see where each design started. Names are Urhmauuri. No. Name Gloss Source Notes 1 Naisiru The Sterling Sturgeon + oarfish Armoured, 5 to 11 m. Paralysing skin; screams through water. Hunts in pods with a herder. Seen as living ancestors; keeping one is either respect or arrogance. 2 Kauareia The Ancestor Glider Coelacanth + manta ray A manta-winged coelacanth up to 6 m across. Its wingbeats pulse through a fluid-filled spine, and water-Ruala users read them as the ocean’s mood. Killing one is the deepest taboo. 3 Zorunaia The Storm Shepherd Hammerhead + manta ray Senses electric fields from far off and cannot be ambushed. Groups gather before storms, so cities keep watchers who read them. The name also means “Harmonious Design.” 4 Dailore The Lantern Drifter Vampire squid + jellyfish A purple-black cloak topped with a glowing bell. Its glow changes with mood. Its fluid is a base for ceremonial light-food. 5 Borumaura The Ridge Grazer Dugong + whale shark 8 to 12 m, gentle and spotted. A gardener and grazer that has shaped coral geography. The dugong is the source of real mermaid legends. Protected by civic law. 6 Kirusoa The Spine Walker Stonefish + coconut crab Dog-sized, rock-camouflaged, walks on any surface including ceilings. Its venom can kill an adult in hours. Wealthy households keep them as guards. 7 Miruhau The Deep Lantern Anglerfish + barreleye About 1.5 m. A transparent dome gives 270 degrees of sight, and a mobile glowing lure covers the blind spot behind it. 8 Iziloa Cultivated hallucinogen A microalga Grown by Borutira specialists and chewed dried. Users describe being “shown light from inside.” 9 Vohuraki The Spined Puffer Pufferfish + lionfish A wild, reclusive reef hazard, especially to children reaching into crevices. Its venom is also used diluted. 10 Borulume Bioluminescent deep coral A cultivar Bred to live on glow rather than sunlight, with a symbiotic glowing bacteria. Cultivated for building and light. 11 Moruhoze The Forgetting Bloom A flower Common in gardens. A brush gives a few minutes of fog and every child is warned once. A concentrated dose causes real memory loss. 12 Kuvamuma The Grip-Weaver Octopus, amplified Strong, hard to catch, valued as a harvest. 13 Sileuma The eel Eel A lesser echo of the Serpent Guardian spirit. Eel leather and sinew appear throughout material culture. 14 Kohusoa The Iron Snail Scaly-foot gastropod Vent-only. Its shed scales stay magnetic. The main native iron source for smiths, and crushed shell paves roads. 15 Izilouma The Silver Herald Oarfish An omen creature. Harvested strips are reserved for priestly garments. 16 Tunyauma The Chimney Worm Giant tube worm Cultivated at vent cities. Its casings are harvested without killing the colony, for sheaths and small plumbing. 17 Kiruuma The Deep Beak Giant or colossal squid Rare, formidable and respected. Beak (Zakiru) is gathered from natural deaths for tool tips and harpoon points. 18 Zheuma The Slime Warden Hagfish Harmless harvest. Its slime becomes sealant and fine cordage. 19 Reiuma The Quickcurrent Mako shark A thrill-mount for young riders and fast messengers. Dangerous if poorly handled. 20 Tsurauma The Willing Partner Dolphin Never owned. A freely chosen and re-chosen working partner that herds fish, guides the lost and sometimes gives a ride. 21 Mauatsura The Elder Pod Orca or whale Rare and generational. Befriended, not acquired. Baleen is gifted or respectfully gathered, never hunted. 22 Amaiuma The Quiet Grazer Sea cucumber Domesticated livestock: meat, leather and waste management. 23 Kuvatsura The Chosen Guest Octopus A wild animal that chooses a person and stays a few months to a couple of years. 24 Soanaka The Deep Armor Giant isopod Shell becomes flexible segmented armour. Living ones dig as labour. 25 Rakinaka The Hard Shell Deep-sea crab or lobster Rigid single-plate armour that absorbs one heavy blow. 26 Miruveka’s source The Ghost Drifter Vampire squid Rare and gentle. Its glowing mucus is a luxury adhesive that marks genuine goods. 27 Kohuzauma The Glass Lattice Glass sponge Grown into building panels and light conduits. Structures grow around a living lattice. 28 Borukohu Mermaid’s Fan A reef growth Dried for rigid pieces such as armour panels and headdresses. 29 Soraboru Dragon’s Breath A red-orange alga Reserved for ceremonial and high-status colour. 30 Boruza Blue Hypnea A seaweed The closest thing to silk in everyday life. Used in skirts and trim, with finer grades for formal wear. 31 Pezauma The Silkweaver Noble pen shell Source of Pezalini thread and Pezaraga cloth. Harvested without harm. The real top-tier fabric. Danger and dependence Venomous animals such as the Spine Walker and the Spined Puffer can kill careless Urhmaiia, especially children. The exception is Urhmate melded with the same species, who carry resistance or immunity. They are central to antivenom work in every city, which gives them value and also treats their bodies as a medical resource. That tension is unresolved. Companions and mounts Dolphins are companions and never food. The Quickcurrent is a thrill-mount, the Willing Partner is a chosen collaborator, and the Elder Pod is a revered friend. The Sterling is kept by some as a companion, which is respectful to some and arrogant to others. Opinion splits by caste and generation. Materials Almost every creature above feeds a craft: sealant from hagfish slime, sinew and leather from eel, thread from the noble pen shell, armour from isopod and crab shell, magnetic scales for iron, grown glass for building and light. Open A full materials page is planned.

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Food and craft Food and craft The oldest rule in Urhmaiia food is to speak to what you eat. The newest is about who has to. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. Amairuua Amairuua is a brief ritual of acknowledgment before eating any living thing, spoken or telepathic. It recognises the creature’s life and returns its Ruua to the current. It is relational ethics, not prayer, and it is the oldest practice in the culture. What has split is who still does it, and why. Group Practice Upper-tier Urhmauuka Still observed, but calcified into display. They eat everything, and some deliberately eat the fish that Urhmate are melded with. Lower-tier Urhmauuka Mostly dropped for practical reasons. They eat what there is, and upper tiers look down on this. Traditional Urhmate Keep Amairuua and refuse their own melded species, since eating it collapses the boundary between self and food. Some refuse only the exact species, some related species, some all fish. Young Urhmate Two roads. One is full-practice revival: eat everything with real Amairuua, as a statement that fish heritage is not shameful. The other is invertebrates and plants only, as kinship with fish. Esu is the word for any non-Urhmaiia sea creature that anyone may eat. Garesu is the Urhmate-only word for their own species-line, who are kin and never food. Azoiesu is the Urhmauuka term for the status-coded act of eating a species an Urhmate is melded with. What they eat Food Notes Cultivated seaweed and kelp The most democratic food. A staple for every class. Coral-farm produce A mid-tier staple. Invertebrates Clams, cephalopods, crustaceans, urchins and sea cucumbers. Even “vegetarian” Urhmate eat them. Fish The common protein, with the debates above. Large marine mammals Occasional, and ceremonial among the traditional. More common in lean seasons. Vent organisms Tube worms, vent crabs and other extremophiles. A deep-water delicacy. Glowing organisms Some are edible, and their glow transfers briefly to the eater. Used at Haza and mating ceremonies. Dolphin Not food. Dolphins are companions, and eating one would be like eating family. Cooking without fire There is no fire underwater, so every method is either geothermal (real vent heat, up to about 700°F at black smoker outflows) or chemical (acid, enzyme or fermentation). Dish Method Tsoraifila Precision-sliced raw fish. The usual special-occasion home dish. Borufila Raw fish or invertebrate wrapped in cured kelp. Zorufila Cooked or dried at a vent. Food in vessels at the outflow bakes, and strips hung in the superheated mineral air dry to jerky. A deep-water delicacy with a mineral flavour. Zaifila Fish “cooked” by acid marination in mineral-pool brine, like ceviche. Amaifila Cold-fermented seafood sealed in shell or coral vessels. The everyday counterpart to Zoruamai. Izilofila Glowing organisms prepared so the glow transfers. Luxury and ceremonial. Food has to hold together in open water, so loose soups do not exist. Borubeka, an alginate paste, binds cooked fish, and Boruzhila, an edible kelp leaf, wraps it into something that can be bitten cleanly. Cooked food on land overwhelms first-timers, because the browning reaction makes flavours that have no underwater equivalent. Amaiurhzakha, September to November, is the lean season. Elites draw on stored reserves while lower-tier Urhmauuka and most Urhmate compete for common food, and traditional abstentions get harder to keep. Drinks and intoxicants Urhmaiia take in water through food, so there is no drinking culture in the land sense. Still, there is a social structure of three tiers: Tier Substance What it is Casual Borulora Kelp pods injected with Luaruua nutrient sap and crushed against the roof of the mouth. Intoxicant Zoruamai A glowing, warming gel brewed by a Zoruii (vent-brewer) from sulfur bacteria and sweet seagrass roots, fermented in sealed vessels at a vent. Psychedelic Kirutokha, Vohutokha, or Iziloa Diluted venom from the Spine Walker or the Spined Puffer, or Iziloa, a cultivated hallucinogenic microalga. The social centre is the Vent Lounge: a gathering place around a vent or gas seep where one substance is passed from hand to hand, or mouth to gill, through a group. A Zoruii’s whole living depends on secure access to a vent. The syringe they use is a cured swim bladder fitted with a sharpened bone nozzle.

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Language and time Language and time Urhmauuri is built for mouths that vary widely. Its rules are tendencies, not walls. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. Sounds Allowed syllables are CV, VCV, CVV and V. The only consonant allowed at the end of a syllable is rh, a sacred exception used in roots such as Urh, “water.” Consonant clusters survive only as an archaism in ancient sacred Haulorai. Vowel harmony is a tendency, and all diphthongs are legal. The rules exist to accommodate the wide range of Urhmaiia mouths. Group Letters Stops p b t d k g Uvulars rh (ʁ), kh (χ) Fricatives s z sh h Affricates ts tsh dz Nasals m n ng ny Other y, r (flap), rr (trill), l, lh (ł), the glottal stop Clicks ! ǁ ǀ Vowels i e ii (ɨ), u o uu (ʉ), a The letters w, v and q do not exist. Words borrowed with w, v or bh become sh (in front-vowel words) or ny (in back-vowel words), so tuva becomes tunya. The sound lh marks deep native vocabulary, and in loanwords it appears only beside a uvular or after a back vowel. Politeness Five grammatically marked levels, set by the main or final verb and kept through the sentence: Register Verb ending Used for Plain polite -o Most formal or polite situations. Informal none Friends and equals. Intimate -e A life partner only. Respectful -i Someone higher in status or age. Royal -u Those who hold royal titles only. This is separate from the register system for names of Urhaha: Urhahaureiara (formal), Urhaiiza (everyday), Naturhzaia (intimate), Urhzakoa (casual). Amaiurhzakha September to November Oceanic, the lean season. Festival: Amaiurhzele. The sacred root. Ruua The sacred resonance current in all water. Ruala The magical gift. Haulorai Uvular call speech. Gizo A human, in everyday speech. Garomaia “Root-people.” A formal or mythic word for humans, used when invoking shared ancestry. Maitauua A life partner or chosen mate. Rinahiru A destined mate or soulmate. Kide A close partner or friend. Ezilii, Izilii, Arhtsilii Neutral (the birth state), receptive, and insertive. Kautsorii The messengers and scribes of the Sofa current. Zoruii A vent-brewer. The cord family Urhmaiia have no pockets or shelves, so they use cords: Cord Use Naialini The identity cord. It starts as a carved name-piece and collects meaningful objects over a lifetime. Sacred, worn across the chest and never removed. Amailini The sleep anchor. Torilini The everyday carrying cord for tools, knives and coin strings. Small valuables may instead be braided into hair on long swims. Religion in brief Urhaha is the creator. The full pantheon, the origin myth and the words of belief are on Gods and faith . h: Birth The hatching, Jaiotsetsho The nameless window Haza, the change Bonding Urhmake and the ripening Death Eating an Urhmaiia
x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Birth, change and death Birth, change and death Urhmaiia are born into a song, change when they meet the right person, and are given back to the sea as a reef. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. Birth A parent expels the embryo through the throat. It grows in a community natal centre, a Raunutua, in a translucent sac hung from a central living anchor of coral or root. Gestation is six to nine human months, following the seasons more than the calendar. The season of release sets the season of hatching. The sac, Raunuvera, is tough and leathery like a shark egg case. A sinew line, Maualini, runs from its loop to the anchor, fixed with a barnacle-cement glue. A one-way feeding port lets a parent pass Lualini, a nutrient fluid, into the sac. Caretakers called Raunutii can feed on a family’s behalf. No navel forms. Only Urhmake and transformed Urhmate, who begin life in ordinary human birth, have one. All Urhmaiia are born Ezilii : intersex, with an insertive organ, a receptive vulva and an anus. Wealthier families may raise embryos in private. The ideology calls this superior, and the biology suggests otherwise. The hatching, Jaiotsetsho The embryo’s glow changes pattern in the days before it emerges. Neighbours gather at the Raunutua and sing Haulorai, which physically helps guide the hatchling out. A child born into a whole city’s song has an easier time than one hatched in near silence. A community hatching is open to all. A standard household invites family and allies. An elite private hatching has only retainers, and a quieter song. The nameless window No name is given for two years. The child doubles in size repeatedly, grows full gills and makes first Haulorai sounds. The first hatching day marks survival and the second marks identity. At the end of the second year, if the child is thriving, the family gathers in private. The child announces their own name in Haulorai, which is their first deliberate voiced communication. The name is then told to the community. Caste Naming convention Urhmauuka Prestigious and inherited. Titles, lineage markers, ordinal positions. Elite families add a lineage title for three elements: personal, family and lineage. Urhmate Describe the child. A trait such as scale colour, eye pattern or glow; temperament in the nameless years; or the season or trench of hatching. Urhmake Aspirational and forward-looking. Most translate or adapt their human name into Urhmauuri to honour both origins. Names are social signals. A name that describes a trait is Urhmate, a name that invokes lineage is Urhmauuka, and a name that reaches forward is Urhmake. Haza, the change Haza is a puberty triggered by meeting a possible life partner (Maitauua), not by age alone. The usual window is 13 to 30. Late Haza, 30 to 60, is rare. After 60 it is dangerous because the body is too set, and an unchanged Urhmaiia nearing 60 is a community worry. Symptoms are intense body heat, severe cramps, hormonal swings, and rapid growth in height and bulk. Scaled Urhmate molt faster, and some grow new fins. Uhinemi is the general change. Uhinaudia is the narrower shift in organ roles, and it can happen many times in life. An Urhmaiia may move from Arhtsilii (insertive) back to Ezilii (neutral) or on to Izilii (receptive) on meeting a new partner. Gender is biologically fluid across a lifetime. All three states are honoured, and Ezilii is sacred as the original birth state. Deliberately avoiding Haza by avoiding any possible partner is considered deeply strange. If the interest is not returned, the drive fades in about two months (ilesha). Cross-species attraction still triggers the change. Bonding Maitauzelai is the nose-press bond. Glands on each side of the nose release pheromones and dopamine. It is done only with a life partner (Maitauua) or a destined mate (Rinahiru) and is never casual. The death of a partner can kill an Urhmaiia or bring a long, deep depression. Banauketa is reproductive copulation. It can be with a partner or a close friend (Kide). The two acts are distinct: Maitauzelai is for love and Banauketa is mainly reproductive. A human female and an Arhtsilii can mate, as can a human male and an Izilii, but conception is rare with high fetal mortality. Surviving children are Urhmake, and the trait can skip generations. Urhmake and the ripening Tsitsia is the Urhmake’s version of Haza. It starts after human puberty, at about 17 to 20, and is triggered by the body’s own clock together with water exposure. Gills, water tolerance, telepathy and the magnetic sense develop. Haza does not occur, so the organ-prioritisation process never fires. Reproductive biology locks at the moment of Tsitsia. A trans Urhmake already on hormones before Tsitsia completes with a biology that matches their current hormones. Tsitsia honours the lived body, not the birth assignment. Goria is a siren-like Haulorai call that pulls Urhmake descendants to the water. It can speed Tsitsia, but done too early it risks incomplete gills and stunted Ruala. The ripening has real dangers: predation by sea animals, missing the window by being too far inland, or losing the watcher who is meant to guide the child. Death There is no universal good or bad death. The specific wrong is death by pollution or at human hands, because it blocks the Ruuanakha: a poisoned body grows no reef. The Ruua leaves the body at death and flows toward the deepest, cleanest current, building up near Maubuʁ. Ruuanakha , the ideal death: the body sinks into the deep, and over decades becomes a living reef of tube worms, vent crabs and other life. It feeds the sea for up to a century. Zorugoria is the death call. Family and local guards swim to the body. They witness it, take a small keepsake (Ruuanai) such as a scale or fin fragment, and leave the body to the deep. Leaving is trust. Zhaʉelekha is community mourning, sung in Haulorai for a month for a respected elder or a few days for a hatchling. The dead are remembered at seasonal gatherings. The Ruuatira is the memorial garden, usually beside the Raunutua so birth and death share a place. The keepsake is planted, and the dead feed living plants. It is the only permanent institution that is alive rather than built. The Naizhaʉe is an unofficial role in fringe cities: someone known for carrying bodies to deep water. Circumstance Body Rite Deep clean water Left where it lies Becomes a Ruuanakha. Visit, death call, keepsake, mourning. Shallow or fringe water Carried to deep clean water The carrying is itself the rite of care. Near human cities Carried urgently to deep water Urgency is the rite. On land Cremated; ashes scattered in the deepest water reachable A fragment is planted in the garden. Pollution Carried if possible, cremated if too contaminated Mourning carries the grief of a stolen legacy. Eaten by another Urhmaiia Consumed No keepsake and no planting. The specific horror. Eating an Urhmaiia Consuming another Urhmaiia is the deepest wrong. The mainstream belief is that the consumed Ruua is trapped inside the eater and cannot return to the current. A fringe counter-belief holds that eating an enemy takes their strength and gifts. Communities that follow Dagan, the god of crossing boundaries, find the second idea easier to imagine, which is part of why Dagan worship draws suspicion from Urhaha-orthodox circles.

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Appearance and dress Appearance and dress An Urhmaiia on land is read as a Black or brown person of Austronesian, Polynesian or Sub-Saharan African descent. The sea shows second. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. Faces Three inspiration groups appear singly and mixed throughout the species, which is ancient and widespread. Group Features Austronesian and Southeast Asian Almond eyes, broad nose, strong jaw, prominent cheekbones, straight to wavy hair, warm medium to deep brown skin. Polynesian Wide strong bone structure, prominent brow, full lips, broader build, wavy to coily hair, deep warm brown to near-black skin. Southern African, Bantu and Khoisan Full lips, wide nose, a very deep melanin range including blue-undertone black, coily hair, high cheekbones. Skin Lineage Urhmauuka skin tone Notes Surface and fringe Warm deep brown to rich dark brown More human contact; melanin most visible. Mid-water Cool dark brown to near-black Less surface exposure. Deep water Blue-black to indigo-black Rare, and a mark of high status in deep cities. Urhmauuka keep a full melanin baseline. The sea shows in a shimmer when wet, slightly wide pupils, a third eyelid, pointed or webbed ear edges, and neck gills that close flat on land. Urhmate share the same baseline, with a second layer from the fish species they are melded with: Scale density Effect Low Melanin fully visible. Scales read as jewellery. Medium Melanin still leads. Scale colour makes contrast patterns. High Greens, purples and blues begin to shift the overall look. Full Scale colour dominates, but the warmth of dark skin always shows at face, joints and palms. An Urhmate is never simply “green.” They are a dark-skinned person whose body has partly transformed. Deep-water lineages Urhmauuka: blue-black to indigo skin, very large pupils, faint natural glow along the jaw, collarbones and spine, and hair of deep black with a blue sheen. Urhmate: melded with anglerfish, viperfish, barreleye or lanternfish. Glow is stronger and pulses with emotion. Some have translucent patches, and some have longer, more numerous teeth. Eyes Group Range Universal baseline Deep brown. Urhmauuka Wide and layered: warm hazel to amber, grey-green, deep teal, slate blue, gold-flecked brown. Colour shifts with light. Urhmate Narrower: occasional warm amber, muted green or grey. Their sea heritage shows in the body, not the eyes. Deep water Large pupils. Urhmate may add a reflective layer or sideways pupils. Hair Every texture occurs. Underwater, hair fans and floats weightlessly. In deep lineages it can hold glowing particles. In Urhmate with strong fish melding it can take on scale colour, and unusual shades such as navy or green-tinted are typical of strong melding or deep-water lineage. Ceremonial tattoos Only Urhmauuka who have graduated from magic training or shown mastery of Ruala wear them. They glow, and three rules govern them: Colour complements skin: warm gold on blue-black, cool silver-white or deep copper on rich dark brown, jewel tones such as teal and cobalt on mid-brown. Intensity grows with power. New graduates have fine lines that barely glow. Masters have broad lines. The oldest glow in daylight. Pattern follows the Ruala: flowing waves for water, branching Lichtenberg figures for electricity, scale geometry for fish command, and the most elaborate patterns of all for invisibility, which vanish with the caster. Albinism and pale complexion True albinism is genetic and occurs in either caste. Albino Urhmauuka are exceptionally rare, and reactions range from reverence to suspicion. In deep cities, where glow is the main visual language, their lack of pigment makes their own markings unusually vivid. A pale Urhmaiia without albinism is almost always an Urhmate whose fish is a light species, or an Urhmake of mixed descent. The dark skin is still underneath. Inheritance among Urhmate Parents of the same type pass on their species’ traits predictably, with small differences. Parents of mixed types pass on the dominant parent’s traits most strongly, with blended or mosaic results. Some traits compete rather than blend. Asymmetry, such as one arm scaled like one parent and the other like the other, is not unusual or alarming. Garments Urhmaiia dress for adornment, not cover, because loose fabric is no use in the water. Wardrobe is androgynous. Gender among the Urhmaiia is fluid and exists for mating, not for presentation, so nothing about dress is gendered. Status shows in material, craft and body modification. A loincloth, Borumora, is universal and worn by everyone. Layers are added by means and occasion. Common materials are seagrass and kelp, then Boruza (woven Blue Hypnea), and at the top Pezaraga, woven sea silk. Gold, Azoilira, is reserved for the Ajoiru royal line and ceremonial stewards, and is never functional because gold is too soft. Garment Name Loincloth, the universal base Borumora Vest or chest piece Ilimora Hypnea skirt Zamora Flowing mantle or blouse Loremora Wrapped sash or belt Torimora Shell-fringe trim Pezamora Foot sleeves Nakamora Leg-binding speed piece Reiamora Ear-wrap for deep dives and storms Kiruvenaka Restricted royal gold ornament Azoilira Ears are cartilage and fold flat against the skull in fast swimming or deep pressure. Most everyday clothing is biodegradable and nothing piles up in a home. Treated leather, reforged metal and status materials are the deliberate exceptions, kept and passed down precisely because permanence is rare.

x: Home / Earth / Urhmaiia / Cities and the deep Cities and the deep Urhmaiia civilisation lives in Earth’s trenches. The oldest and holiest part lies in Maubuʁ, a sacred ocean no human has mapped. Lines without a tag are settled canon from the Urhmaiia Canon Reference. Tags mark anything less settled. Terms are given in the keyboard romanisation, with the uvular letter written rh. Maubuʁ Maubuʁ is a real, physical, sacred ocean, not an afterlife. It is the deep network of trenches in which most established Urhmaiia civilisation has always lived. Humanity has mapped only about a fifth of the ocean floor at useful resolution, and the great trenches (Challenger Deep, the Tonga Trench, the Philippine Trench) remain largely unmapped in fine detail. The Ruua current runs strongest and most undisturbed here because pollution and extraction have never touched it. That affects health, lifespan, Ruala strength and the quality of Haza. Fringe-city Urhmaiia who visit for the first time say the Ruua is overwhelming, like breathing fully after a lifetime of thin air. The edge of Maubuʁ is called the Urhkatea, felt as a pressure against the skin and gills, then a sudden release and a rush of current. Zones Zone Cities Character Maubuʁ interior Lejanizarua (royal capital), Inokohodua (religious capital), Zoritunua (judicial capital), Tsoritunua (the scribal archive), Zaruhotunua (ancient ruins) The oldest and holiest. Highest Ruua density. Maubuʁ threshold Adzuratunua, at Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench A city split by the Urhkatea. The political capital of the fringe confederation, whose name is still to be decided, and the nearest any unsanctioned city gets to Maubuʁ proper. Placeholder Deep fringe (about 7,400 to 10,500 m) Talarua (Tonga Trench), Zarehurua (South Shetland Trench), Nakatunua (Kermadec Trench), Naiatunua (Diamantina Trench) Mixed, Urhmauuka-led, with some Urhmate. Scholarship, medicine and naval garrisons. Mid fringe (about 4,000 to 7,800 m) Izoratunua (Molloy Deep), Luratunua (Java), Itsalidunua (South Sandwich), Reiatunua (Romanche Trench), Amaitunua (Fram Basin) More Urhmate. Industry, science and sport. A scholarly city and an industrial one, exporting Zoruamai, vent-crafted goods and blades. Inokohodua Mariana Trench The priestly city of the religious capital. Zoritunua Philippine Trench The seat of the courts, telepathic truth-hearings and the Honor Swim tribunals. Tsoritunua Japan Trench The great scribal archive and the training ground for Kautsorii. Six trenches remain unmapped and unnamed: Peru-Chile (Atacama), Laurentian Abyss, Sunda, Amundsen Abyssal Plain, Eurasian Basin and Nansen Basin. Open Adzuratunua and the Kitezori Adzuratunua is split by the Urhkatea. The Maubuʁ side holds the wealthiest old families and gate authorities. A checkpoint wall, the Kitezori, controls entry from the fringe, and its official purpose is sacred protection of Maubuʁ. The outer city is open, Urhmate-heavy and working class. Class Class Notes Elite Urhmauuka Maubuʁ households of old lineages and gate authorities. Professional Urhmauuka Scholars, warriors and local officials. Comfortable. Merchant Urhmauuka Wealth does not fully match status. Retainer and staff Urhmauuka They work in elite households. Quietly resented from above and below. Fringe-poor Urhmauuka Locked out of Maubuʁ by money, not law. Affluent Urhmate Merchant, civic, scholarly and warrior families who branched from Urhmauuka households. Politically conservative. Professional Urhmate Kautsorii, tube escorts, specialist crafts, antivenom. Working Urhmate Household staff, labourers, kelp and coral farmers. The backbone of fringe economies. Urhmate-watching families They live in the shallow fringe waiting for Urhmake descendants. Fringe-poor Urhmate The most exposed to pollution and humans. Urhmake They enter at their family’s class. Travel and messages Network What it is Toritunua, the current roads The ocean’s deep circulation, supercharged by Ruua. Basin crossings take days, not months. Knowledge is passed down in families and deliberately not taught. Finding one as a child is an Urhaha-given sign. Tunya, lava-tube transit Ancient tubes between basins. Fast and dangerous. Needs a guide who knows the route, or military-grade Ruala. Tube mouths carry standard markers, though some are outdated as tubes shift. Sofa, the message current The deep sound channel. Haulorai sent into it at the right depth crosses an entire basin as a slightly reverbed, flattened echo. Kautsorii descend to Sofa depth on rotation, listen, transcribe onto shell or basalt, and carry messages. They are almost always Urhmate. Historical markers Basalt, volcanic rock or carved coral signs at tube mouths, city edges and ancient Ruuanakha. The oldest are in Maubuʁ. Some are not yet translated. Government and vents Each city-state was governed by a steward of Ajoiru royal blood, tasked with balancing Urhmauuka and Urhmate in their trench. The whole realm under the royal crown is called Ejasantunua. Hydrothermal vents are among the most contested resources, a bit like dams: whoever holds a vent holds energy, forging and the intoxicant supply. Zarehurua’s vent was never fully brought under a single faction. Dry chambers Dry air pockets (anchialine chambers) are real geological features. Some are trapped air in sloped limestone caves flooded as seas rose. Others are volcanic gas pockets near vents, and some of those are toxic. Wealthy households build artificial ones by carving a reversed diving-bell dome and holding the waterline down. A private dry room is a major status symbol. Surfacing into one is a physical event: the neck gills collapse and flare, the third eyelid snaps back, skin sheds water in an instant, the muscles that push against ocean pressure suddenly relax, and the constant hum of the sea is replaced by sharp silence. Because telepathy is how Urhmaiia speak underwater, a dry room is where they speak aloud. Speaking with breath is intimate, private or formal, so the respectful and royal registers are most often spoken here. Architecture Urhmaiia cities are grown. Glyphs can be carved into young, soft coral, so they harden and rise as the coral matures. Older buildings have deeper, more weathered inscriptions and new wings have crisp ones. The Urhtsorna script groups letters by manner of articulation, and the idea is that building types might be marked by their dominant glyph family: stops for administration, r and rh for water-management structures, l and lh for temples and natal centres. Proposed Real-world sources to adapt: Bamum script from Cameroon, invented under King Njoya, and Adinkra symbols from the Akan of Ghana, which are carved into buildings as meaning-bearing decoration.
